_purpose: Words for the settings catalog, read by engine\pro-settings\Build-SISettingsCatalog.ps1. "groups": the areas settings are shown in, in this order, each with a one-line description -- grouped by what an admin wants to do, not by engine. "descriptions": a fallback description for settings whose configuration files carry no comment (a comment above the setting in the shipped files always wins). "help": per setting, what a person reads on the Settings page and in the Community reference -- label (plain display name), purpose, defaultText (what really applies when it is not set), effect (what changing it does), whenToChange, unit, advanced (true = tuning / diagnostic / older-name knob, folded away) and group (one of "groups"); for a setting with a fixed set of choices also type "enum", values (the allowed values) and valueLabels (value -> the plain words the Settings page shows in its dropdown). "retired": settings that no longer exist (name -> why); a value left for one in a configuration file or the Pro database is ignored without a message, and the tool never lists it as a setting. Written from the code that reads each setting (descriptions 2026-10-02, help 2026-10-04). Add an entry for every new setting, then re-run the tool. "categories" and "cards": how the Pro Settings page lays the settings out -- one category at a time (a category lists the groups whose settings it shows when they name no card), one card per topic with one Save, listing its settings in the order shown; per setting "hint" is the one short line under the field, and "needs" names the on/off setting it only works with ("!Name": only works while that setting is off).

descriptions.CustomYamlFile: File name of your own asset-tagging rules YAML, loaded from the settings folder on top of the shipped rules; defaults to AssetTagging.custom.yaml.
descriptions.DceResourceGroup: Resource group of the data collection endpoint used when risk-analysis results are sent to Log Analytics; the newer SI_DcrResourceGroup takes precedence when set.
descriptions.DebugQueryHash: When on, risk analysis logs each auto-bucketed report's query fingerprint and writes the hashed query to an OUTPUT\Debug folder for troubleshooting; off by default.
descriptions.Detailed: Runs risk analysis in Detailed mode (one row per affected asset finding) using the Detailed report template, table and recipients; cannot be combined with Summary.
descriptions.GraphQueryMaxRetries: How many times risk analysis retries a Defender advanced-hunting query after a transient error before giving up; defaults to 4 attempts.
descriptions.Mail_SecurityInsight_Detailed_SendMail: Older name for turning on e-mail of the Detailed risk-analysis report; used only when RiskAnalysis_Detailed_SendMail is not set.
descriptions.Mail_SecurityInsight_Detailed_To: Older name for the Detailed report recipient list; used only when RiskAnalysis_Detailed_To is empty.
descriptions.Mail_SecurityInsight_Summary_To: Older name for the Summary report recipient list; used only when RiskAnalysis_Summary_To is empty.
descriptions.MailTo: Fallback list of e-mail recipients for risk-analysis reports, used when no report-specific (Summary or Detailed) recipient list is set.
descriptions.OpenAI_deployment: Name of the Azure OpenAI model deployment used for AI classification and AI summaries; AI features stay off unless endpoint, key and deployment are all set.
descriptions.OpenAI_endpoint: URL of your Azure OpenAI resource used for AI classification and AI summaries; AI features stay off unless endpoint, key and deployment are all set.
descriptions.OpenAI_MaxTokensPerRequest: Maximum number of tokens the AI may return per request when building risk-analysis summaries; defaults to 16384.
descriptions.OverwriteXlsx: When on (default), risk analysis deletes the previous Excel workbook at the start of a run and writes a fresh one instead of adding to it.
descriptions.PowerBI_AuthClientId: App (client) id used to publish risk-analysis results to Power BI; defaults to the main SecurityInsight service principal when empty.
descriptions.PowerBI_AuthClientSecret: Client secret of the app used to publish to Power BI; defaults to the main service principal's secret when empty.
descriptions.PowerBI_AuthTenantId: Entra tenant id used when signing in to Power BI; defaults to the main service principal's tenant when empty.
descriptions.PowerBI_DatasetName: Name of the Power BI dataset risk-analysis results are pushed to; defaults to "SecurityInsight - Risk Analysis".
descriptions.PowerBI_WorkspaceName: Name of the Power BI workspace that holds the risk-analysis dataset; defaults to "SecurityInsight-Reports".
descriptions.RiskAnalysis_Detailed_Override: When on, risk analysis runs in Detailed mode by default unless Summary is explicitly requested on the command line; off by default.
descriptions.RiskAnalysis_Detailed_To: E-mail recipients for the Detailed risk-analysis report; falls back to MailTo when empty.
descriptions.RiskAnalysis_ReportTemplate_Default_Deta: Report template used when risk analysis runs in Detailed mode and no template is named explicitly; defaults to RiskAnalysis_Detailed.
descriptions.RiskAnalysis_Summary_To: E-mail recipients for the Summary risk-analysis report; falls back to MailTo when empty.
descriptions.ShowConfig: When on, risk analysis prints the fully resolved configuration at start-up so you can see which values are in effect; off by default.
descriptions.SI_AssetTagActivityTable: Log Analytics table that receives the asset-tagging activity log (which tags were applied or removed); defaults to SI_AssetTagActivity.
descriptions.SI_Azure_DcrName: Overrides the data collection rule name the Azure profiling engine ingests through; when empty, the standard naming pattern is used.
descriptions.SI_Azure_TableName: Overrides the Log Analytics table the Azure profiling engine writes to; when empty, the standard SI_Azure_Profile table is used.
descriptions.SI_AzureExposureGraph_AccessEdgeLabels: Exposure-graph relationship types (such as "has access to") treated as access paths from identities to Azure resources; the shipped list is used when empty.
descriptions.SI_AzureExposureGraph_IdentityLabels: Exposure-graph node types treated as identities (such as user and service principal) when mapping who can access Azure resources; the shipped list is used when empty.
descriptions.SI_AzureRecommendation_DcrName: Data collection rule name used to ingest Azure (Defender for Cloud) recommendations; defaults to dcr-si-azure-recommendation.
descriptions.SI_AzureRecommendation_TableName: Log Analytics table that receives Azure (Defender for Cloud) recommendations; defaults to SI_AzureRecommendation.
descriptions.SI_Bootstrap_AcrName: Name of the Azure Container Registry that holds the SecurityInsight container image; created by the container setup if it does not exist.
descriptions.SI_Bootstrap_EnvName: Name of the Azure Container Apps environment the SecurityInsight jobs run in; created by the container setup if it does not exist.
descriptions.SI_Bootstrap_ImageTag: Container image tag the container setup builds and the scheduled jobs run; defaults to latest.
descriptions.SI_Bootstrap_KedaMaxReplicas: Maximum number of worker containers that may run at the same time when queue-driven scaling (UseKEDA) is on; defaults to 30.
descriptions.SI_Bootstrap_ParallelismAzure: Number of containers the Azure profiling job runs in parallel per execution; defaults to 1.
descriptions.SI_Bootstrap_ParallelismIdentity: Number of containers the identity profiling job runs in parallel per execution; defaults to 1.
descriptions.SI_Bootstrap_ParallelismSchemaDiscovery: Number of containers the schema-discovery job runs in parallel per execution; defaults to 1.
descriptions.SI_Bootstrap_RaMaxWorkers: How many Risk Analysis queue workers may run Detailed reports at the same time; defaults to 4.
descriptions.SI_Bootstrap_RaScaleOut: Runs the Risk Analysis Detailed reports on queue workers, several reports at once; on by default wherever queue scaling and the managed identity let them run. Off: the reports run one after another in the Risk Analysis job.
descriptions.SI_Bootstrap_ScheduleAzure: Cron schedule (UTC) for the Azure profiling container job; defaults to daily at 05:00.
descriptions.SI_Bootstrap_ScheduleIdentity: Cron schedule (UTC) for the identity profiling container job; defaults to daily at 04:30.
descriptions.SI_Bootstrap_ScheduleRiskAnalysis: Cron schedule (UTC) for the Summary risk-analysis container job; defaults to daily at 06:00, after collection has finished.
descriptions.SI_Bootstrap_ScheduleSchemaDiscovery: Cron schedule (UTC) for the schema-discovery container job; defaults to Sundays at 03:00.
descriptions.SI_Bootstrap_SkipImageBuild: When on, container setup skips building the container image and reuses the image already in the registry; off by default.
descriptions.SI_Bootstrap_SqlServiceObjective: The Pro database's size (Azure SQL service objective, S1 to S12) that setup and every update keep, also when it is smaller than the product's; empty = the product's rule (Standard S3).
descriptions.SI_Bootstrap_WebAppCpu: The web app's CPU (0.5 to 4, in steps of 0.25) that every update keeps, also when it is smaller than the product's; empty = the product's size (2 CPU / 4 GiB).
descriptions.SI_Bootstrap_WebAppMemory: The web app's memory (for example 4Gi) that every update keeps; empty = twice the CPU.
descriptions.SI_Bootstrap_UseKEDA: When on, collection engines run as queue-driven workers that scale from zero with the amount of work instead of one scheduled job each; risk analysis is unaffected.
descriptions.SI_Bootstrap_UseManagedIdentity: Container setup signs the jobs in as one user-assigned managed identity (the default unless the configuration carries a client secret).
descriptions.SI_CmdbCsvPath: Full path to your CMDB export CSV when it is kept outside the SecurityInsight folder; when empty, the CSV is looked for in the CMDB provider folder.
descriptions.SI_CmdbRefreshIntervalHours: How many hours the cached CMDB data is reused before it is refreshed from the CSV; defaults to 24.
descriptions.SI_DcrResourceGroup: Resource group holding the data collection rules (and, by default, the data collection endpoint) used to ingest SecurityInsight data into Log Analytics.
descriptions.SI_DisableAI_endpoint: When on, switches off AI classification for the endpoint engine only, even if Azure OpenAI is configured; AI stays on for the other engines.
descriptions.SI_Endpoint_DcrName: Overrides the data collection rule name the endpoint profiling engine ingests through; when empty, the standard naming pattern is used.
descriptions.SI_Graph_Secret: Older name for the service principal's client secret; used only when SI_SPN_Secret is not set.
descriptions.SI_Graph_TenantId: Older name for the Entra tenant id the service principal signs in to; used only when SI_SPN_TenantId is not set.
descriptions.SI_Identity_DcrName: Overrides the data collection rule name the identity profiling engine ingests through; when empty, the standard naming pattern is used.
descriptions.SI_Identity_TableName: Overrides the Log Analytics table the identity profiling engine writes to; when empty, the standard SI_Identity_Profile table is used.
descriptions.SI_LogIngest_AppId: Older name for the app id used to ingest data into Log Analytics; used only when SI_SPN_AppId is not set.
descriptions.SI_LogIngest_ObjectId: Older name for the object id of the ingesting service principal, used to grant it rights on data collection rules; used only when SI_SPN_ObjectId is not set.
descriptions.SI_LogIngest_Secret: Older name for the client secret used to ingest data into Log Analytics; used only when SI_SPN_Secret is not set.
descriptions.SI_LogIngest_TenantId: Older name for the Entra tenant id used to ingest data into Log Analytics; used only when SI_SPN_TenantId is not set.
descriptions.SI_PublicIp_DcrName: Data collection rule name the public-IP engine ingests its results through; defaults to dcr-si-publicip-profile.
descriptions.SI_RATop50_BlobName: Blob path of the shared top-50 risk cache, so several hosts or containers reuse one AI summary instead of each building it; defaults to risk-analysis/RiskAnalysis_Top50_Shared.json.
descriptions.SI_RiskAnalysis_BuildSummaryByAI: When on, the risk-analysis container job asks Azure OpenAI to write an AI summary of the findings; off by default.
descriptions.SI_RiskAnalysis_DcrName_Detailed: Data collection rule name used to send Detailed risk-analysis rows to Log Analytics; defaults to dcr-si-risk-analysis-detailed.
descriptions.SI_RiskAnalysis_DcrName_Summary: Data collection rule name used to send Summary risk-analysis rows to Log Analytics; defaults to dcr-si-risk-analysis-summary.
descriptions.SI_RiskAnalysis_ExportContainer: Storage container the risk-analysis container job saves its Excel and JSON reports to; defaults to sistaging.
descriptions.SI_RiskAnalysis_ExportDestination: Full storage URL the risk-analysis container job saves its reports to; when empty it is built from the storage account, export container and export prefix.
descriptions.SI_RiskAnalysis_ExportPrefix: Folder inside the export container where the risk-analysis container job saves its reports; defaults to risk-analysis.
descriptions.SI_RiskAnalysis_Mode: Whether the scheduled risk-analysis container job produces the Summary or the Detailed report; must be Summary or Detailed and defaults to Summary.
descriptions.SI_RiskAnalysis_SendToLogAnalytics: When on, the risk-analysis container jobs are made with the copy of their report rows to Log Analytics switched on; not set = they follow Copy Risk Analysis report rows to Log Analytics, off by default.
descriptions.SI_RiskAnalysis_TableName_Detailed: Log Analytics table that receives Detailed risk-analysis rows; defaults to SI_RiskAnalysis_Detailed.
descriptions.SI_RiskReport_GlobalWeight_Azure: Share of the overall risk score contributed by Azure findings, as a fraction; defaults to 0.20.
descriptions.SI_RiskReport_GlobalWeight_Identity: Share of the overall risk score contributed by identity findings, as a fraction; defaults to 0.30.
descriptions.SI_RiskReport_GlobalWeight_PublicIP: Share of the overall risk score contributed by public-IP findings, as a fraction; defaults to 0.20.
descriptions.SI_RiskReport_SeverityWeight_High: Score weight given to a High (or Medium-High) severity finding in the risk report; defaults to 5.0.
descriptions.SI_RiskReport_SeverityWeight_Low: Score weight given to a Low severity finding in the risk report; defaults to 1.0.
descriptions.SI_RiskReport_SeverityWeight_Medium: Score weight given to a Medium severity finding in the risk report; defaults to 2.0.
descriptions.SI_RiskReport_TierMultiplier_T1: Multiplier applied to the risk score of findings on Tier 1 assets; defaults to 2.0.
descriptions.SI_RiskReport_TierMultiplier_T2: Multiplier applied to the risk score of findings on Tier 2 assets; defaults to 1.0.
descriptions.SI_RiskReport_TierMultiplier_T3: Multiplier applied to the risk score of findings on Tier 3 assets; defaults to 0.5.
descriptions.SI_SchemaCatalogTable: Log Analytics table that receives the schema-discovery catalog of proposed asset properties and rule drafts; defaults to SI_SchemaCatalog.
descriptions.SI_Shodan_AssetLimit: Maximum number of public IP addresses sent to Shodan per run; 0 (default) means no limit.
descriptions.SI_Shodan_LastFreshScanPath: File path where the time of the last fresh Shodan scan is remembered between runs; defaults to a file in the solution's data folder.
descriptions.SI_Shodan_PendingScansPath: File path where a submitted but unfinished Shodan scan is remembered so a later run can collect it without paying for a new scan; defaults to the data folder.
descriptions.SI_Shodan_ScanPollIntervalSec: Seconds to wait between checks on whether a submitted Shodan scan has finished; defaults to 30.
descriptions.SI_SignInBatchSize: Number of users looked up per sign-in log query during identity sign-in enrichment; defaults to 200.
descriptions.SI_SignInLookbackDays: How many days of sign-in history identity enrichment looks back over; defaults to 7.
descriptions.SI_SPN_AppId: Application (client) id of the SecurityInsight service principal used to sign in to Microsoft Graph, Azure and Log Analytics.
descriptions.SI_SPN_CertThumbprint: Thumbprint of the service principal's certificate (with its private key in the machine or user certificate store); used when SI_AuthMethod is Certificate.
descriptions.SI_StorageResourceGroup: Resource group of the SecurityInsight storage account, used when setup checks or creates the storage account and its permissions; defaults to the workspace's resource group.
descriptions.SI_UAMI_ClientId: Client id of a user-assigned managed identity that container jobs use to sign in instead of the service principal, when managed-identity sign-in is enabled.
descriptions.SI_WorkspaceName: Name of the Log Analytics workspace SecurityInsight writes its data to and reads from.
descriptions.SMTP_UseSSL: Whether e-mails of risk-analysis reports are sent to the SMTP server over an encrypted (SSL/TLS) connection.
descriptions.SMTPPassword: Password (or app password) for the SMTP account used to send risk-analysis report e-mails; required when sending with authentication.
descriptions.SpnCertificateThumbprint: Thumbprint of the certificate (in the local certificate store) the service principal signs in with; the recommended alternative to a client secret.
descriptions.SpnClientId: Application (client) id of the service principal the engines sign in as; older name kept in step with SI_SPN_AppId.
descriptions.SpnClientSecret: Client secret of the service principal the engines sign in as, used when no certificate thumbprint is set; prefer a certificate or Key Vault.
descriptions.SpnKeyVaultName: Name of the Azure Key Vault SecurityInsight reads its service principal secret and other credentials from; older name accepted alongside SI_KeyVaultName.
descriptions.SpnSecretName: Name of the Key Vault secret that holds the service principal's client secret, used when no certificate thumbprint or direct secret is set.
descriptions.WorkspaceResourceGroup: Resource group of the Log Analytics workspace used when risk-analysis results are sent to Log Analytics; a risk-analysis-specific override takes precedence when set.

SI_Pro_Responsibility_Sources.label: Department sources, in order
SI_Pro_Responsibility_Sources.purpose: Where SecurityInsight looks to decide which department is responsible for an asset: the platform tags (tags) and the department rules defined on the web app (rules), in the order listed.
SI_Pro_Responsibility_Sources.effect: Changes which department owns which assets and findings. Every retained collection is re-resolved on the next data sync, so the department pages, trends and monthly reports follow the new order. Overrides set on the web app always win; an asset nothing places goes to the default department, else Unassigned. Leave a source out to switch it off.
SI_Pro_Responsibility_Sources.whenToChange: When your rules are more reliable than your tags (put rules first), or when one of the two is not used at all.

SI_Pro_Responsibility_TagNames.label: Tag names that name a department
SI_Pro_Responsibility_TagNames.purpose: The tag names whose value names the responsible department: Azure resource tags (and the subscription's), Defender device tags written as Name:Value, and the Entra Department attribute.
SI_Pro_Responsibility_TagNames.effect: An asset whose tag value equals a department's name, or one of its 'also matches' values, is placed in that department; an earlier name wins over a later one. Every retained collection is re-resolved on the next data sync.
SI_Pro_Responsibility_TagNames.whenToChange: When your organisation tags ownership under another name (for example BusinessUnit or cost-center).

SI_Pro_Responsibility_DefaultDepartment.label: Default department
SI_Pro_Responsibility_DefaultDepartment.purpose: The department that receives every asset no override, tag or rule places.
SI_Pro_Responsibility_DefaultDepartment.defaultText: none -- such assets go to the Unassigned queue
SI_Pro_Responsibility_DefaultDepartment.effect: With a default set, nothing is Unassigned: the default department sees and is reported on every unplaced asset. Without one, unplaced assets wait in the Unassigned triage view. A name that is not an active department counts as none.
SI_Pro_Responsibility_DefaultDepartment.whenToChange: When one team (for example central IT) should own everything nobody else does.

SI_Pro_Responsibility_OverdueDays.label: Overdue after (days, per severity)
SI_Pro_Responsibility_OverdueDays.purpose: When an open vulnerability counts as overdue in the business owners' monthly report, counted from when it was first seen.
SI_Pro_Responsibility_OverdueDays.effect: Only the Overdue section of the monthly report changes; nothing is closed or escalated.
SI_Pro_Responsibility_OverdueDays.whenToChange: To match the remediation targets your organisation has agreed.

SI_Exempted_CountInManagement.label: Count exempted findings in the management numbers
SI_Exempted_CountInManagement.purpose: Whether findings covered by an approved exemption are counted in the management numbers: Risk Analysis's workbook, JSON, summary and mail, and the web app's dashboards, KPIs, trends, closure and Services view and the wall board.
SI_Exempted_CountInManagement.effect: An exemption never removes a finding: it is kept, marked, in Log Analytics and the Pro database either way. Off: every management number leaves exempted findings out and says how many it left out; each dashboard has an 'Include exempted' tick that recomputes its figures with them (shown as simulated, never saved). On: they are counted everywhere by default.
SI_Exempted_CountInManagement.whenToChange: Turn on if management should see the risk including accepted exemptions.

SI_Exempted_InDepartmentReports.label: Count exempted findings for departments
SI_Exempted_InDepartmentReports.purpose: Whether findings with an approved exemption count on the department pages and in the department mails.
SI_Exempted_InDepartmentReports.effect: Off: department pages and mails leave exempted findings out and say how many they left out; a department page's 'Include exempted' tick shows them for that view only. On: they are counted by default. The data keeps them either way.
SI_Exempted_InDepartmentReports.whenToChange: Turn on if departments should keep seeing the findings they have an exemption for.

SI_Pro_DepartmentReport_SendMail.label: Monthly report to business owners
SI_Pro_DepartmentReport_SendMail.purpose: Sends each department's business owners a monthly mail with the status of their assets and services.
SI_Pro_DepartmentReport_SendMail.effect: When on, the daily close-loop mail job sends each department its report for the previous month from the chosen day on, once per month, through the same mail relay as the Risk Analysis mail. Departments without a business owner with a mail address get none.
SI_Pro_DepartmentReport_SendMail.whenToChange: Once departments and their business owners are set up.

SI_Pro_DepartmentReport_DayOfMonth.label: Monthly report day
SI_Pro_DepartmentReport_DayOfMonth.purpose: The day of the month from which the report for the previous month is sent.
SI_Pro_DepartmentReport_DayOfMonth.effect: The report goes out on the first daily run on or after this day; a day the mail relay fails is retried the next day.
SI_Pro_DepartmentReport_DayOfMonth.whenToChange: When the previous month's data settles later (for example after a monthly patch window).

SI_Pro_GovernanceNotify_SendMail.label: New-findings digest to technical owners
SI_Pro_GovernanceNotify_SendMail.purpose: After each data sync, sends each department's technical owners one mail with their new findings.
SI_Pro_GovernanceNotify_SendMail.effect: When on, the daily close-loop mail job compares the newest collection with the last one each department was told about and sends one digest per department (nothing new means no mail), through the same mail relay as the Risk Analysis mail. Each collection is announced once per department; the very first collection is only recorded as the starting point. Departments without a technical owner with a mail address get none.
SI_Pro_GovernanceNotify_SendMail.whenToChange: Once departments and their technical owners are set up and they want to hear about new findings without opening the web app.

SI_Pro_GovernanceNotify_Mode.label: New-findings digest: one row per
SI_Pro_GovernanceNotify_Mode.purpose: How the technical owners' digest lists what is new: one row per vulnerability, or one row per asset with how many new findings it has and the highest severity.
SI_Pro_GovernanceNotify_Mode.effect: Only the layout of the digest changes; it is still one mail per department per collection, listing the 50 most severe rows with the rest counted.
SI_Pro_GovernanceNotify_Mode.whenToChange: Choose asset when the team works machine by machine (for example a server team patching hosts), vulnerability when it works issue by issue.

SI_Pro_GovernanceNotify_MinSeverity.label: New-findings digest: lowest severity
SI_Pro_GovernanceNotify_MinSeverity.purpose: The lowest severity the technical owners' digest announces (Critical, High, Medium or Low).
SI_Pro_GovernanceNotify_MinSeverity.effect: Findings below this severity are not announced (they are still on the department page and in the monthly review).
SI_Pro_GovernanceNotify_MinSeverity.whenToChange: Lower it for a team that wants to hear about every new finding; raise it to Critical when the digest is too long.

SI_Pro_TechnicalReview_SendMail.label: Monthly review to technical owners
SI_Pro_TechnicalReview_SendMail.purpose: Sends each department's technical owners a monthly mail to review their findings.
SI_Pro_TechnicalReview_SendMail.effect: When on, the daily close-loop mail job sends each department its review of the previous month from the chosen day on, once per month, through the same mail relay as the Risk Analysis mail. Nothing is closed or changed by it.
SI_Pro_TechnicalReview_SendMail.whenToChange: Once departments and their technical owners are set up and the governance log is in use.

SI_Pro_TechnicalReview_DayOfMonth.label: Monthly review day (technical owners)
SI_Pro_TechnicalReview_DayOfMonth.purpose: The day of the month from which the technical owners' review of the previous month is sent.
SI_Pro_TechnicalReview_DayOfMonth.effect: The review goes out on the first daily run on or after this day; a day the mail relay fails is retried the next day.
SI_Pro_TechnicalReview_DayOfMonth.whenToChange: To send it after your monthly patch window, so the review shows what the window fixed.

SI_Pro_TaskDigest_SendMail.label: Daily task reminder to assignees
SI_Pro_TaskDigest_SendMail.purpose: Once a day, mails each person whose follow-up tasks are overdue, due soon or have a reminder today.
SI_Pro_TaskDigest_SendMail.effect: When on, the daily close-loop mail job sends one digest per assignee per day (overdue first), through the same mail relay as the Risk Analysis mail, and records it so nobody gets two the same day; a day the relay fails is tried again on the next run. A task's mail address is the department person's or advisor's, or the one given when the task was created; a task without one gets no mail. Nobody with nothing due gets a mail.
SI_Pro_TaskDigest_SendMail.whenToChange: Once follow-up tasks are in use and people want a reminder without opening the web app.

SI_Pro_TaskDigest_DueSoonDays.label: Task reminder: due soon means within
SI_Pro_TaskDigest_DueSoonDays.purpose: How many days ahead the daily task digest counts an open task as due soon.
SI_Pro_TaskDigest_DueSoonDays.effect: An open task due within this many days (or already overdue, or whose reminder day has come) is in the assignee's digest. 0 lists only overdue tasks, tasks due today and reminders.
SI_Pro_TaskDigest_DueSoonDays.whenToChange: Shorten it when people find the digest too long; lengthen it for teams that plan further ahead.

SI_Pro_Remediation_AutoSchedule.label: Plan findings automatically (Auto in the maintenance window)
SI_Pro_Remediation_AutoSchedule.purpose: Lets the daily mail job plan every finding that has no governance status yet and whose department's remediation flow is 'Auto in the maintenance window' for that department's next maintenance window.
SI_Pro_Remediation_AutoSchedule.defaultText: off -- findings are planned only when a person applies the flow on the finding's page
SI_Pro_Remediation_AutoSchedule.effect: When on, such findings get a 'planned' entry in their governance log (by SecurityInsight, with the window) and show as planned on the department page and in the technical owners' mails. SecurityInsight never pushes a change to Defender, Intune, Entra or Azure: the fix itself is made by the platform's own tooling, and the next collections show whether it worked. A department without a maintenance window gets nothing planned.
SI_Pro_Remediation_AutoSchedule.whenToChange: Once the remediation flows and the departments' maintenance windows are set up and agreed.

AI_MaxAttempts.label: AI call attempts
AI_MaxAttempts.purpose: How many times Risk Analysis tries an AI request when the AI service times out, throttles or has a temporary failure.
AI_MaxAttempts.effect: More attempts make the AI summary more likely to succeed under load, but a failing service makes the run take longer. Other errors fail at once regardless.
AI_MaxAttempts.whenToChange: Raise if AI summaries often fail on throttling or timeouts.

SI_PatchCycle_MsrcDates.label: Patch cycle: read Microsoft update release dates
SI_PatchCycle_MsrcDates.purpose: Reads the release date of each Microsoft update (by its KB number) from Microsoft's public Security Update Guide (api.msrc.microsoft.com, no sign-in), once a day, and keeps it in the install. Defender names the update and its KB but not when it was released.
SI_PatchCycle_MsrcDates.effect: On: a Microsoft fix's own release date decides In monthly cycle / Catch-up (an out-of-band update by its own date). Off: no call to api.msrc.microsoft.com; the month the update's name says (its Patch Tuesday) is used. A third-party fix uses the first detection either way.
SI_PatchCycle_MsrcDates.whenToChange: Turn off when the install must not call out to api.msrc.microsoft.com (a private network that does not allow it). A failed call is said once per run and the name rule is used.

SI_PatchCycle_CatchUpDays.label: Patch cycle: catch-up after
SI_PatchCycle_CatchUpDays.purpose: When a finding counts as catch-up instead of being fixed in the monthly patch cycle: its fix was released (the month a "October 2026 Security Updates" text names -> that month's Patch Tuesday), or -- without one dated update -- the finding was first detected, more than this many days before the collection.
SI_PatchCycle_CatchUpDays.effect: The Patch cycle column of every finding (In monthly cycle / Catch-up / No fix available / Unknown) and its filter use this number from the next Risk Analysis run; findings already stored keep the value they were given.
SI_PatchCycle_CatchUpDays.whenToChange: Match your patch policy: e.g. 45 when monthly patches are allowed six weeks.

AutoBucketCache.label: Remember query split counts
AutoBucketCache.purpose: Saves how many parts each large risk analysis query had to be split into, so later runs start at the right number.
AutoBucketCache.defaultText: On: split counts are saved and reused.
AutoBucketCache.effect: Off, every run probes again from one part upward, which makes large estates noticeably slower. On, a changed query is detected and re-probed automatically.
AutoBucketCache.whenToChange: Rarely; turn off only while troubleshooting query splitting.

AutoBucketCount.label: Automatic query splitting
AutoBucketCount.purpose: Splits large risk analysis queries into smaller parts automatically so results stay under Defender's row limit.
AutoBucketCount.effect: Off, large queries run at a fixed split and can exceed Defender's limit, giving incomplete or failed reports on big estates.
AutoBucketCount.whenToChange: Leave on; turn off only for troubleshooting.

AutoBucketChallenger_ConfirmDays.label: Split count re-test pause
AutoBucketChallenger_ConfirmDays.purpose: After a run decided a report's split count, how many days pass before a suspiciously high count is tested again.
AutoBucketChallenger_ConfirmDays.effect: Shorter re-tests a count that looks too high sooner, at the cost of extra queries; longer keeps a wrong count longer.
AutoBucketChallenger_ConfirmDays.whenToChange: Rarely; only with support while tuning query splitting.

AutoBucketChallenger_MedianMultiplier.label: Split count re-test threshold
AutoBucketChallenger_MedianMultiplier.purpose: A report's split count this many times the median of the other reports' counts is treated as suspicious and tested again.
AutoBucketChallenger_MedianMultiplier.effect: Lower re-tests more reports (more queries); higher re-tests only extreme counts.
AutoBucketChallenger_MedianMultiplier.whenToChange: Rarely; only with support while tuning query splitting.

AutoBucketChallenger_MinEntries.label: Split count re-test sample size
AutoBucketChallenger_MinEntries.purpose: How many reports must have a split count before one count is compared with the others at all.
AutoBucketChallenger_MinEntries.effect: Lower compares sooner on small installs; higher waits for more reports before re-testing anything.
AutoBucketChallenger_MinEntries.whenToChange: Rarely; only with support while tuning query splitting.

AutoBucketMax.label: Query split upper limit
AutoBucketMax.purpose: The most parts automatic query splitting may divide a risk analysis query into.
AutoBucketMax.effect: A lower limit stops probing sooner, so a query too large for that many parts can still fail or return incomplete rows; a higher limit is accepted but rarely needed.

AutomationFramework.label: Internal platform sign-in mode
AutomationFramework.purpose: Marks a run as hosted on the vendor's internal automation platform, which provides the sign-in identity instead of SecurityInsight's own settings.
AutomationFramework.defaultText: Off: SecurityInsight's own sign-in settings are used.
AutomationFramework.effect: When on, engines take their identity and connections from the internal platform and skip their own sign-in. On a normal install this breaks sign-in.
AutomationFramework.whenToChange: Never on a customer install; it is set automatically by the internal platform.

BuildSummaryByAI.label: AI summary in the report mail
BuildSummaryByAI.purpose: Adds an AI-written executive summary of the Risk Analysis findings to the report email.
BuildSummaryByAI.effect: When on, each Risk Analysis run calls your Azure OpenAI deployment, adding run time and AI cost. If the AI settings are missing, a VM run stops with an error; a container run skips the summary.
BuildSummaryByAI.whenToChange: Turn on when you have Azure OpenAI set up and want a narrative summary in the mail.
BuildSummaryByAI.hint: When the reports run on a server.

CsaAttributeSet.label: Custom security attribute set
CsaAttributeSet.purpose: The Entra custom security attribute set that identity tagging rules write their tags into.
CsaAttributeSet.effect: Identity tags are written into the named attribute set instead. The set must exist in Entra; a rule that names its own set still wins over this value.
CsaAttributeSet.whenToChange: Only if your Entra tenant uses a different attribute set name for these tags.

CustomYamlFile.label: Your asset tagging rules file
CustomYamlFile.purpose: File name of your own asset tagging rules, loaded from the rules folder on top of the shipped rules.
CustomYamlFile.effect: Rules in this file are added to the shipped rules. If the file does not exist, only the shipped rules run. Ignored when rules come from the Pro settings database.
CustomYamlFile.whenToChange: Only if you keep your tagging rules under another file name.

DceIngestionUri.label: Ingestion endpoint address (older name)
DceIngestionUri.purpose: Older name for the data collection endpoint's ingestion address, used by Risk Analysis when sending results to Log Analytics.
DceIngestionUri.defaultText: Not set: looked up from the endpoint name
DceIngestionUri.effect: Used only when SI_RiskAnalysis_DceIngestionUri and SI_DceIngestionUri are not set. A wrong address makes Risk Analysis ingestion fail.
DceIngestionUri.whenToChange: Never on new installs; use SI_DceIngestionUri or leave it to automatic lookup.

DceName.label: Data collection endpoint name (older name)
DceName.purpose: Older name for the data collection endpoint that Risk Analysis sends its results through.
DceName.effect: Used by Risk Analysis only when SI_RiskAnalysis_DceName and SI_DceName are not set; in a container it also fills SI_DceName. A wrong name stops Risk Analysis ingestion or creates a new endpoint.
DceName.whenToChange: Never on new installs; set SI_DceName instead.

DceResourceGroup.label: Endpoint resource group (older name)
DceResourceGroup.purpose: Older name for the resource group of the data collection endpoint used by Risk Analysis and setup checks.
DceResourceGroup.effect: Used only when SI_DceResourceGroup (and, for other engines, SI_DcrResourceGroup) is not set. A wrong group makes the engine look in, or create resources in, the wrong place.
DceResourceGroup.whenToChange: Never on new installs; set SI_DceResourceGroup only if you split resource groups.

DcrResourceGroup.label: Rules resource group (older name)
DcrResourceGroup.purpose: Older name for the resource group holding the data collection rules that Risk Analysis uses.
DcrResourceGroup.effect: Used by Risk Analysis only when SI_RiskAnalysis_DcrResourceGroup and SI_DcrResourceGroup are not set; in a container it also fills SI_DcrResourceGroup. A wrong group puts rules in the wrong place.
DcrResourceGroup.whenToChange: Never on new installs; set SI_DcrResourceGroup instead.

DebugQueryHash.label: Query fingerprint debug output
DebugQueryHash.purpose: Logs each split query's fingerprint and saves the query to a debug folder for troubleshooting.
DebugQueryHash.effect: On writes one query file per report to the output Debug folder and adds log lines; no effect on report content.
DebugQueryHash.whenToChange: Only when asked to diagnose query splitting.

Detailed.label: Detailed run mode
Detailed.purpose: Runs risk analysis in Detailed mode: one row per affected asset, with the Detailed template, table and mail recipients.
Detailed.effect: Honoured when the engine is run directly. The launchers and containers decide the mode themselves (command-line switch, RiskAnalysis_Detailed_Override, or the template name) and replace this value.
Detailed.whenToChange: Use the -Detailed switch or RiskAnalysis_Detailed_Override instead.

ExportDestination.label: Report upload destination
ExportDestination.purpose: Where Risk Analysis copies its Excel (and JSON) report after a run: an Azure Blob container URL or a Windows file share path.
ExportDestination.defaultText: On a server: no upload. In a container: the staging storage account's report folder
ExportDestination.effect: Reports are also uploaded there; an existing file with the same name is first kept as a timestamped backup. The run's identity needs write access to that location.
ExportDestination.whenToChange: Set it when reports should land on a share or storage container people or tools read from.

GraphQueryMaxRetries.label: Defender query retries
GraphQueryMaxRetries.purpose: How many attempts risk analysis makes for a Defender advanced hunting query before giving up.
GraphQueryMaxRetries.effect: More attempts ride out longer outages but can make a failing run take much longer; fewer attempts fail sooner and risk missing report sections after a brief error.
GraphQueryMaxRetries.whenToChange: Raise it if transient Defender errors often break runs.

GraphReconnectMaxAgeMinutes.label: Graph reconnect interval
GraphReconnectMaxAgeMinutes.purpose: How old the Microsoft Graph sign-in may get before risk analysis signs in again before a query.
GraphReconnectMaxAgeMinutes.effect: Shorter reconnects more often (small overhead); longer risks a sign-in expiring during long runs and queries failing.
GraphReconnectMaxAgeMinutes.whenToChange: Only if long runs fail with expired sign-ins.

Location.label: Azure region (older name)
Location.purpose: Older name for the Azure region Risk Analysis uses when it has to create a missing workspace or ingestion resources.
Location.defaultText: westeurope; the workspace resource group's region wins when it exists
Location.effect: Used only when SI_Location is not set, and only when Risk Analysis creates missing resources. Existing resources are not moved.
Location.whenToChange: Never on new installs; set SI_Location instead.

LockedYamlFile.label: Shipped asset tagging rules file
LockedYamlFile.purpose: File name of the shipped asset tagging rules in the rules folder.
LockedYamlFile.effect: The engine loads the shipped rules from this file. A wrong name loses the shipped rules; with neither rules file present the run stops. Ignored when rules come from the Pro settings database.
LockedYamlFile.whenToChange: Practically never; the shipped name should be kept.

Mail_CloseLoop_Daily_SendMail.label: Send the daily vulnerability mail
Mail_CloseLoop_Daily_SendMail.purpose: Sends one mail a day with the vulnerabilities opened, closed and reopened in the last 24 hours, what is open now and the mean time to fix.
Mail_CloseLoop_Daily_SendMail.effect: On: a daily job mails the summary to the close-loop recipients through the same mail server as the Risk Analysis mail. Nothing is sent without recipients.
Mail_CloseLoop_Daily_SendMail.whenToChange: Turn on when the team should get a daily view of vulnerability progress.

Mail_CloseLoop_Daily_SendTimeUtc.label: Daily vulnerability mail time (UTC)
Mail_CloseLoop_Daily_SendTimeUtc.purpose: The time of day, in UTC, the daily vulnerability mail is sent.
Mail_CloseLoop_Daily_SendTimeUtc.defaultText: 10:45 UTC, after the close-loop and data sync
Mail_CloseLoop_Daily_SendTimeUtc.effect: Moves when the daily mail is sent. A time before the close-loop finishes mails yesterday's state. An invalid value falls back to 10:45. Takes effect when setup is run again.
Mail_CloseLoop_Daily_SendTimeUtc.whenToChange: Only to fit recipients' working hours; keep it after the close-loop run.
Mail_CloseLoop_Daily_SendTimeUtc.hint: HH:mm. Takes effect when setup runs again.

Mail_CloseLoop_Daily_To.label: Daily vulnerability mail recipients
Mail_CloseLoop_Daily_To.purpose: The addresses that receive the daily vulnerability mail.
Mail_CloseLoop_Daily_To.defaultText: No recipients: the mail is not sent, and the run says so
Mail_CloseLoop_Daily_To.effect: Adding addresses makes the daily close-loop mail go to them, provided Mail_CloseLoop_Daily_SendMail is on. Removing them all stops the mail without failing the job.
Mail_CloseLoop_Daily_To.whenToChange: Set it when you turn on the close-loop daily mail, or when the team that follows up on fixes changes.

Mail_SecurityInsight_Detailed_SendMail.label: Detailed report mail on (older name)
Mail_SecurityInsight_Detailed_SendMail.purpose: Older name for switching e-mail of the Detailed Risk Analysis report on or off.
Mail_SecurityInsight_Detailed_SendMail.defaultText: Not set: RiskAnalysis_Detailed_SendMail or SendMail decides
Mail_SecurityInsight_Detailed_SendMail.effect: Same as RiskAnalysis_Detailed_SendMail, which wins when both are set.
Mail_SecurityInsight_Detailed_SendMail.whenToChange: Only kept for older configuration files; use RiskAnalysis_Detailed_SendMail instead.

Mail_SecurityInsight_Detailed_To.label: Detailed report recipients (older name)
Mail_SecurityInsight_Detailed_To.purpose: Older name for the recipient list of the Detailed Risk Analysis report.
Mail_SecurityInsight_Detailed_To.defaultText: Not set: RiskAnalysis_Detailed_To, else MailTo, is used
Mail_SecurityInsight_Detailed_To.effect: Same as RiskAnalysis_Detailed_To, which wins when both are set.
Mail_SecurityInsight_Detailed_To.whenToChange: Only kept for older configuration files; use RiskAnalysis_Detailed_To instead.

Mail_SecurityInsight_Summary_SendMail.label: Summary report mail on (older name)
Mail_SecurityInsight_Summary_SendMail.purpose: Older name for switching e-mail of the Summary Risk Analysis report on or off.
Mail_SecurityInsight_Summary_SendMail.defaultText: Not set: RiskAnalysis_Summary_SendMail or SendMail decides
Mail_SecurityInsight_Summary_SendMail.effect: Same as RiskAnalysis_Summary_SendMail, which wins when both are set.
Mail_SecurityInsight_Summary_SendMail.whenToChange: Only kept for older configuration files; use RiskAnalysis_Summary_SendMail instead.

Mail_SecurityInsight_Summary_To.label: Summary report recipients (older name)
Mail_SecurityInsight_Summary_To.purpose: Older name for the recipient list of the Summary Risk Analysis report.
Mail_SecurityInsight_Summary_To.defaultText: Not set: RiskAnalysis_Summary_To, else MailTo, is used
Mail_SecurityInsight_Summary_To.effect: Same as RiskAnalysis_Summary_To, which wins when both are set.
Mail_SecurityInsight_Summary_To.whenToChange: Only kept for older configuration files; use RiskAnalysis_Summary_To instead.

Mail_SendAnonymous.label: Send mail without sign-in
Mail_SendAnonymous.purpose: Sends mail through a relay that accepts mail without a user name and password.
Mail_SendAnonymous.defaultText: Off: the mail server sign-in (user, password, sender) is required
Mail_SendAnonymous.effect: On: no SMTP credentials are needed or checked. Off with mail switched on: the run stops at start if the sender, user or password is missing. A relay that requires sign-in rejects anonymous mail.
Mail_SendAnonymous.whenToChange: Only when your internal relay accepts unauthenticated mail from this host.

MailTo.label: Default recipients
MailTo.purpose: The addresses that receive every Risk Analysis report that has no recipient list of its own.
MailTo.effect: Reports go to these addresses unless a report-specific list exists. If mail is switched on and no recipient list is set anywhere, the run stops at start.
MailTo.whenToChange: Set it when one group should receive every Risk Analysis report.
MailTo.hint: Get every report without a list of its own.

MaxAiSpendPerRun.label: AI spend limit per run
MaxAiSpendPerRun.purpose: Caps the estimated Azure OpenAI spend (in US dollars) of AI classification in one profiling run.
MaxAiSpendPerRun.defaultText: Container jobs: 4 US dollars. VM runs: no limit
MaxAiSpendPerRun.effect: When the estimate reaches the cap, remaining assets are classified without AI and marked as budget-capped. Higher caps allow more AI classification at more cost.
MaxAiSpendPerRun.whenToChange: Raise for large estates using AI classification; lower to control cost.

OpenAI_apiKey.label: Azure OpenAI key (Key Vault secret name)
OpenAI_apiKey.purpose: The NAME of the Key Vault secret that holds the key of your Azure OpenAI resource -- never the key itself. Get Started > AI integration stores the key in your Key Vault and fills this in.
OpenAI_apiKey.defaultText: Not set: AI classification is skipped; an AI summary request fails
OpenAI_apiKey.effect: With endpoint and deployment set, AI features can run. Keep it in Key Vault rather than in a file.
OpenAI_apiKey.whenToChange: When turning on AI features or rotating the key.

OpenAI_apiVersion.label: Azure OpenAI API version
OpenAI_apiVersion.purpose: The Azure OpenAI API version used when calling your model deployment.
OpenAI_apiVersion.defaultText: 2024-08-01-preview (Risk Analysis, the tier classifier and the profiling engines alike)
OpenAI_apiVersion.effect: Must be a version your Azure OpenAI resource supports; an unsupported version makes AI calls fail.
OpenAI_apiVersion.whenToChange: Rarely; when your deployment needs a newer API version.

OpenAI_deployment.label: Azure OpenAI deployment
OpenAI_deployment.purpose: Name of the Azure OpenAI model deployment used for AI classification and AI summaries.
OpenAI_deployment.defaultText: Not set: AI classification is skipped; an AI summary request fails
OpenAI_deployment.effect: Chooses which model answers; a larger model may give better text at higher cost. AI features stay off unless endpoint, key and deployment are all set.
OpenAI_deployment.whenToChange: When turning on AI features or moving to another model deployment.

OpenAI_endpoint.label: Azure OpenAI endpoint
OpenAI_endpoint.purpose: The web address of your Azure OpenAI resource, used for AI classification, AI tiering of roles and AI report summaries.
OpenAI_endpoint.defaultText: Not set: AI classification is skipped and AI summaries cannot run.
OpenAI_endpoint.effect: With endpoint, key and deployment all set, engines that have AI switched on call your Azure OpenAI. Missing it, profiling falls back to rule-based tiers, role tiering marks items for manual review, and an AI summary request stops the report run.
OpenAI_endpoint.whenToChange: Set it when you want AI features; change it only when you move to another Azure OpenAI resource.

OpenAI_MaxTokensPerRequest.label: AI summary answer length
OpenAI_MaxTokensPerRequest.purpose: The largest answer, in tokens, the AI may return for each risk-analysis summary request.
OpenAI_MaxTokensPerRequest.defaultText: 16384 tokens, unless the older AI_MaxTokensPerRequest is set
OpenAI_MaxTokensPerRequest.effect: Higher allows longer AI summaries but costs more per call and may exceed what your model deployment allows; lower gives shorter, cheaper summaries that may be cut off.
OpenAI_MaxTokensPerRequest.whenToChange: Rarely; lower it if your model has a smaller limit, raise it if summaries are cut short.

OverwriteXlsx.label: Replace Excel workbook each run
OverwriteXlsx.purpose: Deletes the previous risk analysis Excel workbook at the start of a run and writes a fresh one.
OverwriteXlsx.defaultText: On: a fresh workbook every run.
OverwriteXlsx.effect: Off, the run writes into the existing workbook instead, so older content can remain alongside new results.

RA_MailEvenIfEmpty.label: Mail reports with no findings
RA_MailEvenIfEmpty.purpose: Sends the report mail even when a run found nothing, as a sign the job ran.
RA_MailEvenIfEmpty.defaultText: Off: a report with no rows is not mailed.
RA_MailEvenIfEmpty.effect: When on, recipients get a mail after every run, including empty ones, confirming the job is alive. When off, an empty run sends nothing.
RA_MailEvenIfEmpty.whenToChange: Turn on if you want a daily confirmation mail even when there are no findings.

ReportTemplate.label: Risk analysis report template
ReportTemplate.purpose: Names the report template risk analysis runs: RiskAnalysis_Summary (compact) or RiskAnalysis_Detailed (one row per finding).
ReportTemplate.effect: The launchers and containers set this themselves from the command line or the per-mode template settings, so a value in the config file is only honoured when the engine is run directly.

ResetCache.label: Reset query split memory
ResetCache.purpose: Deletes the saved query split counts at the start of a run so they are probed again.
ResetCache.effect: On, the next run re-probes every large query from scratch, so it takes longer; the new counts are saved again afterwards.
ResetCache.whenToChange: For one run when reports look incomplete or after a large estate change.

RiskAnalysis_Detailed_Override.label: Default to Detailed mode
RiskAnalysis_Detailed_Override.purpose: Makes risk analysis run in Detailed mode unless Summary is asked for on the command line.
RiskAnalysis_Detailed_Override.defaultText: Off: runs default to Summary mode.
RiskAnalysis_Detailed_Override.effect: On, scheduled runs produce one row per affected asset: larger Excel files, longer runs, more data ingested, and the Detailed mail recipients. Cannot be on together with RiskAnalysis_Summary_Override.
RiskAnalysis_Detailed_Override.whenToChange: When a host should produce Detailed reports by default.
RiskAnalysis_Detailed_Override.hint: Used when a run does not say which report.

RiskAnalysis_Detailed_SendMail.label: Mail the Detailed report
RiskAnalysis_Detailed_SendMail.purpose: Mails the Detailed Risk Analysis report after each run.
RiskAnalysis_Detailed_SendMail.defaultText: Not set: the older name, else SendMail (off) decides
RiskAnalysis_Detailed_SendMail.effect: On: each Detailed run mails the full report to its recipients; this needs working mail server settings. A report template's own mail switch still wins.
RiskAnalysis_Detailed_SendMail.whenToChange: Turn on when the security team should receive the full Detailed report by mail.
RiskAnalysis_Detailed_SendMail.hint: Not set: Mail every report decides.

RiskAnalysis_Detailed_To.label: Detailed report recipients
RiskAnalysis_Detailed_To.purpose: The addresses that receive the Detailed Risk Analysis report.
RiskAnalysis_Detailed_To.defaultText: Not set: the older name, else MailTo, is used
RiskAnalysis_Detailed_To.effect: Detailed reports go to these addresses instead of the default list. Blank entries are dropped with a warning. A report template's own recipients still win.
RiskAnalysis_Detailed_To.whenToChange: Set it when the Detailed report should go to different people than the default list.
RiskAnalysis_Detailed_To.hint: Empty: the default recipients get it.

RiskAnalysis_ReportTemplate_Default_Deta.label: Detailed report template
RiskAnalysis_ReportTemplate_Default_Deta.purpose: The report template used for Detailed runs when no template is named explicitly.
RiskAnalysis_ReportTemplate_Default_Deta.effect: Detailed runs and the Detailed container job use the named template instead. A template name that does not exist makes the run fail.
RiskAnalysis_ReportTemplate_Default_Deta.whenToChange: When you have created your own Detailed template.

RiskAnalysis_ReportTemplate_Default_Summ.label: Summary report template
RiskAnalysis_ReportTemplate_Default_Summ.purpose: The report template used for Summary runs when no template is named explicitly.
RiskAnalysis_ReportTemplate_Default_Summ.effect: Summary runs and the Summary container job use the named template instead. A template name that does not exist makes the run fail.
RiskAnalysis_ReportTemplate_Default_Summ.whenToChange: When you have created your own Summary template.

RiskAnalysis_Summary_Override.label: Default to Summary mode
RiskAnalysis_Summary_Override.purpose: Makes risk analysis run in Summary mode unless Detailed is asked for on the command line.
RiskAnalysis_Summary_Override.defaultText: Summary mode is already the launcher's default.
RiskAnalysis_Summary_Override.effect: On keeps runs in compact Summary mode with the Summary table and recipients. Cannot be on together with RiskAnalysis_Detailed_Override; set it off when you switch a host to Detailed.
RiskAnalysis_Summary_Override.whenToChange: Rarely; only to make the Summary choice explicit.
RiskAnalysis_Summary_Override.hint: Used when a run does not say which report.

RiskAnalysis_Summary_SendMail.label: Mail the Summary report
RiskAnalysis_Summary_SendMail.purpose: Mails the Summary Risk Analysis report after each run.
RiskAnalysis_Summary_SendMail.defaultText: Not set: the older name, else SendMail (off) decides
RiskAnalysis_Summary_SendMail.effect: On: each Summary run mails the report to its recipients; this needs working mail server settings. A report template's own mail switch still wins. While the Summary step is off (the default since 2026-10), the management mail -- the Detailed report's mail, with its management summary -- goes to these recipients instead.
RiskAnalysis_Summary_SendMail.whenToChange: Turn on when management or the security team should receive the Summary report by mail.
RiskAnalysis_Summary_SendMail.hint: Not set: Mail every report decides.

RiskAnalysis_Summary_To.label: Summary report recipients
RiskAnalysis_Summary_To.purpose: The addresses that receive the Summary Risk Analysis report.
RiskAnalysis_Summary_To.defaultText: Not set: the older name, else MailTo, is used
RiskAnalysis_Summary_To.effect: Summary reports go to these addresses instead of the default list. Blank entries are dropped with a warning. A report template's own recipients still win. While the Summary step is off (the default since 2026-10), these addresses receive the management mail -- the Detailed report's mail -- when Mail the Summary report is on.
RiskAnalysis_Summary_To.whenToChange: Set it when the Summary report should go to different people than the default list.
RiskAnalysis_Summary_To.hint: Empty: the default recipients get it.

Scope.label: Asset tagging rule scope
Scope.purpose: Which asset tagging rules run, by the mode each rule is marked with: PROD, TEST, or both.
Scope.effect: Adding TEST also runs rules marked as test rules, which can tag assets with untried logic. Rules whose mode is not listed are skipped. Risk analysis does not read this setting.
Scope.whenToChange: To try new tagging rules marked TEST before promoting them.

SendMail.label: Mail every report
SendMail.purpose: Mails each Risk Analysis report, unless a report's own switch says otherwise.
SendMail.effect: On: reports are mailed to MailTo (or the report-specific lists). The run stops at start if mail is on but no recipients or required mail server sign-in details are set.
SendMail.whenToChange: Turn on to mail every report; use the Summary/Detailed switches for finer control.
SendMail.hint: Used when a report's own switch below is not set.

SendToLogAnalytics.label: Copy Risk Analysis report rows to Log Analytics (SI_RiskAnalysis_Detailed_CL)
SendToLogAnalytics.purpose: Optional. After each Risk Analysis run, copies its report rows into your Log Analytics workspace (SI_RiskAnalysis_Detailed_CL, and SI_RiskAnalysis_Summary_CL when the Summary report runs; the day's trend row in SI_Trend_CL), for your own workbooks, Sentinel or KQL. SecurityInsight itself does not need it: its pages, the data sync, the vulnerability connectors and the trends read the results from its database. On a large estate the copy takes a long time and adds Log Analytics ingestion cost. Off by default.
SendToLogAnalytics.defaultText: Off: the report rows are kept in the database only
SendToLogAnalytics.effect: On: after every Risk Analysis run its report rows are also posted to SI_RiskAnalysis_Detailed_CL (SI_RiskAnalysis_Summary_CL for the Summary report), after the result is complete in the database, and the day's trend row to SI_Trend_CL. On a large estate that is close to an hour, and it costs ingestion for every row, every run. Off: nothing is copied; the Excel reports, the mail and everything SecurityInsight shows are unchanged. The Azure workbook in preview\AzureWorkbook reads the copy, so it needs it on.
SendToLogAnalytics.whenToChange: Only when your own workbooks, Sentinel rules or KQL queries read SI_RiskAnalysis_Detailed_CL, SI_RiskAnalysis_Summary_CL or SI_Trend_CL; leave off otherwise.
SendToLogAnalytics.hint: Off = the report rows stay in the database. On = also a copy in Log Analytics (takes long on a large estate, costs ingestion).

SettingsPath.label: Asset tagging rules folder
SettingsPath.purpose: The folder the asset tagging engine reads its tagging rule files from.
SettingsPath.defaultText: The shipped rule files next to the endpoint enrichment rules.
SettingsPath.effect: Point it at your own folder to tag with your own rule files instead of the shipped ones. A missing folder stops the run with a clear error. The Risk Analysis and privilege tier launchers set their own folder and ignore this value.
SettingsPath.whenToChange: Only when you keep your own tagging rule files outside the installation.

SHODAN_ApiKey.label: Shodan API key (older name)
SHODAN_ApiKey.purpose: Older name for the Shodan API key the public IP engine uses to look up your public IP addresses.
SHODAN_ApiKey.defaultText: Not set: the key under its current name is used; without any key, Shodan details stay empty.
SHODAN_ApiKey.effect: Used only when SI_Shodan_ApiKey is not set. Without any key the public IP engine still runs, but every Shodan field (open ports, services, vulnerabilities) is empty.
SHODAN_ApiKey.whenToChange: Prefer SI_Shodan_ApiKey; keep this only for older configuration files.

ShowConfig.label: Show resolved configuration
ShowConfig.purpose: Prints the configuration risk analysis actually uses at start-up, so you can see which values are in effect.
ShowConfig.effect: On adds a configuration listing to the run log, including identifiers from your setup; no effect on reports.
ShowConfig.whenToChange: When troubleshooting which value is in effect.

SI_ActiveStaleDays.label: Active asset freshness window
SI_ActiveStaleDays.purpose: Sets how recently an asset must have been seen (or an identity signed in) to count as active.
SI_ActiveStaleDays.effect: Lower values mark more assets inactive; inactive endpoints are left out of the profile output and identities without a recent sign-in are flagged inactive. Higher values keep older, possibly retired assets in reports.
SI_ActiveStaleDays.whenToChange: Most installs keep 30. Lower for tighter hygiene reporting; raise if devices are often offline for long periods.

SI_AI_CostPerCallEstimate.label: AI cost per call estimate
SI_AI_CostPerCallEstimate.purpose: The estimated price in US dollars of one AI call, used to keep each run within its AI spending budget.
SI_AI_CostPerCallEstimate.effect: The engines count this amount per AI call against the run's AI budget. A higher estimate stops AI calls sooner (more assets classified by rules only); a lower one allows more calls and higher real cost.
SI_AI_CostPerCallEstimate.whenToChange: After a few real runs, set it to your observed cost per call.

SI_AISummary_Leader.label: Leading report for AI summary
SI_AISummary_Leader.purpose: In Consistent mode, chooses which report (Summary or Detailed) builds the AI summary, risk score and top list that the other report reuses.
SI_AISummary_Leader.effect: The leading report always computes its own figures; the other copies them so both mails agree. An unknown value falls back to Detailed with a warning. Ignored in PerReport mode. With the Summary step off (the default) only the Detailed report runs, so it always leads.
SI_AISummary_Leader.whenToChange: Set to Summary only when the Summary step is switched on and management mainly receives the Summary report.
SI_AISummary_Leader.group: Risk Analysis -- mails and executive view

SI_AISummary_MaxAgeHours.label: AI summary reuse age limit
SI_AISummary_MaxAgeHours.purpose: How old the leading report's saved summary may be before the other report stops reusing it and builds its own.
SI_AISummary_MaxAgeHours.effect: Higher lets an older summary be reused, so figures can be stale after a missed run. Lower makes the follower build its own figures more often, costing more AI calls.
SI_AISummary_MaxAgeHours.whenToChange: Only if your two reports run more than a day apart.
SI_AISummary_MaxAgeHours.group: Risk Analysis -- mails and executive view

SI_AISummary_Mode.label: Summary and Detailed agreement
SI_AISummary_Mode.purpose: Chooses whether the Summary and Detailed reports show identical AI summary, risk score and top list, or each shows its own figures.
SI_AISummary_Mode.defaultText: Depends on the edition. SecurityInsight Pro: PerReport -- each report shows its own figures (Summary counts distinct assets, Detailed counts individual findings). Community: Consistent -- both reports show the same figures. A value you set wins in both editions.
SI_AISummary_Mode.effect: Consistent makes one report reuse the other's figures, saving AI calls. PerReport makes each report compute its own, so totals differ. Unknown values fall back to the edition's default.
SI_AISummary_Mode.whenToChange: Choose PerReport when each audience receives only one report, or (Pro) to compare Summary and Detailed in the web app. Choose Consistent when management receives both mails and they must show the same figures.
SI_AISummary_Mode.group: Risk Analysis -- mails and executive view

valueLabels.Consistent: Same figures in both reports, from the leading report
valueLabels.PerReport: Each report shows its own figures

SI_AssetDecisionsPath.label: Asset decisions file
SI_AssetDecisionsPath.purpose: Path to your file of asset decisions: tier overrides, exceptions and exemptions applied during profiling.
SI_AssetDecisionsPath.defaultText: The asset decisions file in the config folder and in your enrichment data folder, if they exist.
SI_AssetDecisionsPath.effect: When set, only this file is read and the default locations are ignored. A path that does not exist is reported, and none of your decisions are applied.
SI_AssetDecisionsPath.whenToChange: When you keep the decisions file outside the installation folder.

SI_AssetProperties.label: Asset properties
SI_AssetProperties.purpose: How much SecurityInsight keeps about each asset: security (what SecurityInsight needs for risk) or full (all metadata from every source, kept a few days).
SI_AssetProperties.defaultText: security: the security profile only -- what SecurityInsight needs for risk
SI_AssetProperties.effect: 'security' (the default) keeps what SecurityInsight needs for risk -- name, kind, tier and the security fields each profile carries -- and stores nothing extra. 'full' also keeps every property each source knows about an asset -- Defender, Entra, Intune, Active Directory, Azure, Exposure Graph and VM extensions, including serial numbers and MAC addresses. Each source is still read only once: the profiler reads it with every property and builds the same security profile from it, so the profile does not change. The whole objects go to SI_AssetProperties_CL for the CMDB and vulnerability hand-off, and the data sync stores them in the Pro database, where the asset page shows them under "Full metadata" per source (lists stay lists), with a history of every snapshot kept and what changed between them. It is kept for the days set in "Full asset metadata: days kept" (default 3). Full adds Log Analytics ingest on every run; switching back to security stops the collection, and what was stored ages out after those days.
SI_AssetProperties.whenToChange: Choose full when you want to see every property of an asset in the web app, or when SecurityInsight should hand asset metadata to a CMDB (for example ServiceNow); leave security otherwise.
SI_AssetProperties.hint: Security = what SecurityInsight needs for risk. Full = all metadata from every source, kept a few days.

valueLabels.security: Security: what SecurityInsight needs for risk
valueLabels.full: Full: all metadata from every source, kept a few days

SI_AssetProperties_ChangeGuardPercent.label: Full asset metadata: allowed change between runs
SI_AssetProperties_ChangeGuardPercent.purpose: How much the full asset metadata collected from one source may change from one run to the next before the hand-off of that source is held.
SI_AssetProperties_ChangeGuardPercent.effect: When a source (for example Defender, Entra or Azure) returns more than this share more or fewer objects than in the previous run, the previous collection of that source is kept for the CMDB and vulnerability hand-off, and a guard event is raised (mail and Operations > Guards (safety checks)). The hold ends by itself on the next run that is back within the limit, or once when an Admin releases it.
SI_AssetProperties_ChangeGuardPercent.whenToChange: Raise it if your estate legitimately changes a lot between runs; lower it to be warned of smaller changes.

SI_AssetProperties_RetentionDays.label: Full asset metadata: days kept
SI_AssetProperties_RetentionDays.purpose: How many days the full asset metadata is kept, in Log Analytics and in the Pro database.
SI_AssetProperties_RetentionDays.effect: The run sets the retention of SI_AssetProperties_CL to this many days (Log Analytics keeps a table at least 4 days, so a lower value is raised to 4 and the run says so), and the data sync removes older full metadata from the Pro database. Every snapshot inside these days is kept, so the asset page's history goes back this far. The data is only needed for the hand-off, the history and the change guard, so a short retention keeps the cost low.
SI_AssetProperties_RetentionDays.whenToChange: Raise it only if the full asset metadata must be looked up further back.

SI_AssetLimit_Azure.label: Azure asset limit
SI_AssetLimit_Azure.purpose: Caps how many discovered Azure resources the Azure engine processes in one run, for testing.
SI_AssetLimit_Azure.effect: Keeps only the first N resources after discovery, so runs are faster but the inventory and every report built on it are incomplete. A command-line value wins over this.
SI_AssetLimit_Azure.whenToChange: Never in production; only for quick local tests.

SI_AssetLimit_Endpoint.label: Endpoint asset limit
SI_AssetLimit_Endpoint.purpose: Caps how many discovered devices the endpoint engine processes in one run, for testing.
SI_AssetLimit_Endpoint.effect: Keeps only the first N devices after discovery, so runs are faster but the inventory and every report built on it are incomplete. A command-line value wins over this.
SI_AssetLimit_Endpoint.whenToChange: Never in production; only for quick local tests.

SI_AssetLimit_Identity.label: Identity asset limit
SI_AssetLimit_Identity.purpose: Caps how many discovered users and service principals the identity engine processes in one run, for testing.
SI_AssetLimit_Identity.effect: Keeps only the first N identities after discovery, so runs are faster but the inventory and every report built on it are incomplete. A command-line value wins over this.
SI_AssetLimit_Identity.whenToChange: Never in production; only for quick local tests.

SI_AssetLimit_PublicIp.label: Public IP asset limit
SI_AssetLimit_PublicIp.purpose: Caps how many public IP addresses the public IP engine processes in one run, for testing.
SI_AssetLimit_PublicIp.effect: Keeps only the first N addresses after discovery, so runs are faster and use fewer Shodan credits, but the inventory and reports are incomplete. A command-line value wins over this.
SI_AssetLimit_PublicIp.whenToChange: Never in production; only for quick local tests.

SI_AssetTagActivityDcr.label: Tag activity collection rule
SI_AssetTagActivityDcr.purpose: Name of the data collection rule used to send the asset-tagging activity log to Log Analytics.
SI_AssetTagActivityDcr.effect: Tagging activity rows are sent through this rule instead. A rule that does not match the activity table makes the activity log stop arriving.
SI_AssetTagActivityDcr.whenToChange: Almost never; only to avoid a name clash with an existing rule.

SI_AssetTagActivityTable.label: Tag activity table name
SI_AssetTagActivityTable.purpose: Log Analytics table receiving the asset-tagging activity log: which tags were or would be applied or removed.
SI_AssetTagActivityTable.effect: Tagging activity from both the tagging engine and the profilers' read-only tagging check goes to this table. Queries reading the standard table will no longer see new rows.
SI_AssetTagActivityTable.whenToChange: Almost never; only to avoid a clash with an existing table.

SI_AuthMethod.label: Sign-in method
SI_AuthMethod.purpose: Chooses how SecurityInsight signs in to Microsoft services: managed identity, service principal with certificate, or service principal with client secret.
SI_AuthMethod.defaultText: Keeps a configured service principal; otherwise the host's managed identity
SI_AuthMethod.effect: Decides which identity every engine uses, and therefore which permissions must be granted. An unknown value stops the run with an error. Choosing a service principal switches managed-identity sign-in off.
SI_AuthMethod.whenToChange: Set during setup. Change when moving between managed identity and a service principal.

SI_AutoBucketDefaultDetailed.label: Detailed report starting buckets
SI_AutoBucketDefaultDetailed.purpose: How many slices a Detailed Risk Analysis query is split into on the first try, before automatic splitting adapts.
SI_AutoBucketDefaultDetailed.effect: More slices avoid query timeouts on very large tenants but add overhead per slice, making small tenants slower. A per-report bucket count in the report template still wins.
SI_AutoBucketDefaultDetailed.whenToChange: Only if Detailed reports repeatedly time out on a very large tenant.

SI_AutoBucketSubFanOut.label: Query split fan-out
SI_AutoBucketSubFanOut.purpose: How many smaller pieces a timed-out Risk Analysis query slice is split into each time.
SI_AutoBucketSubFanOut.effect: More pieces shrink heavy slices faster but run more queries; fewer pieces mean more split rounds. No rows are lost either way.
SI_AutoBucketSubFanOut.whenToChange: Rarely; only when tuning very large tenants with support.

SI_AzSubscriptionId.label: Azure subscription for ingestion
SI_AzSubscriptionId.purpose: The Azure subscription in which the engines look up and create the data collection endpoint and rules.
SI_AzSubscriptionId.defaultText: Taken from the workspace resource id, else SubscriptionId
SI_AzSubscriptionId.effect: Scopes all endpoint and rule lookups and resource creation to this subscription. A wrong value makes ingestion refuse to post or create resources in the wrong subscription.
SI_AzSubscriptionId.whenToChange: Only when the ingestion resources live in a different subscription than the workspace.

SI_Azure_DcrName.label: Azure profile collection rule
SI_Azure_DcrName.purpose: Name of the data collection rule the Azure profiling engine sends its results through.
SI_Azure_DcrName.effect: Azure profile rows are ingested through this rule instead. Useful to avoid picking up a same-named rule from an older install; a wrong name makes ingestion fail.
SI_Azure_DcrName.whenToChange: Only when another rule with the standard name is visible to the identity.

SI_Azure_TableName.label: Azure profile table name
SI_Azure_TableName.purpose: Log Analytics table the Azure profiling engine writes its asset profiles to.
SI_Azure_TableName.effect: Azure profiles go to this table instead. Risk Analysis and workbooks that read the standard table will no longer see new Azure data unless changed too.
SI_Azure_TableName.whenToChange: Almost never; only to avoid a clash with an existing table.

SI_AzureEgNonAssetTypes.label: Azure types not treated as assets
SI_AzureEgNonAssetTypes.purpose: Azure resource types from the exposure graph that are settings on other resources, not assets, and are left out of Azure collection.
SI_AzureEgNonAssetTypes.defaultText: Role and policy assignments and definitions, locks and diagnostic settings.
SI_AzureEgNonAssetTypes.effect: Replaces the list. Removing a type brings those items back as Azure assets, which can greatly increase row counts and duplicates; adding a type removes it from collection.
SI_AzureEgNonAssetTypes.whenToChange: Only if you genuinely want one of these types profiled, or another type excluded.

SI_AzureEgTypeAllowlist.label: Azure exposure graph type list
SI_AzureEgTypeAllowlist.purpose: Fixes which Azure resource types are read from the Defender exposure graph, the Azure engine's main source.
SI_AzureEgTypeAllowlist.defaultText: Every Azure type in the exposure graph, minus role/policy assignments, locks and diagnostic settings.
SI_AzureEgTypeAllowlist.effect: Replaces the automatically discovered type list entirely, so only the types you list are collected from the exposure graph. New Azure types are no longer picked up automatically, and the built-in exclusion of non-asset types no longer applies.
SI_AzureEgTypeAllowlist.whenToChange: Only to narrow collection to specific types, for example in a very large estate.

SI_AzureExcludeTypes.label: Azure resource types to skip
SI_AzureExcludeTypes.purpose: Extra Azure resource types the Resource Graph source leaves out, on top of the built-in list of noisy types.
SI_AzureExcludeTypes.defaultText: Only the built-in list of 7 noisy types (alerts, assessments, policy states and similar) is skipped.
SI_AzureExcludeTypes.effect: The types you list are added to the built-in skip list for the Resource Graph source, reducing data volume and run time. Resources of those types disappear from the Azure inventory unless the exposure graph also returns them.
SI_AzureExcludeTypes.whenToChange: When a high-volume type adds noise to your Azure inventory.

SI_AzureExposureGraph_AccessEdgeLabels.label: Azure access relationship types
SI_AzureExposureGraph_AccessEdgeLabels.purpose: Which exposure graph relationship types count as an identity having access to an Azure resource.
SI_AzureExposureGraph_AccessEdgeLabels.defaultText: The shipped list of 6 relationship types, such as 'has access to' and 'has permissions to'.
SI_AzureExposureGraph_AccessEdgeLabels.effect: Changes which access paths are counted when the engine works out which privileged identities can reach each Azure resource. A list that misses real relationship names leaves those counts empty.
SI_AzureExposureGraph_AccessEdgeLabels.whenToChange: Only if your Defender exposure graph uses non-standard relationship names.

SI_AzureExposureGraph_IdentityLabels.label: Azure access identity types
SI_AzureExposureGraph_IdentityLabels.purpose: Which exposure graph node types are treated as identities when mapping who can access Azure resources.
SI_AzureExposureGraph_IdentityLabels.defaultText: User, service principal, managed identity and group.
SI_AzureExposureGraph_IdentityLabels.effect: Changes which kinds of identity are counted as having access to Azure resources. Leaving a type out hides access held by that kind of identity.
SI_AzureExposureGraph_IdentityLabels.whenToChange: Only if your Defender exposure graph uses non-standard node names.

SI_AzureExposureGraph_ResourceLabels.label: Azure exposure graph resource types
SI_AzureExposureGraph_ResourceLabels.purpose: Which exposure graph node types are treated as Azure resources for extra exposure details and access mapping.
SI_AzureExposureGraph_ResourceLabels.defaultText: The shipped list of 16 resource types; access mapping also includes every other Azure resource type.
SI_AzureExposureGraph_ResourceLabels.effect: Restricts exposure detail lookups and access mapping to the types you list. Once set, access mapping no longer covers every other Azure resource type, so access counts can shrink.
SI_AzureExposureGraph_ResourceLabels.whenToChange: Only if your Defender exposure graph uses non-standard node names.

SI_AzureMaxResources.label: Azure Resource Graph row cap
SI_AzureMaxResources.purpose: A safety cap on how many resources the Azure engine pulls from Azure Resource Graph in one run.
SI_AzureMaxResources.defaultText: No cap of its own; Resource Graph's own limit still applies.
SI_AzureMaxResources.effect: Stops reading Resource Graph once the cap is reached, which shortens first runs in large estates and limits AI spend. Resources beyond the cap are missing unless the exposure graph returns them.
SI_AzureMaxResources.whenToChange: For a first run in a very large estate; remove it afterwards.

SI_AzureRecommendation_DcrName.label: Azure recommendations collection rule
SI_AzureRecommendation_DcrName.purpose: Name of the data collection rule used to send Defender for Cloud recommendations to Log Analytics.
SI_AzureRecommendation_DcrName.effect: Recommendations are sent through this rule instead. A rule that does not match the recommendations table makes them stop arriving.
SI_AzureRecommendation_DcrName.whenToChange: Almost never; only to avoid a name clash with an existing rule.
