SI_AzureRecommendation_TableName.label: Azure recommendations table name
SI_AzureRecommendation_TableName.purpose: Log Analytics table that receives Defender for Cloud recommendations collected with the Azure engine.
SI_AzureRecommendation_TableName.effect: Recommendations go to this table instead. Queries reading the standard table will no longer see new rows.
SI_AzureRecommendation_TableName.whenToChange: Almost never; only to avoid a clash with an existing table.

SI_AzureResourceTypes.label: Azure resource types to collect
SI_AzureResourceTypes.purpose: Restricts the Azure Resource Graph source to a hand-picked list of resource types.
SI_AzureResourceTypes.defaultText: Every resource type the sign-in identity can read.
SI_AzureResourceTypes.effect: Only the listed types are read from Resource Graph, which lowers run time and data volume. Other types then come only from the exposure graph, so brand-new resources of those types may be missed.
SI_AzureResourceTypes.whenToChange: Only when you deliberately want a narrow Azure inventory.

SI_AzureSubscriptionExcludePatterns.label: Subscriptions skipped for identity roles
SI_AzureSubscriptionExcludePatterns.purpose: Subscription names (wildcards allowed) skipped when the identity engine scans Azure role assignments.
SI_AzureSubscriptionExcludePatterns.defaultText: No subscriptions skipped; every visible subscription is scanned.
SI_AzureSubscriptionExcludePatterns.effect: Role assignments in matching subscriptions are ignored, which speeds up the scan but hides privileges granted there, so identities may get a lower tier than they really hold.
SI_AzureSubscriptionExcludePatterns.whenToChange: To skip personal, trial or lab subscriptions that do not matter for privilege.

SI_Bootstrap_AcrName.label: Container registry name
SI_Bootstrap_AcrName.purpose: Name of the Azure Container Registry that holds the SecurityInsight container image; container setup creates it if it does not exist.
SI_Bootstrap_AcrName.defaultText: acrsecurityinsight (new installs get a name chosen by setup)
SI_Bootstrap_AcrName.effect: Setup builds and stores the image in this registry and the jobs pull from it. A new name creates a new registry and image; updates also use it to find a container install.
SI_Bootstrap_AcrName.whenToChange: Only before the first container setup, to follow your naming rules.

SI_Pipeline_StartTime.label: Daily pipeline start time
SI_Pipeline_StartTime.purpose: The time of day a new install's daily pipeline (Collect, Correlate, Deliver) starts, in the pipeline's time zone.
SI_Pipeline_StartTime.defaultText: 19:00 in the local time of the install's Azure region (Danish time when the region is not known)
SI_Pipeline_StartTime.effect: The pipeline starts at this local time every day; summer time moves the time in UTC, never the local time. A pipeline already stored on Operations > Jobs or in config\job-flow.custom.json keeps its own time -- change that one there.
SI_Pipeline_StartTime.whenToChange: When the collection should run at another time of day, for example to finish before the working day starts.

SI_Pipeline_TimeZone.label: Daily pipeline time zone
SI_Pipeline_TimeZone.purpose: The time zone the daily pipeline's start time is read in.
SI_Pipeline_TimeZone.defaultText: The time zone of the install's Azure region, written by the install (Europe/Copenhagen, Danish time, when the region is not known)
SI_Pipeline_TimeZone.effect: An IANA id such as Europe/Oslo or America/New_York, or a Windows id. The start time stays the same local time all year. An id the machine does not know is read as UTC, with a warning in the run log.
SI_Pipeline_TimeZone.whenToChange: Set it to the time zone of the people who read the results; the guided installer asks for it.

SI_CiBuild_FullReconcileDays.label: CI build: days between full rebuilds
SI_CiBuild_FullReconcileDays.purpose: The CI build (correlation) rebuilds only the CIs whose input changed since their last build: a record new, changed, moved or gone, a link state, a time threshold, an identity anchor or a manual override. Every CI is rebuilt (a full reconcile) when the last full build is this many days old; also at once when the data model, rules, mappings or CMDB change, and after a build that failed.
SI_CiBuild_FullReconcileDays.defaultText: 7 days: every CI is rebuilt at least once a week; the days between build only what changed
SI_CiBuild_FullReconcileDays.effect: A lower value rebuilds every CI more often (a longer correlation run on those days); 0 rebuilds every CI on every run, as before. A full reconcile that finds a CI the daily builds should have changed says so in the run log.
SI_CiBuild_FullReconcileDays.whenToChange: Set 0 while support investigates a CI that looks out of date; otherwise keep the default.

SI_CiRulesBudgetSeconds.label: CI build: time limit for the rules of one asset
SI_CiRulesBudgetSeconds.purpose: How long the rules of one asset may take in the CI build (correlation) before the build goes on with the next asset. Applying the rules to one asset normally takes milliseconds; an asset with unusually large data could otherwise hold the whole build, and with it every step after it.
SI_CiRulesBudgetSeconds.effect: An asset that takes longer is not fully evaluated in that run. Nothing of the half evaluation is stored: Risk Analysis and the views keep what the asset had from its last complete evaluation, and a new asset is left out until it is fully evaluated. It is named in the run log, counted ("N asset(s) not fully evaluated in this run") and evaluated again in the next run. A higher value gives a slow asset more time; 0 removes the limit, and one asset can then hold the build for as long as its rules take.
SI_CiRulesBudgetSeconds.whenToChange: Raise it when the run log names the same assets as not fully evaluated run after run and they must be included before the cause is fixed; otherwise keep the default.

SI_Trend_AtEndOfRiskAnalysis.label: Write the risk trend at the end of Risk Analysis
SI_Trend_AtEndOfRiskAnalysis.purpose: Whether a Risk Analysis summary run writes the day's risk trend row itself, from the rows it has just published.
SI_Trend_AtEndOfRiskAnalysis.effect: On: one trend row per day, written by Risk Analysis -- the separate risk trend job is not needed and waits for a run by hand. Off: no trend row unless the risk trend job runs. A run that was partial writes no row (a gap, not a drop).
SI_Trend_AtEndOfRiskAnalysis.whenToChange: Only when you run the risk trend job on its own schedule instead.

SI_Bootstrap_Engines.label: Container jobs to deploy
SI_Bootstrap_Engines.purpose: The list of engines container setup creates scheduled jobs for.
SI_Bootstrap_Engines.defaultText: All standard engines, plus asset trend and the Pro engines where installed
SI_Bootstrap_Engines.effect: Only the listed engines get a job. When you set a list it is used exactly as given, so Pro and trend jobs are not added automatically. The role classifier is left out when Azure OpenAI is not configured.
SI_Bootstrap_Engines.whenToChange: When you want fewer jobs, or an engine not deployed by default, such as schema discovery.

SI_Bootstrap_EnvName.label: Container Apps environment name
SI_Bootstrap_EnvName.purpose: Name of the Azure Container Apps environment the SecurityInsight jobs run in; container setup creates it if it does not exist.
SI_Bootstrap_EnvName.defaultText: cae-securityinsight (new installs get a name chosen by setup)
SI_Bootstrap_EnvName.effect: All jobs are created in this environment. A new name creates a new environment and new jobs there; the old ones are left in place.
SI_Bootstrap_EnvName.whenToChange: Only before the first container setup, to follow your naming rules.

SI_Bootstrap_GrantTaggingRoles.label: Grant asset tagging write rights
SI_Bootstrap_GrantTaggingRoles.purpose: Lets container setup give the asset tagging job's own identity the rights it needs, including writing tags.
SI_Bootstrap_GrantTaggingRoles.defaultText: Off: rights are only listed, and the job can only report.
SI_Bootstrap_GrantTaggingRoles.effect: When on, setup grants the tagging identity its read rights plus write rights for Defender machine tags, Azure resource tags and Entra security attributes. Tags are written only when asset tagging is also set to apply.
SI_Bootstrap_GrantTaggingRoles.whenToChange: When you have decided SecurityInsight may write tags in your tenant.

SI_Bootstrap_ImageTag.label: Container image tag
SI_Bootstrap_ImageTag.purpose: The tag of the container image that setup builds and every scheduled job runs.
SI_Bootstrap_ImageTag.effect: Jobs run the image with this tag. A different tag lets you keep or test a specific build; a tag that was never built makes the jobs fail to start.
SI_Bootstrap_ImageTag.whenToChange: Only to pin or test a specific image build.

SI_Bootstrap_KedaMaxReplicas.label: Maximum queue-driven workers
SI_Bootstrap_KedaMaxReplicas.purpose: The most worker containers that may run at the same time per engine when queue-driven scaling is on.
SI_Bootstrap_KedaMaxReplicas.effect: Higher finishes large collections faster but runs more containers at once, raising peak cost and load on the source APIs. Has no effect unless queue-driven scaling is on.
SI_Bootstrap_KedaMaxReplicas.whenToChange: Only with queue-driven scaling, to speed up very large tenants or cap cost.

SI_Bootstrap_Location.label: Container hosting region
SI_Bootstrap_Location.purpose: The Azure region where container setup creates the registry, environment and identities.
SI_Bootstrap_Location.defaultText: Uses SI_Location; setup stops if neither is set.
SI_Bootstrap_Location.effect: All container resources are created in this region. It should match your other SecurityInsight resources; changing it later creates new resources in the new region.
SI_Bootstrap_Location.whenToChange: Set it once at setup if containers should live in a different region than SI_Location.

SI_Bootstrap_ParallelismAzure.label: Azure job containers in parallel
SI_Bootstrap_ParallelismAzure.purpose: How many containers the Azure profiling job runs side by side in each run.
SI_Bootstrap_ParallelismAzure.effect: More containers split the Azure collection and finish sooner, at higher compute cost per run and more parallel load on Azure APIs.
SI_Bootstrap_ParallelismAzure.whenToChange: Only for large Azure estates where the job runs too long.

SI_Bootstrap_ParallelismEndpoint.label: Endpoint job containers in parallel
SI_Bootstrap_ParallelismEndpoint.purpose: How many containers the endpoint profiling job runs side by side; also used for jobs that have no parallel setting of their own.
SI_Bootstrap_ParallelismEndpoint.effect: More containers split the collection and finish sooner, at higher compute cost per run. It also applies to other collection jobs without their own setting, such as public IP.
SI_Bootstrap_ParallelismEndpoint.whenToChange: Only for large estates where the endpoint job runs too long.

SI_Bootstrap_ParallelismIdentity.label: Identity job containers in parallel
SI_Bootstrap_ParallelismIdentity.purpose: How many containers the identity profiling job runs side by side in each run.
SI_Bootstrap_ParallelismIdentity.effect: More containers split the identity collection and finish sooner, at higher compute cost per run and more parallel load on Microsoft Graph.
SI_Bootstrap_ParallelismIdentity.whenToChange: Only for large directories where the job runs too long.

SI_Bootstrap_ParallelismSchemaDiscovery.label: Schema discovery containers in parallel
SI_Bootstrap_ParallelismSchemaDiscovery.purpose: How many containers the schema discovery job runs side by side in each run.
SI_Bootstrap_ParallelismSchemaDiscovery.effect: More containers finish schema discovery sooner at higher compute cost. Only matters when schema discovery is in the list of container jobs, which it is not by default.
SI_Bootstrap_ParallelismSchemaDiscovery.whenToChange: Rarely; only when schema discovery is deployed and runs too long.

SI_Bootstrap_RaMaxWorkers.label: Risk Analysis workers at once
SI_Bootstrap_RaMaxWorkers.purpose: How many Risk Analysis queue workers may run Detailed reports at the same time.
SI_Bootstrap_RaMaxWorkers.effect: More workers finish a long Risk Analysis sooner but run more containers at once. The workers share the parts one Risk Analysis job may ask Defender at a time (each at least one), so more workers do not multiply what Defender is asked at once. Has no effect when the Risk Analysis workers are off.
SI_Bootstrap_RaMaxWorkers.whenToChange: Rarely; only when Risk Analysis Detailed runs too long on a very large tenant.

SI_Bootstrap_RaScaleOut.label: Risk Analysis on queue workers
SI_Bootstrap_RaScaleOut.purpose: Runs the Risk Analysis Detailed reports on queue workers, several reports at the same time, instead of one after another in one job.
SI_Bootstrap_RaScaleOut.defaultText: On wherever queue scaling and the managed identity let it run; otherwise the reports run in their job.
SI_Bootstrap_RaScaleOut.effect: On: setup and every update give the install a worker job that scales from zero with the reports to run, and the Detailed run finishes sooner; the stored findings and what Log Analytics receives are the same. Off: the reports run one after another in the Risk Analysis job.
SI_Bootstrap_RaScaleOut.whenToChange: Only switch it off if support asks you to.

SI_Bootstrap_SqlServiceObjective.label: Pro database size
SI_Bootstrap_SqlServiceObjective.purpose: The size (Azure SQL service objective) of the Pro database. Allowed values: S1, S2, S3, S4, S6, S7, S9, S12. Empty = the product's rule.
SI_Bootstrap_SqlServiceObjective.defaultText: Empty: the product's rule -- Standard S3 for every install, raised to it when smaller, never lowered.
SI_Bootstrap_SqlServiceObjective.effect: Every update sets the Pro database to this size, raising or LOWERING it, by one online change (no data loss; open connections reconnect once). Never below S1. A database on Premium, vCore or in an elastic pool is left as it is. The identity database is not affected: it stays S1. A smaller size costs less but makes pages and the nightly writes slower.
SI_Bootstrap_SqlServiceObjective.whenToChange: Only when support advises it -- for example S2 for a small install whose database is mostly idle.

SI_Bootstrap_WebAppCpu.label: Web app CPU
SI_Bootstrap_WebAppCpu.purpose: The CPU of the web app's own container: 0.5 to 4, in steps of 0.25. Empty = the product's size.
SI_Bootstrap_WebAppCpu.defaultText: Empty: the product's size, 2 CPU / 4 GiB.
SI_Bootstrap_WebAppCpu.effect: Every update sets the web app to this CPU, raising or lowering it, with memory twice the CPU unless Web app memory says otherwise. The sign-in front next to it keeps its own 0.25 CPU / 0.5 GiB; together they stay within 4 CPU / 8 GiB.
SI_Bootstrap_WebAppCpu.whenToChange: Only when support advises it -- the web app normally uses a small part of 2 CPU.

SI_Bootstrap_WebAppMemory.label: Web app memory
SI_Bootstrap_WebAppMemory.purpose: The memory of the web app's own container, for example 4Gi. Empty = twice the web app's CPU.
SI_Bootstrap_WebAppMemory.defaultText: Empty: twice the CPU (4 GiB with the product's 2 CPU).
SI_Bootstrap_WebAppMemory.effect: Every update sets the web app to this memory. Azure takes memory as twice the CPU, so a memory set alone also sets the CPU to half of it.
SI_Bootstrap_WebAppMemory.whenToChange: Rarely; set Web app CPU instead.

SI_Bootstrap_ResourceGroupName.label: Container resource group
SI_Bootstrap_ResourceGroupName.purpose: The Azure resource group where container setup creates the registry, environment, identities and jobs.
SI_Bootstrap_ResourceGroupName.defaultText: rg-securityinsight (new installs get a name chosen by setup)
SI_Bootstrap_ResourceGroupName.effect: All container resources go into this group. Its presence also marks the install as container-hosted, so updates and checks treat it that way; a new name creates everything anew there.
SI_Bootstrap_ResourceGroupName.whenToChange: Set once at setup to follow your naming rules; remove it on a machine-only install.

SI_Bootstrap_ScheduleAssetTagging.label: Asset tagging schedule
SI_Bootstrap_ScheduleAssetTagging.purpose: When the asset tagging container job runs, as a cron expression in UTC.
SI_Bootstrap_ScheduleAssetTagging.defaultText: Daily at 05:50 UTC, after the collection jobs
SI_Bootstrap_ScheduleAssetTagging.effect: Sets when tagging rules are evaluated. Running before the collection jobs finish means rules see the previous day's assets.
SI_Bootstrap_ScheduleAssetTagging.whenToChange: When you move the collection schedules, to keep tagging after them.

SI_Bootstrap_ScheduleAzure.label: Azure collection schedule
SI_Bootstrap_ScheduleAzure.purpose: When the Azure profiling container job runs, as a cron expression in UTC.
SI_Bootstrap_ScheduleAzure.effect: Sets when Azure assets are collected. Reports and later jobs read the result, so keep it before risk analysis.
SI_Bootstrap_ScheduleAzure.whenToChange: To fit your own maintenance window or time zone.

SI_Bootstrap_ScheduleEndpoint.label: Endpoint collection schedule
SI_Bootstrap_ScheduleEndpoint.purpose: When the endpoint profiling container job runs, as a cron expression in UTC; also used for jobs without a schedule of their own.
SI_Bootstrap_ScheduleEndpoint.effect: Sets when endpoints are collected. Reports and later jobs read the result, so keep it before risk analysis.
SI_Bootstrap_ScheduleEndpoint.whenToChange: To fit your own maintenance window or time zone.

SI_Bootstrap_ScheduleIdentity.label: Identity collection schedule
SI_Bootstrap_ScheduleIdentity.purpose: When the identity profiling container job runs, as a cron expression in UTC.
SI_Bootstrap_ScheduleIdentity.effect: Sets when identities are collected. Reports and later jobs read the result, so keep it before risk analysis.
SI_Bootstrap_ScheduleIdentity.whenToChange: To fit your own maintenance window or time zone.

SI_Bootstrap_ScheduleRiskAnalysis.label: Summary report schedule
SI_Bootstrap_ScheduleRiskAnalysis.purpose: When the Summary risk-analysis container job runs, as a cron expression in UTC.
SI_Bootstrap_ScheduleRiskAnalysis.effect: Sets when the Summary report is built. Running it before collection finishes reports on the previous day's data.
SI_Bootstrap_ScheduleRiskAnalysis.whenToChange: When you move the collection schedules or want the report at another time.

SI_Bootstrap_ScheduleSchemaDiscovery.label: Schema discovery schedule
SI_Bootstrap_ScheduleSchemaDiscovery.purpose: When the schema discovery container job runs, as a cron expression in UTC.
SI_Bootstrap_ScheduleSchemaDiscovery.effect: Sets how often schema discovery runs. Only used when schema discovery is in the list of container jobs, which it is not by default.
SI_Bootstrap_ScheduleSchemaDiscovery.whenToChange: Only when schema discovery is deployed and you want another day or time.

SI_Bootstrap_ScheduleConfigBackup.label: Configuration backup job schedule
SI_Bootstrap_ScheduleConfigBackup.purpose: Schedule (cron, UTC) of the container job that backs up your configuration once a day.
SI_Bootstrap_ScheduleConfigBackup.defaultText: Daily at 18:00 UTC: after the working day, before the evening pipeline, never at the 23:00 update.
SI_Bootstrap_ScheduleConfigBackup.effect: Container setup gives the configuration backup job this schedule on its next run. The job is never a step of the pipeline and never runs twice at the same time.
SI_Bootstrap_ScheduleConfigBackup.whenToChange: Only if your configuration changes happen at another time of day, or the pipeline starts earlier.

SI_Bootstrap_ScheduleTrend.label: Asset trend job schedule
SI_Bootstrap_ScheduleTrend.purpose: Schedule (cron, UTC) of the container job that builds the asset trend; it should run after the Detailed report.
SI_Bootstrap_ScheduleTrend.defaultText: Daily at 09:00 UTC, moved with the start hour chosen in guided setup.
SI_Bootstrap_ScheduleTrend.effect: Container setup gives the trend job this schedule on its next run (an explicit -ScheduleTrend on the setup command still wins). Running it before the Detailed report trends the previous day's data.
SI_Bootstrap_ScheduleTrend.whenToChange: Only if the trend job must run at another time, for example after you moved the Detailed report.

SI_Bootstrap_SkipImageBuild.label: Skip container image build
SI_Bootstrap_SkipImageBuild.purpose: Lets container setup reuse the image already in the registry instead of building a new one.
SI_Bootstrap_SkipImageBuild.defaultText: Off: setup builds the image each time.
SI_Bootstrap_SkipImageBuild.effect: When on, setup is much faster but the jobs keep running the image already stored, so code changes are not picked up. If no image exists, the jobs fail to start.
SI_Bootstrap_SkipImageBuild.whenToChange: When re-running setup only to change settings and the image is already current.

SI_Bootstrap_SubscriptionId.label: Container hosting subscription
SI_Bootstrap_SubscriptionId.purpose: The Azure subscription the SecurityInsight containers are installed in, saved by setup so later updates and upgrades work in the same subscription.
SI_Bootstrap_SubscriptionId.defaultText: Falls back to SI_AzSubscriptionId, then the workspace subscription, then the signed-in Azure context.
SI_Bootstrap_SubscriptionId.effect: Container setup, updates and upgrades create and look for the containers in this subscription. A wrong value points updates at a subscription where the containers do not exist.
SI_Bootstrap_SubscriptionId.whenToChange: Setup writes it. Change only if the container hosting was moved to another subscription.

SI_Bootstrap_TaggingIdentityName.label: Asset tagging identity name
SI_Bootstrap_TaggingIdentityName.purpose: Name of the separate managed identity the asset tagging job runs as, so the collection identity stays read-only.
SI_Bootstrap_TaggingIdentityName.effect: Setup creates or reuses this identity for the tagging job. It must differ from the collection identity, or setup stops.
SI_Bootstrap_TaggingIdentityName.whenToChange: Only to follow your naming rules before first deployment.

SI_Bootstrap_TaggingScopes.label: Where Azure tags may be written
SI_Bootstrap_TaggingScopes.purpose: The Azure scopes, such as subscriptions or resource groups, where the asset tagging identity may write resource tags.
SI_Bootstrap_TaggingScopes.defaultText: The same scopes the jobs read from (the subscription by default)
SI_Bootstrap_TaggingScopes.effect: A narrower list limits where tags can ever be written; a wider list allows tagging in more places. Rights are granted only when tagging write rights are granted.
SI_Bootstrap_TaggingScopes.whenToChange: When tags should only be written in part of your estate.

SI_Bootstrap_TriggerNowAfter.label: Start jobs right after setup
SI_Bootstrap_TriggerNowAfter.purpose: Makes container setup start each job once immediately after creating or updating it.
SI_Bootstrap_TriggerNowAfter.defaultText: Off: jobs wait for their schedule.
SI_Bootstrap_TriggerNowAfter.effect: When on, every deployed job runs at once, giving results straight away but running all engines at the same time, out of their normal order, with the compute and API load that brings.
SI_Bootstrap_TriggerNowAfter.whenToChange: For a first test run after setup; leave off otherwise.

SI_Bootstrap_UseKEDA.label: Queue-driven scaling
SI_Bootstrap_UseKEDA.purpose: Runs the collection engines as queue-driven workers that scale from zero with the amount of work, instead of one scheduled job each.
SI_Bootstrap_UseKEDA.defaultText: Off: one scheduled job per engine.
SI_Bootstrap_UseKEDA.effect: When on, each collection engine gets a scheduler and a worker job that scales up to the worker maximum, speeding up large tenants. Risk analysis and asset tagging are not affected.
SI_Bootstrap_UseKEDA.whenToChange: Only for very large tenants where scheduled jobs run too long.

SI_Bootstrap_UseManagedIdentity.label: Jobs sign in with managed identity
SI_Bootstrap_UseManagedIdentity.purpose: Makes all container jobs sign in as one user-assigned managed identity, said explicitly.
SI_Bootstrap_UseManagedIdentity.defaultText: Not set: the managed identity anyway, unless the configuration carries a client secret (an existing install keeps it).
SI_Bootstrap_UseManagedIdentity.effect: On, setup creates the identity and the jobs carry no secret; the image is also pulled as that identity. Its rights are listed, and granted only when setup is told to grant them; some database access is a one-time manual step.
SI_Bootstrap_UseManagedIdentity.whenToChange: To move an existing install that signs in with a client secret to a managed identity; guided installs switch it on.

SI_Bootstrap_UseClientSecret.label: Jobs sign in with a client secret
SI_Bootstrap_UseClientSecret.purpose: Makes all container jobs sign in as the app registration (service principal) with its client secret instead of a managed identity.
SI_Bootstrap_UseClientSecret.defaultText: Off: the jobs sign in as a managed identity, unless the configuration already carries a client secret.
SI_Bootstrap_UseClientSecret.effect: On, every job carries the client secret as a job secret. Queue scaling is not available with it. A supported choice, never the default.
SI_Bootstrap_UseClientSecret.whenToChange: Only when a managed identity or a certificate cannot be used.

SI_BucketLateRetries.label: Risk Analysis late bucket retries
SI_BucketLateRetries.purpose: How many extra attempts a query slice gets at the end of a Risk Analysis report when it failed earlier because the service was throttling or unavailable.
SI_BucketLateRetries.effect: More attempts recover more slices on a busy tenant but lengthen the run (each waits up to 10 minutes). Fewer, or 0, ends sooner but the rows of a failed slice are missing from the report.
SI_BucketLateRetries.whenToChange: Most installs never should. Raise it if reports often miss rows because of throttling.

SI_BucketOverflowRetries.label: Risk Analysis too-large slice retries
SI_BucketOverflowRetries.purpose: How many times a Risk Analysis query slice that the service answers as too large is sent at the same size before it is split into smaller slices. 1 splits it on the first too-large answer.
SI_BucketOverflowRetries.effect: Higher sends the same too-large request again, after a 30 s and then a 60 s pause, before splitting it. The same request at the same size fails the same way, so this only adds time. Throttling, timeouts and service errors are retried separately (Risk Analysis transient error retries).

SI_RA_PartsInParallel_Max.label: Risk Analysis parts asked at a time (most)
SI_RA_PartsInParallel_Max.purpose: A large Risk Analysis report is asked from Microsoft Defender in parts. While one part is processed (risk scores, the database), the next parts are already asked, so Defender and SecurityInsight work at the same time. This is the most parts asked at a time.
SI_RA_PartsInParallel_Max.effect: The number adapts by itself: each report starts at 2, asks more while Defender answers quickly, and halves at once when Defender asks to slow down (it then waits as long as Defender says). A higher maximum lets a large report finish sooner when Defender keeps up; 1 asks one part at a time. The parts are processed in their order either way: the stored findings are the same.
SI_RA_PartsInParallel_Max.whenToChange: Most installs never should. Set 1 only if support asks you to; lower it if other tools in the tenant share Defender's advanced hunting limits.

SI_BucketTransientRetries.label: Risk Analysis transient error retries
SI_BucketTransientRetries.purpose: How many times a Risk Analysis query slice is retried, after signing in again, when it fails with a temporary error such as an expired token or a gateway timeout.
SI_BucketTransientRetries.effect: More attempts make long reports more robust against brief outages, at the cost of a longer run when the service stays unavailable. Fewer gives up on a slice sooner.
SI_BucketTransientRetries.whenToChange: Most installs never should. Raise it on tenants with frequent temporary service errors.

SI_CmdbCsvPath.label: CMDB export file location
SI_CmdbCsvPath.purpose: Points the CMDB provider at your CMDB export CSV when it is stored outside the SecurityInsight folder, for example on a file share.
SI_CmdbCsvPath.defaultText: The CMDB.csv in the CMDB provider folder is used
SI_CmdbCsvPath.effect: The CMDB cache is loaded from this file instead of the provider folder. A wrong path means no CMDB data, so CMDB columns stay empty. In SecurityInsight Pro the file is read once, by setup, to move it into the CMDB in the Pro database; runs then read the Pro CMDB.
SI_CmdbCsvPath.whenToChange: Only when your CMDB export lives on a share or other folder; leave empty when you drop CMDB.csv in the provider folder.

SI_CmdbRefreshIntervalHours.label: CMDB cache refresh interval
SI_CmdbRefreshIntervalHours.purpose: How long the cached CMDB data is reused before it is reloaded from the CSV at the start of a profiling run.
SI_CmdbRefreshIntervalHours.effect: Lower values pick up CMDB changes sooner but re-read the CSV more often; higher values save work but CMDB changes appear later. A full run always refreshes.
SI_CmdbRefreshIntervalHours.whenToChange: Rarely. Lower it if your CMDB export changes several times a day.

SI_CollectDefenderRecommendations.label: Defender for Cloud recommendations
SI_CollectDefenderRecommendations.purpose: Whether the Azure engine also collects every unhealthy Defender for Cloud recommendation into its own table for the Risk Analysis reports.
SI_CollectDefenderRecommendations.defaultText: On: recommendations are collected on every Azure run
SI_CollectDefenderRecommendations.effect: Setting it to false skips the recommendations step: the Azure run is a little shorter and ingests less data, but reports have no Defender for Cloud recommendation findings.
SI_CollectDefenderRecommendations.whenToChange: Turn off only if you do not use Defender for Cloud or do not want these findings.

SI_CustomConfigPath.label: Custom configuration file path
SI_CustomConfigPath.purpose: Points the asset-profiling engine at a custom configuration file kept outside the standard config folder.
SI_CustomConfigPath.defaultText: The standard custom configuration file in the config folder
SI_CustomConfigPath.effect: When set, the profiling engine loads this file at start, even when started by a launcher. A wrong path means your settings are not applied.
SI_CustomConfigPath.whenToChange: Very rarely; only if your custom configuration file lives outside the config folder.

SI_CVE_MaxPublishedAgeDays.label: CVE maximum age
SI_CVE_MaxPublishedAgeDays.purpose: Limits the vulnerability (CVE) reports to vulnerabilities published within the last number of days.
SI_CVE_MaxPublishedAgeDays.defaultText: Off: CVEs of every age are reported
SI_CVE_MaxPublishedAgeDays.effect: Any value above 0 removes older CVEs from the reports, making them shorter and faster, but old unpatched vulnerabilities are no longer shown.
SI_CVE_MaxPublishedAgeDays.whenToChange: Only if you deliberately want to focus on recently published vulnerabilities.

SI_CVE_MinCvssScore.label: CVE minimum CVSS score
SI_CVE_MinCvssScore.purpose: Limits the vulnerability (CVE) reports to vulnerabilities at or above this CVSS score (0 to 10).
SI_CVE_MinCvssScore.defaultText: Off: CVEs of every score are reported
SI_CVE_MinCvssScore.effect: A value above 0 removes lower-scored CVEs from the reports, making them shorter and faster but hiding those findings completely.
SI_CVE_MinCvssScore.whenToChange: Only if you want to focus on high-impact vulnerabilities, for example 7.0.

SI_CVE_MinSeverity.label: CVE minimum severity
SI_CVE_MinSeverity.purpose: Limits the vulnerability (CVE) reports to this severity and above: Critical, High or Medium.
SI_CVE_MinSeverity.defaultText: Off: CVEs of every severity are reported
SI_CVE_MinSeverity.effect: Setting it removes all less severe CVEs from the reports. Shorter, faster reports, but those findings are not shown anywhere in the report. An unknown value is ignored.
SI_CVE_MinSeverity.whenToChange: Only if you want the reports to focus on the most severe vulnerabilities.

SI_CVE_RequireExploit.label: Only CVEs with known exploits
SI_CVE_RequireExploit.purpose: Limits the vulnerability (CVE) reports to vulnerabilities for which an exploit is known to exist.
SI_CVE_RequireExploit.defaultText: Off: CVEs are reported whether or not an exploit is known
SI_CVE_RequireExploit.effect: When on, every CVE without a known exploit is removed from the reports. Much shorter reports, but unexploited vulnerabilities are hidden.
SI_CVE_RequireExploit.whenToChange: Only if you want to prioritise vulnerabilities that are actively exploitable.

SI_DceIngestionUri.label: Ingestion endpoint address
SI_DceIngestionUri.purpose: The ingestion address of the data collection endpoint that Risk Analysis sends results to.
SI_DceIngestionUri.defaultText: Not set: looked up from the endpoint name
SI_DceIngestionUri.effect: Used by Risk Analysis unless SI_RiskAnalysis_DceIngestionUri is set. A wrong address makes Risk Analysis ingestion fail; the collection engines do not read it.
SI_DceIngestionUri.whenToChange: Rarely; only if automatic lookup of the endpoint cannot work in your environment.

SI_DceName.label: Data collection endpoint name
SI_DceName.purpose: Name of the data collection endpoint all engines send their data to Log Analytics through.
SI_DceName.defaultText: Not set: endpoint pinning is skipped; setup may create dce-si-securityinsight
SI_DceName.effect: Tells the engines which endpoint to use. A wrong name stops ingestion or, during setup, creates a new endpoint. Run health rows are not sent without it.
SI_DceName.whenToChange: Set at install to the endpoint your setup created; change only if you rename or move it.

SI_DceResourceGroup.label: Data collection endpoint resource group
SI_DceResourceGroup.purpose: The resource group that holds the data collection endpoint used to send data to Log Analytics.
SI_DceResourceGroup.defaultText: Same resource group as the data collection rules
SI_DceResourceGroup.effect: Tells the engines where to find the endpoint. A wrong value makes runs refuse to post when several endpoints share the name, or print misleading ingestion lines.
SI_DceResourceGroup.whenToChange: Only when you have deliberately placed the endpoint in a different resource group than the rules.

SI_DcrMergeDiagnostic.label: Rule column diagnostic
SI_DcrMergeDiagnostic.purpose: Logs the difference between a data collection rule's columns and the data being sent, on every ingestion call.
SI_DcrMergeDiagnostic.effect: On, each ingestion call logs added, removed and changed columns. Makes logs longer and runs slightly slower; never stops ingestion.
SI_DcrMergeDiagnostic.whenToChange: Turn on briefly when investigating warnings about dropped columns.

SI_DcrNamePattern.label: Rule name pattern
SI_DcrNamePattern.purpose: The pattern used to name each collection engine's data collection rule, where {0} is replaced by the engine name.
SI_DcrNamePattern.effect: Changing it makes engines create and use differently named rules; existing rules are left behind and new ones are made.
SI_DcrNamePattern.whenToChange: Only if you maintain a parallel naming scheme; most installs never should.

SI_DcrResourceGroup.label: Data collection rules resource group
SI_DcrResourceGroup.purpose: Resource group holding the data collection rules (and, by default, the endpoint) used to send data to Log Analytics.
SI_DcrResourceGroup.defaultText: Not set: Risk Analysis uses DcrResourceGroup; setup uses rg-securityinsight
SI_DcrResourceGroup.effect: Tells engines where to find and create rules. A wrong group creates duplicate rules or refuses to post. Run health rows are not sent without it.
SI_DcrResourceGroup.whenToChange: Set at install; change only if you move the rules.

SI_DefenderWorkspaceResourceId.label: Defender data workspace
SI_DefenderWorkspaceResourceId.purpose: Full resource id of a separate Log Analytics workspace holding Defender data, when it is not the SecurityInsight workspace.
SI_DefenderWorkspaceResourceId.defaultText: Not set: Defender data is read from the SecurityInsight workspace
SI_DefenderWorkspaceResourceId.effect: Identity discovery and Risk Analysis queries read Defender tables from this workspace. A wrong value makes those queries return nothing or fail.
SI_DefenderWorkspaceResourceId.whenToChange: Only when your Defender data is in a different workspace than SecurityInsight's own.

SI_DisableAI.label: Turn off AI classification (all engines)
SI_DisableAI.purpose: A master switch that turns off AI asset classification for every collection engine, whatever else is switched on.
SI_DisableAI.defaultText: Off: AI runs where it has been switched on.
SI_DisableAI.effect: When on, asset profiling, signal maps and schema proposals use rules only and send nothing to Azure OpenAI. It does not stop the role tiering classifier or the risk-analysis AI summary, which have their own switches.
SI_DisableAI.whenToChange: When AI must not be used, for example for a policy or cost reason.

SI_DisableAI_endpoint.label: Turn off AI for the endpoint engine
SI_DisableAI_endpoint.purpose: Switches off AI classification for the endpoint engine only, even when AI is on for all engines.
SI_DisableAI_endpoint.defaultText: Off: the endpoint engine follows the general AI switches.
SI_DisableAI_endpoint.effect: Devices are classified by rules only; any device without a rule-based tier gets the default tier. Removes AI cost for endpoints. Wins over every AI turn-on switch.
SI_DisableAI_endpoint.whenToChange: When you use AI elsewhere but want rule-only tiering for devices.
SI_DisableAI_endpoint.hint: Wins over the switches above, for endpoints only.

SI_DisableEndpointAzureCorrelation.label: Azure VM to device tier linking off
SI_DisableEndpointAzureCorrelation.purpose: Stops the Azure engine from giving an Azure VM or Arc machine the same tier as its matching Defender device.
SI_DisableEndpointAzureCorrelation.defaultText: Off: an Azure VM takes the tier of the matching endpoint device.
SI_DisableEndpointAzureCorrelation.effect: When on, Azure VMs and Arc machines keep their own Azure-side tier and lose the link to their endpoint record, so the same machine can show different tiers in the two views.
SI_DisableEndpointAzureCorrelation.whenToChange: Only while diagnosing a problem with this linking.

SI_DisableTranscript.label: Turn off run logs
SI_DisableTranscript.purpose: Stops the launchers from writing a run log (transcript) to disk and uploading it to storage.
SI_DisableTranscript.defaultText: Off: every run writes and keeps a run log.
SI_DisableTranscript.effect: No run log is kept, so failed runs cannot be investigated afterwards. Collection and reports are unaffected.
SI_DisableTranscript.whenToChange: Only in lab or test pipelines where logs are not wanted.

SI_DumpAIPayload.label: Save AI requests to disk
SI_DumpAIPayload.purpose: A troubleshooting switch that saves every AI classification request to a file in the machine's temp folder.
SI_DumpAIPayload.effect: When on, each AI call writes one file holding the prompt and the asset data sent, so prompts can be inspected. This adds disk writes and leaves asset details on disk.
SI_DumpAIPayload.whenToChange: Only while diagnosing AI results; switch it off again afterwards.

SI_EgIdentityBucketThreshold.label: Identity exposure graph split size
SI_EgIdentityBucketThreshold.purpose: Above this many identities of one kind, the identity engine reads the exposure graph in several smaller queries instead of one.
SI_EgIdentityBucketThreshold.effect: A lower value splits reads sooner: more queries, but each stays within response limits. A higher value risks a single oversized query failing in very large tenants.
SI_EgIdentityBucketThreshold.whenToChange: Only if exposure graph reads for identities fail or time out.

SI_EnableAI.label: AI integration
SI_EnableAI.purpose: ONE switch for AI: on = AI for every engine that has an AI step (the endpoint and Azure engines classify the assets their rules cannot place). It needs the Azure OpenAI endpoint, deployment and key.
SI_EnableAI.defaultText: Off: assets are classified by rules only.
SI_EnableAI.effect: When on, and Azure OpenAI is configured, assets that rules cannot place are sent to Azure OpenAI for a tier and service type. This adds AI cost and run time. The identity and public IP engines never use AI.
SI_EnableAI.whenToChange: When you want AI help classifying assets -- in Get Started > AI integration, with the endpoint, deployment and key.
SI_EnableAI.hint: On = on for all engines. The per-engine switches (Advanced) only matter to turn ONE engine on or off against this switch.

SI_EnableAI_azure.label: AI for the Azure engine
SI_EnableAI_azure.purpose: An override for ONE engine: turns on Azure OpenAI classification and application grouping for the Azure engine only, while AI integration is off. With AI integration on it changes nothing.
SI_EnableAI_azure.defaultText: Off, unless AI is turned on for all engines.
SI_EnableAI_azure.effect: Resources without a rule-based tier are classified by AI, and resource groups are named as applications. Adds AI cost and run time. Needs the Azure OpenAI settings; without them AI stays off. A disable switch wins.
SI_EnableAI_azure.whenToChange: Only to use AI in the Azure engine alone; normally use AI integration (on = on for all engines).

SI_EnableAI_endpoint.label: AI for the endpoint engine
SI_EnableAI_endpoint.purpose: An override for ONE engine: turns on Azure OpenAI classification for the endpoint engine only, while AI integration is off. With AI integration on it changes nothing.
SI_EnableAI_endpoint.defaultText: Off, unless AI is turned on for all engines.
SI_EnableAI_endpoint.effect: Devices without a rule-based tier are classified by AI instead of getting the default tier. Adds AI cost and run time. Needs the Azure OpenAI settings; SI_DisableAI_endpoint wins over it.
SI_EnableAI_endpoint.whenToChange: Only to use AI in the endpoint engine alone; normally use AI integration (on = on for all engines).

SI_EnableAI_identity.label: AI for the identity engine
SI_EnableAI_identity.purpose: Per-engine AI switch for the identity engine.
SI_EnableAI_identity.defaultText: Off; identity classification never uses AI.
SI_EnableAI_identity.effect: No effect today: identity tiers always come from the built-in role and permission catalog, whatever this is set to.
SI_EnableAI_identity.whenToChange: Never at present; it is kept for consistency with the other engines.

SI_EnableCmdbProvider.label: CMDB enrichment on
SI_EnableCmdbProvider.purpose: Turns on enrichment of assets with data from your CMDB export (CMDB id, name, criticality, data sensitivity).
SI_EnableCmdbProvider.defaultText: Off: CMDB data is not used
SI_EnableCmdbProvider.effect: When on and a CMDB.csv is present, profiling runs refresh the CMDB cache and stamp CMDB fields onto matched assets; CMDB ids in custom rules take effect. When off, they are ignored. In SecurityInsight Pro the services come from the CMDB in the Pro database (the CMDB page) instead of a file; a v2.2 CMDB.csv is moved there once by setup, and a CMDB.csv left on disk is not read (the run warns when the Pro CMDB is empty and a CSV was never moved).
SI_EnableCmdbProvider.whenToChange: Turn on when you have a CMDB export (or, in Pro, services on the CMDB page) you want reflected in reports.

SI_EnableServiceNowCmdb.label: ServiceNow CMDB source
SI_EnableServiceNowCmdb.purpose: Marks the live ServiceNow CMDB as the asset-inventory (CMDB) source used to enrich profiled assets.
SI_EnableServiceNowCmdb.defaultText: Off: the generic CMDB file is used when one is provided
SI_EnableServiceNowCmdb.effect: The ServiceNow CMDB source is not available in this version: turning this on is refused with an error and the CMDB columns stay empty. It also does not fall back to the CMDB file.
SI_EnableServiceNowCmdb.whenToChange: Leave off. Not usable until the ServiceNow CMDB connector is released.

SI_EnableSignInEnrich.label: Identity sign-in details
SI_EnableSignInEnrich.purpose: Lets the identity engine add sign-in statistics per user, such as sign-in counts, apps, IP addresses and countries.
SI_EnableSignInEnrich.effect: Turning it off skips the sign-in log queries, so runs are faster and cheaper, but sign-in counts, apps and locations stay empty. Last sign-in date still comes from Entra.
SI_EnableSignInEnrich.whenToChange: Turn off if sign-in queries are too slow or costly in your tenant.

SI_Endpoint_DcrName.label: Endpoint data collection rule name
SI_Endpoint_DcrName.purpose: The name of the data collection rule the endpoint engine sends its asset rows through to Log Analytics.
SI_Endpoint_DcrName.defaultText: The standard name, dcr-si-endpoint-profile (from the naming pattern)
SI_Endpoint_DcrName.effect: Rows are sent through the named rule. A name that does not match an existing or creatable rule makes the endpoint ingest fail.
SI_Endpoint_DcrName.whenToChange: Only if you renamed the rule or must avoid a name clash with another install.

SI_Endpoint_TableName.label: Endpoint table name
SI_Endpoint_TableName.purpose: The Log Analytics table the endpoint engine writes its asset rows to.
SI_Endpoint_TableName.effect: Rows go to the named table instead. Reports, queries and dashboards that read the standard table then no longer see new endpoint data.
SI_Endpoint_TableName.whenToChange: Only if you renamed the destination table.

SI_ExcelMaxDataRows.label: Excel report row limit
SI_ExcelMaxDataRows.purpose: The most rows written to one worksheet of an Excel report; above it, the highest-risk rows are kept and the rest are left out of the workbook.
SI_ExcelMaxDataRows.effect: A lower value gives smaller, quicker workbooks but more rows are left out of the Excel file. Nothing is lost from the run: the JSON file and Log Analytics still hold every row.
SI_ExcelMaxDataRows.whenToChange: Most installs never should. Lower it if workbooks are too large to open or mail.

SI_RA_ExcelExport_Summary.label: Excel workbook of the summary report
SI_RA_ExcelExport_Summary.purpose: Whether a Risk Analysis summary run writes its results to an Excel workbook (attached to the summary mail when it fits).
SI_RA_ExcelExport_Summary.effect: On: the summary run writes its workbook. Off: no workbook is written; the mail says the results are in the web app. The results themselves are the same either way: every row is in the web app and in Log Analytics.
SI_RA_ExcelExport_Summary.whenToChange: Switch it off when nobody uses the summary workbook.

SI_RA_ExcelExport_Detailed.label: Excel workbook of the detailed report
SI_RA_ExcelExport_Detailed.purpose: Whether a Risk Analysis detailed run writes its results to an Excel workbook. The detailed results can hold millions of rows; they are in the web app.
SI_RA_ExcelExport_Detailed.effect: On: the detailed run writes its workbook, as long as the results are not larger than a workbook can hold here -- above that no workbook is written and the Settings page shows the switch greyed out. Off: no workbook is written; the mail says the results are in the web app. Every row is in the web app and in Log Analytics either way.
SI_RA_ExcelExport_Detailed.whenToChange: Switch it on only when someone needs the detailed results as a file.

SI_FingerprintCache_Enabled.label: Asset fingerprint cache
SI_FingerprintCache_Enabled.purpose: Remembers each asset between runs so incremental runs can skip assets that are not yet due for re-processing.
SI_FingerprintCache_Enabled.defaultText: Off: every asset is processed on every run
SI_FingerprintCache_Enabled.effect: On can shorten incremental runs, but adds storage writes, and it has no effect on full runs. Off is safe: every row is still produced.
SI_FingerprintCache_Enabled.whenToChange: Only on installs that run incremental (not full) runs and want shorter run times.

SI_ForceFullRun.label: Full run for all profilers
SI_ForceFullRun.purpose: Makes every asset-profiling engine process all assets on the next run, ignoring the per-asset skip schedule and cached CMDB data.
SI_ForceFullRun.effect: Every asset is re-collected and re-classified, so runs take longer and use more AI calls when AI is on. A per-engine full-run setting that is on wins; a job's own SI_FORCE_FULL_RUN wins over both. Applies the same way on a VM and in container jobs.
SI_ForceFullRun.whenToChange: After changing rules or fixing bad cached data, when you want every asset refreshed at once.

SI_ForceFullRun_Azure.label: Azure full re-run
SI_ForceFullRun_Azure.purpose: Makes the Azure engine reprocess every resource instead of skipping ones that have not changed since the last run.
SI_ForceFullRun_Azure.effect: Every resource is reclassified, so the run takes longer and, with AI on, costs more. Overrides the all-engine full re-run switch for this engine.
SI_ForceFullRun_Azure.whenToChange: Once after changing rules or the schema; then switch it back off.

SI_ForceFullRun_Endpoint.label: Endpoint full re-run
SI_ForceFullRun_Endpoint.purpose: Makes the endpoint engine reprocess every device instead of skipping ones that have not changed since the last run.
SI_ForceFullRun_Endpoint.effect: Every device is reclassified, so the run takes longer and, with AI on, costs more. Overrides the all-engine full re-run switch for this engine.
SI_ForceFullRun_Endpoint.whenToChange: Once after changing rules or the schema; then switch it back off.

SI_ForceFullRun_Identity.label: Identity full re-run
SI_ForceFullRun_Identity.purpose: Makes the identity engine reprocess every identity instead of skipping ones that have not changed since the last run.
SI_ForceFullRun_Identity.effect: Every identity is reprocessed, so the run takes longer. Overrides the all-engine full re-run switch for this engine.
SI_ForceFullRun_Identity.whenToChange: Once after changing rules or the schema; then switch it back off.

SI_ForceFullRun_PublicIp.label: Public IP force full run
SI_ForceFullRun_PublicIp.purpose: Makes the public IP engine process every address, ignoring the per-tier re-check cadence, for this engine only.
SI_ForceFullRun_PublicIp.defaultText: Off; falls back to SI_ForceFullRun, which is also off.
SI_ForceFullRun_PublicIp.effect: On, every address is re-processed on every run. It only changes anything when the fingerprint cache (SI_FingerprintCache_Enabled) is on; without it every address is processed anyway. More run time when it matters.
SI_ForceFullRun_PublicIp.whenToChange: Once after changing tier rules or the schema, then turn it off again.

SI_Graph_AppId.label: App id (older Graph name)
SI_Graph_AppId.purpose: Older name for the service principal's application id; still read when SI_SPN_AppId is not set.
SI_Graph_AppId.effect: Only matters when SI_SPN_AppId is empty; then this app id is used for Microsoft Graph sign-in and setup copies it forward.
SI_Graph_AppId.whenToChange: Never on new installs; use SI_SPN_AppId instead.

SI_Graph_Secret.label: Client secret (older Graph name)
SI_Graph_Secret.purpose: Older name for the service principal's client secret; used only when SI_SPN_Secret is not set.
SI_Graph_Secret.effect: Only matters when SI_SPN_Secret is empty; then this secret is used for Microsoft Graph sign-in.
SI_Graph_Secret.whenToChange: Never on new installs; use SI_SPN_Secret, a certificate or managed identity.

SI_Graph_TenantId.label: Tenant id (older Graph name)
SI_Graph_TenantId.purpose: Older name for the Entra tenant id the service principal signs in to; used only when SI_SPN_TenantId is not set.
SI_Graph_TenantId.effect: Only matters when SI_SPN_TenantId is empty; then this tenant is used for Microsoft Graph sign-in.
SI_Graph_TenantId.whenToChange: Never on new installs; use SI_SPN_TenantId instead.

SI_HasExposureGraphInLA.label: Exposure graph available in workspace
SI_HasExposureGraphInLA.purpose: Tells Risk Analysis that Defender exposure graph tables are mirrored into Log Analytics, so reports needing them can run.
SI_HasExposureGraphInLA.defaultText: Off: reports needing exposure graph tables are skipped
SI_HasExposureGraphInLA.effect: On, Risk Analysis runs the reports that query exposure graph tables in the workspace. Turning it on without the tables present makes those reports fail.
SI_HasExposureGraphInLA.whenToChange: Turn on after enabling exposure graph table mirroring to Log Analytics.

SI_Identity_DcrName.label: Identity data collection rule name
SI_Identity_DcrName.purpose: The name of the data collection rule the identity engine sends its rows through to Log Analytics.
SI_Identity_DcrName.defaultText: The standard name, dcr-si-identity-profile (from the naming pattern)
SI_Identity_DcrName.effect: Rows are sent through the named rule. A name that does not match an existing or creatable rule makes the identity ingest fail.
SI_Identity_DcrName.whenToChange: Only if you renamed the rule or must avoid a name clash with another install.

SI_Identity_TableName.label: Identity table name
SI_Identity_TableName.purpose: The Log Analytics table the identity engine writes its rows to.
SI_Identity_TableName.effect: Rows go to the named table instead. Reports, queries and dashboards that read the standard table then no longer see new identity data.
SI_Identity_TableName.whenToChange: Only if you renamed the destination table.

SI_IncludeFirstPartySpns.label: Include Microsoft service principals
SI_IncludeFirstPartySpns.purpose: Whether the identity engine includes Microsoft's own built-in service principals in its inventory.
SI_IncludeFirstPartySpns.defaultText: On: Microsoft service principals are included.
SI_IncludeFirstPartySpns.effect: Turning it off drops the hundreds of Microsoft-published service principals, giving a smaller, less noisy inventory, but privileged ones among them are no longer reported.
SI_IncludeFirstPartySpns.whenToChange: Turn off if Microsoft service principals add noise you do not want in reports.

SI_IncludeInactive_Endpoint.label: Include inactive endpoints
SI_IncludeInactive_Endpoint.purpose: Turns off the filter that leaves out stale or offboarded devices, so every known device is published.
SI_IncludeInactive_Endpoint.defaultText: Off: devices not seen by any source within the stale-days window are left out
SI_IncludeInactive_Endpoint.effect: On publishes every device, including stale registrations and offboarded machines: more rows, more ingested data, and more noise in reports. Useful when cleaning up stale devices.
SI_IncludeInactive_Endpoint.whenToChange: When you want to find and clean up stale or ghost devices.

SI_IncludeInactive_Identity.label: Include inactive identities
SI_IncludeInactive_Identity.purpose: Turns off the one identity filter left: Microsoft-published applications this tenant granted nothing. Every user (disabled accounts and guests too) and every service principal and managed identity the tenant owns is always published.
SI_IncludeInactive_Identity.defaultText: Off: only Microsoft apps this tenant granted nothing are left out
SI_IncludeInactive_Identity.effect: On publishes the Microsoft-published applications too (hundreds in most tenants): more rows, more ingested data, and more noise in reports.
SI_IncludeInactive_Identity.whenToChange: When you need a complete identity inventory, for example for an audit.

SI_KeyVaultName.label: Key Vault name
SI_KeyVaultName.purpose: The one Key Vault SecurityInsight reads its secrets from: the sign-in secret, integration credentials and a Pro licence.
SI_KeyVaultName.defaultText: Falls back to SpnKeyVaultName; with neither set, secret reads stop with an error
SI_KeyVaultName.effect: All secrets are read from the named vault. A wrong name means sign-in secrets, keys and the licence cannot be read and runs fail or run as Community.
SI_KeyVaultName.whenToChange: Setup writes it. Change only if you move secrets to another Key Vault.

SI_KvMiClientId.label: Key Vault managed identity (older name)
SI_KvMiClientId.purpose: The client id of a user-assigned managed identity used to read Key Vault when no Azure sign-in exists yet. Older name for SI_ManagedIdentityClientId.
SI_KvMiClientId.defaultText: Uses SI_ManagedIdentityClientId; otherwise the machine's own system managed identity
SI_KvMiClientId.effect: Key Vault reads sign in as this user-assigned identity. It is ignored when SI_ManagedIdentityClientId is set, or when an Azure sign-in already exists.
SI_KvMiClientId.whenToChange: Only on older configurations that use a user-assigned identity; new installs use SI_ManagedIdentityClientId.

SI_LAQueryMaxRetries.label: Log Analytics query retries
SI_LAQueryMaxRetries.purpose: How many attempts the asset engines make for a Log Analytics query that fails with a temporary error.
SI_LAQueryMaxRetries.effect: More attempts ride out brief workspace errors at the cost of a slightly longer run; fewer (minimum 1) fails faster and may drop the affected data from the run.
SI_LAQueryMaxRetries.whenToChange: Most installs never should. Raise it if runs log intermittent Log Analytics query failures.

SI_LaExport.label: Copy records to Log Analytics
SI_LaExport.purpose: Optionally copies the provider records (every object a collection reads, mapped to SI fields) to Log Analytics, for Azure Monitor or your own workbooks.
SI_LaExport.defaultText: off: the records are kept only in the database
SI_LaExport.effect: 'records' also posts every record to SI_Record_CL (and, for the providers raw data is on for, the whole object to SI_RecordRaw_CL) on every collection run. This costs Log Analytics ingestion for every record, every run. It is a one-way copy: correlation, the CI build and the data sync read the records from the database only and never read this copy back. The CIs (SI_CI_CL) are in Log Analytics in every install, because Risk Analysis reads them there, so they need no setting; the findings per CI are copied there only when Copy findings per CI to Log Analytics (SI_Finding_CL) is on.
SI_LaExport.whenToChange: Only when you build your own Azure Monitor alerts or workbooks on the raw provider records; leave off otherwise.
SI_LaExport.hint: Off = records in the database only. Records = also a copy in Log Analytics (costs ingestion).

valueLabels.off: Off: records in the database only
valueLabels.records: Records: also copy them to Log Analytics

SI_RA_Findings.label: Copy findings per CI to Log Analytics (SI_Finding_CL)
SI_RA_Findings.purpose: Optional. After each Risk Analysis Detailed run, copies the de-duplicated findings (one row per CI and finding) into your Log Analytics workspace, for your own workbooks, Sentinel or KQL. SecurityInsight itself does not need it: its pages read the findings from its database. On a large estate the copy can take hours and adds Log Analytics ingestion cost. Off by default.
SI_RA_Findings.defaultText: Off: the findings per CI are kept in the database only
SI_RA_Findings.effect: On: at the end of every Risk Analysis Detailed run its findings per CI are also posted to SI_Finding_CL, and the run ends when the copy has ended. On a large estate that is hours, and it costs ingestion for every finding, every run. The data sync reads that copy back only when it is the newest and whole; otherwise it makes the findings per CI from the database, as it does with the copy off. Off: nothing is copied. This is not the Risk Analysis report rows (SI_RiskAnalysis_Detailed_CL): they are their own optional output, Copy Risk Analysis report rows to Log Analytics, off by default.
SI_RA_Findings.whenToChange: Only when your own workbooks, Sentinel rules or KQL queries read SI_Finding_CL; leave off otherwise.
SI_RA_Findings.hint: Off = the findings per CI stay in the database. On = also a copy in Log Analytics (can take hours, costs ingestion).

SI_LicenseRequest_BaseUrl.label: Licence service address
SI_LicenseRequest_BaseUrl.purpose: The address of the licence service that a manual licence request contacts. Must be an https address.
SI_LicenseRequest_BaseUrl.effect: Licence requests go to this address instead. A wrong address means licences cannot be requested or renewed by hand. The updater job uses its own environment setting.
SI_LicenseRequest_BaseUrl.whenToChange: Practically never; only if the licence service tells you to use another address.

SI_LicenseRequest_ContactEmail.label: Licence contact e-mail
SI_LicenseRequest_ContactEmail.purpose: The email address the licence provider may use to contact you about a manual licence request.
SI_LicenseRequest_ContactEmail.defaultText: Not set: no contact address is sent with the request
SI_LicenseRequest_ContactEmail.effect: When set, the address is sent with the licence request so the provider can reach you about it. It changes nothing else.
SI_LicenseRequest_ContactEmail.whenToChange: Set it if you want to be contacted about your licence requests.

SI_LicenseRequest_Auto.label: Automatic licence request
SI_LicenseRequest_Auto.purpose: Whether SecurityInsight Pro asks Invardia for its licence by itself. Every night the updater job checks the licence; when there is none, it ends within 30 days, or it is in its grace period, the job asks Invardia for one, checks the licence it gets and installs it. The result is written to the audit trail and mailed to you. While the licence is valid nothing is asked.
SI_LicenseRequest_Auto.effect: Off: Invardia is never asked for a licence by the updater job, and the Settings page and the job's log say that the automatic licence request is off. A licence then has to be requested by hand (setup\Request-SILicense.ps1) or installed by hand before the current one ends.
SI_LicenseRequest_Auto.whenToChange: Turn it off only if your organisation does not allow the installation to contact Invardia by itself; then renew the licence by hand.

SI_InternetExposedRanges.label: Internet-exposed network ranges
SI_InternetExposedRanges.purpose: Address ranges that are reachable from the internet by design, such as a DMZ or an online landing zone. An asset with an address in them counts as internet exposed in the risk score.
SI_InternetExposedRanges.defaultText: None: only what Defender, Exposure Graph, Azure and Shodan report counts as exposure.
SI_InternetExposedRanges.effect: Assets with an address in these ranges get the Internet exposed risk factor, which adds its impact (default 4) to the asset side of their findings' risk score.
SI_InternetExposedRanges.whenToChange: When you have network segments that face the internet that the providers do not flag, for example a DMZ behind a firewall NAT.

SI_InvardiaUpdate_Enabled.label: Pro updates from Invardia
SI_InvardiaUpdate_Enabled.purpose: Whether SecurityInsight Pro takes its updates from Invardia by itself. Every night the updater job asks Invardia for the release approved for this installation's ring, checks its signature and contents, and applies it; if anything fails the previous version is restored. A release that needs a manual step first, or a newer version than this installation can move to directly, is held and shown on this page.
SI_InvardiaUpdate_Enabled.effect: Off: the updater job never asks Invardia for updates and applies nothing; the Settings page and the job's log say that Pro updates from Invardia are off. The installation stays on its current version until you turn it on again.
SI_InvardiaUpdate_Enabled.whenToChange: Turn it off only to hold an installation on its current version for a while, for example during an audit or a change freeze; turn it on again afterwards.

SI_Update_RenameDisplayNames.label: Rename to the agreed names
SI_Update_RenameDisplayNames.purpose: Whether the update gives this installation's directory objects the names a new installation gets: the engine's application "SecurityInsight Engine", the web app's sign-in application "SecurityInsight" and the SQL admin group shown as "SecurityInsight SQL admins". Only SecurityInsight's earlier names are renamed; a name you chose is kept. Each object is renamed once, read back, and put back if the rename does not take. Azure resources keep their names.
SI_Update_RenameDisplayNames.effect: Off: the update renames nothing and only says, one line each, what it would rename. Where the updater's identity may not rename an application or the SQL admin group, the update says so in one line and an administrator renames with setup\Set-SIDisplayNames.ps1.
SI_Update_RenameDisplayNames.whenToChange: Turn it off only when your own processes still look for SecurityInsight's applications or the SQL admin group by their earlier names; turn it on again once they use the new names.

SI_InvardiaUpdate_HoldMicrosoftContent.label: Hold template packs
SI_InvardiaUpdate_HoldMicrosoftContent.purpose: Whether new template packs wait for you. Between releases SecurityInsight ships template packs: reports and rules for data that Microsoft added to Defender and the Exposure Graph, such as a new attack-path type, and updates to the templates SecurityInsight ships. Normally the updater job installs them by itself once your installation runs the SecurityInsight version a pack needs; your own changes are never overwritten by a pack.
SI_InvardiaUpdate_HoldMicrosoftContent.defaultText: Off: template packs are installed automatically
SI_InvardiaUpdate_HoldMicrosoftContent.effect: On: a template pack is kept on the Template releases page, with what it changes, until you select Install there. Off: it is installed automatically the next time the updater job runs. Your own changes to templates are never touched either way, and an installed pack can be rolled back on Template releases.
SI_InvardiaUpdate_HoldMicrosoftContent.whenToChange: Turn it on when every change to what SecurityInsight reports must be reviewed first, for example during a change freeze or an audit.

SI_UpdateRing.label: Update ring
SI_UpdateRing.purpose: The update ring this installation belongs to: 0 = development, 1 = internal test, 2 = early release, 3 = broad. It is shown in the header (UPDATE RING) and recorded with the installation, so the ring is known from the day it is installed -- also before the updater job has run.
SI_UpdateRing.defaultText: Not set: the ring the installation recorded at install time (from its resource-group name), until the updater records the ring it updates by
SI_UpdateRing.effect: The header shows this ring and setup records it as the installation's ring. Once the updater job has run, the header shows the ring the updater actually updated by -- which ring an installation receives releases on is decided by the update service, not by this setting.
SI_UpdateRing.whenToChange: Once, when the installation's ring is not shown, or was recorded wrongly at install time.

SI_LicenseRequest_Edition.label: Licence request edition
SI_LicenseRequest_Edition.purpose: The edition you ask for when requesting a licence by hand. The licence provider decides what is granted.
SI_LicenseRequest_Edition.defaultText: Not set: no edition is named in the request
SI_LicenseRequest_Edition.effect: The named edition is included in the request as a wish; the licence issued is decided by the provider.
SI_LicenseRequest_Edition.whenToChange: Only when asked to name an edition in your licence request.

SI_LoadPendingRules.label: Use AI-proposed draft rules
SI_LoadPendingRules.purpose: Lets the profiling engines also load draft posture rules proposed by schema discovery, before anyone has reviewed them.
SI_LoadPendingRules.defaultText: Off: only shipped and your own custom rules are used.
SI_LoadPendingRules.effect: When on, unreviewed AI-drafted rules also affect findings and tiers. This can add useful detections but also wrong or noisy results.
SI_LoadPendingRules.whenToChange: Only for testing drafts in a lab; normally review and promote drafts instead.

SI_Location.label: Azure region
SI_Location.purpose: The Azure region setup creates the workspace, endpoint, storage and container resources in. A collection run creates no Azure resource, so it does not need it.
SI_Location.defaultText: Not set: setup asks for the region; a collection run does not use it
SI_Location.effect: Decides where setup creates new resources. Existing resources are not moved. Risk Analysis falls back to Location, then westeurope.
SI_Location.whenToChange: Set once at install to your preferred region.

SI_LogIngest_AppId.label: Ingestion app id (older name)
SI_LogIngest_AppId.purpose: Older name for the app id used to send data to Log Analytics; used only when SI_SPN_AppId is not set.
SI_LogIngest_AppId.effect: Only matters when SI_SPN_AppId is empty; then data ingestion signs in with this app.
SI_LogIngest_AppId.whenToChange: Never on new installs; use SI_SPN_AppId instead.

SI_LogIngest_ObjectId.label: Ingestion object id (older name)
SI_LogIngest_ObjectId.purpose: Older name for the object id of the ingesting service principal, used to grant it rights on data collection rules; used when SI_SPN_ObjectId is not set.
SI_LogIngest_ObjectId.effect: Used only when SI_SPN_ObjectId is empty: every output path that grants ingest rights on a data collection rule takes SI_SPN_ObjectId first and this name second.
SI_LogIngest_ObjectId.whenToChange: Never on new installs; set SI_SPN_ObjectId instead.

SI_LogIngest_Secret.label: Ingestion secret (older name)
SI_LogIngest_Secret.purpose: Older name for the client secret used to send data to Log Analytics; used only when SI_SPN_Secret is not set.
SI_LogIngest_Secret.effect: Only matters when SI_SPN_Secret is empty; then data ingestion signs in with this secret.
SI_LogIngest_Secret.whenToChange: Never on new installs; use SI_SPN_Secret, a certificate or managed identity.

SI_LogIngest_TenantId.label: Ingestion tenant id (older name)
SI_LogIngest_TenantId.purpose: Older name for the Entra tenant id used to send data to Log Analytics; used only when SI_SPN_TenantId is not set.
SI_LogIngest_TenantId.effect: Only matters when SI_SPN_TenantId is empty; then data ingestion signs in to this tenant.
SI_LogIngest_TenantId.whenToChange: Never on new installs; use SI_SPN_TenantId instead.

SI_LogRetentionDays.label: Run log retention
SI_LogRetentionDays.purpose: How many days run logs are kept, both on the local disk and in the storage account, before being deleted.
SI_LogRetentionDays.effect: Longer keeps more history for investigating past runs, using more disk and storage space. Shorter frees space but older runs can no longer be checked.
SI_LogRetentionDays.whenToChange: When your audit or troubleshooting needs require a longer or shorter history.

SI_ManagedIdentityClientId.label: User-assigned managed identity
SI_ManagedIdentityClientId.purpose: Client id of a user-assigned managed identity to sign in with when the sign-in method is managed identity.
SI_ManagedIdentityClientId.effect: Selects which managed identity holds the permissions. A wrong client id makes sign-in fail; empty uses the Azure VM's or Arc server's own identity.
SI_ManagedIdentityClientId.whenToChange: Only when you sign in with a user-assigned identity instead of the host's system-assigned one.

SI_MaxMailAttachmentMB.label: Largest mail attachment
SI_MaxMailAttachmentMB.purpose: The largest Excel attachment, measured as encoded for mail, that a Risk Analysis mail carries; larger reports are mailed without the attachment.
SI_MaxMailAttachmentMB.defaultText: 24 MB (fits a 25 MB mail server limit)
SI_MaxMailAttachmentMB.effect: Raising it lets bigger workbooks be attached, but above your mail server's limit the whole mail is rejected and nothing arrives. Lowering it is always safe.
SI_MaxMailAttachmentMB.whenToChange: Raise only if your mail server accepts larger messages; lower if mails are rejected.
SI_MaxMailAttachmentMB.hint: A larger report is mailed without its Excel file.

SI_PayloadProfile.label: Asset detail level
SI_PayloadProfile.purpose: Chooses how much detail is kept per asset: everything collected (cmdb) or only the columns the schema declares (security).
SI_PayloadProfile.defaultText: cmdb: every collected property is kept
SI_PayloadProfile.effect: security gives smaller rows and lower ingest cost, but drops undeclared properties that queries or dashboards may use; dropped fields are listed in the run log. An unknown value falls back to cmdb.
SI_PayloadProfile.whenToChange: Consider security only if ingest volume matters more than a full asset inventory.

SI_PreferUami.label: Managed identity switch (older name)
SI_PreferUami.purpose: Older switch to sign in with a managed identity, still honoured; SI_AuthMethod is the setting to use.
SI_PreferUami.defaultText: Off, unless the sign-in choice selects managed identity
SI_PreferUami.effect: When on and no service principal is configured, managed identity is used. For Log Analytics ingestion it takes effect only together with a user-assigned client id.
SI_PreferUami.whenToChange: Never on new installs; set SI_AuthMethod instead.

SI_PrivilegeTierClassifier_RunAI.label: AI for privilege tier catalog
SI_PrivilegeTierClassifier_RunAI.purpose: An override for ONE engine: whether the privilege tier classifier asks Azure OpenAI to tier new roles and permissions. It follows its own switch, not AI integration: it calls AI whenever the Azure OpenAI settings are set, unless this is off.
SI_PrivilegeTierClassifier_RunAI.effect: Turning it off sends nothing to Azure OpenAI: roles and permissions already in the catalog keep their tier, and new ones are left unresolved for manual review. Removes AI cost for this engine.
SI_PrivilegeTierClassifier_RunAI.whenToChange: Only to keep AI out of the privilege tier classifier while it is used elsewhere; or turn it off if you tier new roles yourself.

SI_PrivilegeTierClassifier_RefreshDays.label: Privilege tier catalog: days kept while unchanged
SI_PrivilegeTierClassifier_RefreshDays.purpose: How long the privilege tier classifier keeps its catalog while nothing it is made from changed. Every run reads the Entra role definitions, the API permission catalog and the Azure role definitions (seconds); when they, the engine and the AI settings are the same as for the last complete catalog and that catalog is younger than this, the AI pass is skipped and the catalog is kept.
SI_PrivilegeTierClassifier_RefreshDays.defaultText: 7 days: the catalog is rebuilt as soon as a role or permission changes, and at least once a week
SI_PrivilegeTierClassifier_RefreshDays.effect: A lower value rebuilds (and sends the AI requests) more often; 0 rebuilds on every run, as before. A catalog that left items untiered is always rebuilt on the next run.
SI_PrivilegeTierClassifier_RefreshDays.whenToChange: Set 0 to rebuild every run, for example while you test new tiering prompts; raise it to cut AI calls further.

SI_AssetTagging_Enabled.label: Asset tagging
SI_AssetTagging_Enabled.purpose: Turns asset tagging on: the asset-tagging rules (for example Auto-CanBeOnboarded--Excluded--SI for the devices Defender can onboard) apply inside SecurityInsight, and the tagging job may run.
SI_AssetTagging_Enabled.defaultText: Off: no tagging rule sets a tag anywhere and no report treats a device as excluded because of one
SI_AssetTagging_Enabled.effect: On, the asset-tagging rules you have switched on tag the CIs inside SecurityInsight, and a rule whose tag ends in --Excluded--SI takes the device out of every report. Writing the tags to Defender, Azure and Entra stays the separate 'Asset tagging writes tags' setting. Off, no tagging rule tags anything, the tagging job does not run, and a tag an earlier tagging run wrote is ignored; your own exclusion tags keep working.
SI_AssetTagging_Enabled.whenToChange: Turn it on when you want the automatic exclusion rules (devices Defender cannot onboard, name patterns) to take devices out of the reports -- and check the Excluded assets report afterwards.

SI_AssetTagging_Apply.label: Asset tagging on a server writes tags
SI_AssetTagging_Apply.purpose: Lets the asset-tagging script on a server (launcher.community-vm.ps1) write the tags its rules select in Defender, Azure and Entra on every run, instead of only reporting them.
SI_AssetTagging_Apply.defaultText: Off: report only, every planned tag is logged, nothing is changed
SI_AssetTagging_Apply.effect: On, every run changes Defender machine tags, Azure resource tags and Entra custom security attributes in your tenant; -WhatIfMode on a run still makes that run report only. The identity also needs the write grants. For one run only, use -Apply instead.
SI_AssetTagging_Apply.whenToChange: Turn it on after reviewing the report-only results and granting the tagging write grants. An install that wrote tags before 3.0 sets it to keep writing.

SI_Pro_AssetTagging_Apply.label: Asset tagging writes tags
SI_Pro_AssetTagging_Apply.purpose: Lets the asset-tagging job actually write the tags its rules select in Defender, Azure and Entra, instead of only reporting them.
SI_Pro_AssetTagging_Apply.defaultText: Off: report only, every planned tag is logged, nothing is changed
SI_Pro_AssetTagging_Apply.effect: On, the job changes Defender machine tags, Azure resource tags and Entra custom security attributes in your tenant. Only a real true turns it on; the job identity also needs the write roles.
SI_Pro_AssetTagging_Apply.whenToChange: Turn it on after reviewing the report-only results and granting the tagging write roles.

SI_Pro_DataLookbackDays.label: Pro data sync look-back
SI_Pro_DataLookbackDays.purpose: How many days back in Log Analytics the Pro data sync looks for complete runs it has not copied yet.
SI_Pro_DataLookbackDays.effect: A longer look-back catches up after longer outages but makes each sync query more data and take longer. Too short can leave runs from a long outage uncopied. A value below 1 or not a whole number stops the sync.
SI_Pro_DataLookbackDays.whenToChange: Raise it temporarily after the sync has been down for more than a few days.

SI_SqlPacing_Enabled.label: Slow down large writes when the database is busy
SI_SqlPacing_Enabled.purpose: Whether the large database writers (Risk Analysis storing its findings, the data sync preparing the views, the removal of old collections) look at how busy the database is before each batch.
SI_SqlPacing_Enabled.effect: On: while the database is at its limit (log write, data reads or CPU above the high mark), each writer pauses before its next batch and writes smaller batches, so the web app and the other jobs keep a share; below the low mark it writes at full pace again. Nothing is left out -- the same rows are written, only slower while the database is saturated. Off: the writers always write at full pace.
SI_SqlPacing_Enabled.whenToChange: Leave it on. Switch it off only if support asks you to.

SI_SqlPacing_HighPercent.label: Database busy above (percent)
SI_SqlPacing_HighPercent.purpose: The database load (the highest of log write, data reads and CPU, in percent of what its tier allows) above which the large writers slow down.
SI_SqlPacing_HighPercent.effect: Lower: the writers make room for the web app sooner, and a full run takes longer on a busy database. Higher: the writers keep their pace until the database is closer to its limit. A value that is not a number from 1 to 100 uses 85.
SI_SqlPacing_HighPercent.whenToChange: Lower it if the web app is slow during the daily run; raise it if the run must finish sooner and nobody uses the web app then.

SI_SqlPacing_LowPercent.label: Database calm again below (percent)
SI_SqlPacing_LowPercent.purpose: The database load below which the large writers go back to their full pace after they slowed down.
SI_SqlPacing_LowPercent.effect: Between this and the busy mark a writer keeps the pause it has. Must be below the busy mark; a value at or above it uses the busy mark minus 15.
