SI_SqlPacing_LowPercent.whenToChange: Rarely. Lower it if the writers speed up and slow down again and again.

SI_Pro_DataRetentionDays.label: Pro data retention
SI_Pro_DataRetentionDays.purpose: How many days of run data (findings, assets, daily aggregates) the Pro database keeps before older collections are removed.
SI_Pro_DataRetentionDays.effect: Longer keeps more history for trends but grows the database and its cost; shorter purges history permanently. Current vulnerability state and the identity ledger are never purged. An invalid value stops the sync.
SI_Pro_DataRetentionDays.whenToChange: Change it when you need longer history for reporting or must limit database size.

SI_RA_SourceFirstSeen.label: Read Defender's first sighting of each vulnerability
SI_RA_SourceFirstSeen.purpose: Risk Analysis reads Defender for Endpoint's software vulnerabilities export once per run for the first time each CVE was seen on each device (si_source_first_seen).
SI_RA_SourceFirstSeen.effect: The protection score's "within Accepted Lifecycle" view ages a vulnerability by Defender's own first sighting instead of SecurityInsight's first detection. Off: the export is not read and the vulnerability findings carry no source first-seen.
SI_RA_SourceFirstSeen.whenToChange: Turn it off only when the export takes too long or the permission Vulnerability.Read.All is not granted.
SI_RA_SourceFirstSeen.group: Risk Analysis -- mails and executive view

SI_ProtectionScore_GraceDays_Device.label: Protection Score: accepted lifecycle for devices (days)
SI_ProtectionScore_GraceDays_Device.purpose: The protection score's accepted lifecycle for devices: how many days a Very High or High finding may be open before it counts in the "within Accepted Lifecycle" view.
SI_ProtectionScore_GraceDays_Device.effect: Only a PATCH finding (a vulnerability with a vendor fix: a fix release date, a recommended update or a patch cycle) gets this grace; every other finding has its own (SI_ProtectionScore_OtherGraceDays_*, default 0). A device patch finding younger than this (its age: the fix's release date, else the source's first-seen, else SI's first detection) does not lower the "within Accepted Lifecycle" protection score; the Actual Risks view always counts it. A finding with no date always counts. 0 = both views count it at once.
SI_ProtectionScore_GraceDays_Device.whenToChange: Your patching or remediation process gives devices a different grace (for example 14 days for identities).
SI_ProtectionScore_GraceDays_Device.group: Risk Analysis -- mails and executive view

SI_ProtectionScore_GraceDays_Identity.label: Protection Score: accepted lifecycle for identities (days)
SI_ProtectionScore_GraceDays_Identity.purpose: The protection score's accepted lifecycle for identities: how many days a Very High or High finding may be open before it counts in the "within Accepted Lifecycle" view.
SI_ProtectionScore_GraceDays_Identity.effect: Only a PATCH finding (a vulnerability with a vendor fix: a fix release date, a recommended update or a patch cycle) gets this grace; every other finding has its own (SI_ProtectionScore_OtherGraceDays_*, default 0). A identity patch finding younger than this (its age: the fix's release date, else the source's first-seen, else SI's first detection) does not lower the "within Accepted Lifecycle" protection score; the Actual Risks view always counts it. A finding with no date always counts. 0 = both views count it at once.
SI_ProtectionScore_GraceDays_Identity.whenToChange: Your patching or remediation process gives identities a different grace (for example 14 days for identities).
SI_ProtectionScore_GraceDays_Identity.group: Risk Analysis -- mails and executive view

SI_ProtectionScore_GraceDays_CloudResour.label: Protection Score: accepted lifecycle for cloud resources (days)
SI_ProtectionScore_GraceDays_CloudResour.purpose: The protection score's accepted lifecycle for cloud resources (Azure): how many days a Very High or High finding may be open before it counts in the "within Accepted Lifecycle" view.
SI_ProtectionScore_GraceDays_CloudResour.effect: Only a PATCH finding (a vulnerability with a vendor fix: a fix release date, a recommended update or a patch cycle) gets this grace; every other finding has its own (SI_ProtectionScore_OtherGraceDays_*, default 0). A cloud resource patch finding younger than this (its age: the fix's release date, else the source's first-seen, else SI's first detection) does not lower the "within Accepted Lifecycle" protection score; the Actual Risks view always counts it. A finding with no date always counts. 0 = both views count it at once.
SI_ProtectionScore_GraceDays_CloudResour.whenToChange: Your patching or remediation process gives cloud resources a different grace (for example 14 days for identities).
SI_ProtectionScore_GraceDays_CloudResour.group: Risk Analysis -- mails and executive view

SI_ProtectionScore_GraceDays_PublicIp.label: Protection Score: accepted lifecycle for public IPs (days)
SI_ProtectionScore_GraceDays_PublicIp.purpose: The protection score's accepted lifecycle for public IP addresses: how many days a Very High or High finding may be open before it counts in the "within Accepted Lifecycle" view.
SI_ProtectionScore_GraceDays_PublicIp.effect: Only a PATCH finding (a vulnerability with a vendor fix: a fix release date, a recommended update or a patch cycle) gets this grace; every other finding has its own (SI_ProtectionScore_OtherGraceDays_*, default 0). A public IP patch finding younger than this (its age: the fix's release date, else the source's first-seen, else SI's first detection) does not lower the "within Accepted Lifecycle" protection score; the Actual Risks view always counts it. A finding with no date always counts. 0 = both views count it at once.
SI_ProtectionScore_GraceDays_PublicIp.whenToChange: Your patching or remediation process gives public IPs a different grace (for example 14 days for identities).
SI_ProtectionScore_GraceDays_PublicIp.group: Risk Analysis -- mails and executive view

SI_ProtectionScore_OtherGraceDays_Device.label: Protection Score: grace for other device findings (days)
SI_ProtectionScore_OtherGraceDays_Device.purpose: How many days a Very High or High device finding that is NOT a patch (a configuration, an attack path, a vulnerability with no vendor fix) may be open before it counts in the "within Accepted Lifecycle" view.
SI_ProtectionScore_OtherGraceDays_Device.defaultText: 0 days: it counts from the day it is found
SI_ProtectionScore_OtherGraceDays_Device.effect: 0: such a finding is a risk from day one in both views. A higher number gives it a grace like a patch's (its age: the source's first-seen, else SI's first detection); a finding with no date always counts.
SI_ProtectionScore_OtherGraceDays_Device.whenToChange: Your process accepts a time to fix configuration findings too (for example 14 days).
SI_ProtectionScore_OtherGraceDays_Device.group: Risk Analysis -- mails and executive view

SI_ProtectionScore_OtherGraceDays_Identi.label: Protection Score: grace for identity findings (days)
SI_ProtectionScore_OtherGraceDays_Identi.purpose: How many days a Very High or High identity finding (MFA, roles, sign-ins, attack paths -- anything that is not a patch) may be open before it counts in the "within Accepted Lifecycle" view.
SI_ProtectionScore_OtherGraceDays_Identi.defaultText: 0 days: it counts from the day it is found
SI_ProtectionScore_OtherGraceDays_Identi.effect: 0: such a finding is a risk from day one in both views. A higher number gives it a grace (its age: the source's first-seen, else SI's first detection); a finding with no date always counts.
SI_ProtectionScore_OtherGraceDays_Identi.whenToChange: Your identity team has an agreed time to fix (for example 7 days).
SI_ProtectionScore_OtherGraceDays_Identi.group: Risk Analysis -- mails and executive view

SI_ProtectionScore_OtherGraceDays_CloudR.label: Protection Score: grace for Azure findings (days)
SI_ProtectionScore_OtherGraceDays_CloudR.purpose: How many days a Very High or High finding on a cloud resource that is not a patch (an Azure / Defender for Cloud recommendation, an attack path) may be open before it counts in the "within Accepted Lifecycle" view.
SI_ProtectionScore_OtherGraceDays_CloudR.defaultText: 0 days: it counts from the day it is found
SI_ProtectionScore_OtherGraceDays_CloudR.effect: 0: such a finding is a risk from day one in both views. A higher number gives it a grace (its age: the source's first-seen, else SI's first detection); a finding with no date always counts.
SI_ProtectionScore_OtherGraceDays_CloudR.whenToChange: Your cloud team has an agreed time to fix recommendations (for example 30 days).
SI_ProtectionScore_OtherGraceDays_CloudR.group: Risk Analysis -- mails and executive view

SI_ProtectionScore_OtherGraceDays_Public.label: Protection Score: grace for other public IP findings (days)
SI_ProtectionScore_OtherGraceDays_Public.purpose: How many days a Very High or High finding on a public IP that is not a patch (an open port, an exposed service) may be open before it counts in the "within Accepted Lifecycle" view.
SI_ProtectionScore_OtherGraceDays_Public.defaultText: 0 days: it counts from the day it is found
SI_ProtectionScore_OtherGraceDays_Public.effect: 0: such a finding is a risk from day one in both views. A higher number gives it a grace (its age: the source's first-seen, else SI's first detection); a finding with no date always counts.
SI_ProtectionScore_OtherGraceDays_Public.whenToChange: Your network team has an agreed time to close exposures.
SI_ProtectionScore_OtherGraceDays_Public.group: Risk Analysis -- mails and executive view

SI_ProtectionScore_TierWeights.label: Protection score: tier weights
SI_ProtectionScore_TierWeights.purpose: How much an asset of each tier weighs in the protection score, Tier 0 to Tier 3, separated by commas.
SI_ProtectionScore_TierWeights.effect: A Tier 0 asset out of good standing lowers the score as much as eight Tier 3 assets with the default. Four numbers, 0 or more; anything else = the default.
SI_ProtectionScore_TierWeights.group: Risk Analysis -- mails and executive view

SI_KeyFigures_RecentDays.label: Key figures: opened / fixed in the last (days)
SI_KeyFigures_RecentDays.purpose: The window of the key figures "Vulnerabilities opened in the last N days" and "Vulnerabilities fixed in the last N days" (the Executive overview, the Executive report and the management mail).
SI_KeyFigures_RecentDays.effect: The next data sync counts the CVE findings first detected, and the CVE findings remediated, within this many days before the collection; the labels say the number in force. Collections already figured keep the window they were worked out with; an update works the newest ones out again.
SI_KeyFigures_RecentDays.whenToChange: Your management reports per quarter or per sprint (for example 90 or 14).
SI_KeyFigures_RecentDays.group: Risk Analysis -- mails and executive view

SI_KeyFigures_MeanTimeToFixDays.label: Key figures: mean time to fix over the last (days)
SI_KeyFigures_MeanTimeToFixDays.purpose: Which fixed vulnerabilities the key figure "Mean time to fix" averages: those remediated within this many days before the collection.
SI_KeyFigures_MeanTimeToFixDays.effect: The next data sync averages the days from first detection to remediation of the CVE findings remediated in this window; the label says the number in force.
SI_KeyFigures_MeanTimeToFixDays.whenToChange: A longer window gives a steadier number, a shorter one shows a recent change sooner.
SI_KeyFigures_MeanTimeToFixDays.group: Risk Analysis -- mails and executive view

SI_KeyFigures_StaleAdminDays.label: Key figures: privileged accounts without a sign-in for (days)
SI_KeyFigures_StaleAdminDays.purpose: When the key figure "Privileged accounts without a sign-in for N days" counts an enabled, active privileged account: its last sign-in is longer ago than this.
SI_KeyFigures_StaleAdminDays.effect: The next data sync counts the privileged accounts whose last sign-in (Entra ID sign-in activity) is older than this many days before the collection; the label says the number in force.
SI_KeyFigures_StaleAdminDays.whenToChange: Your access review calls an admin account stale sooner (for example 30 or 45 days).
SI_KeyFigures_StaleAdminDays.group: Risk Analysis -- mails and executive view

SI_KeyFigures_CveAgeBands.label: Key figures: age bands of open CVE findings (days)
SI_KeyFigures_CveAgeBands.purpose: The bands of the key figures' table "Age of open CVE findings": one row "older than N days" per number, separated by commas.
SI_KeyFigures_CveAgeBands.effect: The next data sync counts the open CVE findings first detected more than each number of days before the collection. Whole numbers 1 to 3650; a list with none = the default.
SI_KeyFigures_CveAgeBands.whenToChange: Your patch policy has other milestones (for example 14,30,90).
SI_KeyFigures_CveAgeBands.group: Risk Analysis -- mails and executive view

SI_ProtectionScore_Severities.label: Protection score: severities that count
SI_ProtectionScore_Severities.purpose: The finding severities that take an asset out of good standing in the protection score.
SI_ProtectionScore_Severities.effect: An asset with an open, non-exempted finding of one of these severities is not in good standing. Separate with commas.
SI_ProtectionScore_Severities.whenToChange: Also count Medium findings, for a stricter score.
SI_ProtectionScore_Severities.group: Risk Analysis -- mails and executive view

SI_Pro_HiddenViews.label: Hidden named views
SI_Pro_HiddenViews.purpose: The named views SecurityInsight ships for Security recommendations, Summary and Detailed (Critical and High, On Tier 0, Vulnerabilities (CVE), Known exploited, MITRE, Compliance, CVSS) that are hidden from the view picker for everyone.
SI_Pro_HiddenViews.defaultText: None hidden: every shipped view is in the picker
SI_Pro_HiddenViews.effect: A view on the list is no longer offered in the picker of either page (critical-high, tier0, cve, exploited, mitre, compliance, cvss); summary:<view> or detailed:<view> hides it on one page only. Its address still opens it. The findings are unchanged.
SI_Pro_HiddenViews.whenToChange: Hide a view your organisation does not use, so the picker shows only the ones people need.
SI_Pro_HiddenViews.group: Risk Analysis -- mails and executive view

SI_Pro_ConfigBackupRetentionDays.label: Configuration backups kept (days)
SI_Pro_ConfigBackupRetentionDays.purpose: How many days the configuration backups are kept (the daily backup and Back up now).
SI_Pro_ConfigBackupRetentionDays.effect: The backup job removes backups older than this, except pinned ones and a backup whose content a newer one points at; each removal is recorded on the audit trail. A day without changes is recorded as no change, not copied again.
SI_Pro_ConfigBackupRetentionDays.whenToChange: When your policy needs backups for a longer or shorter time. The change journal is always kept at least this long.

SI_Pro_ConfigJournalRetentionDays.label: Change journal kept (days)
SI_Pro_ConfigJournalRetentionDays.purpose: How many days the change journal keeps its rows -- every configuration change, record by record, that undo and restore are built on.
SI_Pro_ConfigJournalRetentionDays.defaultText: not set: the change journal is kept forever
SI_Pro_ConfigJournalRetentionDays.effect: When set, the backup job removes journal rows older than this and records that on the audit trail. It can never be shorter than the backup retention: a shorter value is refused and the journal is kept, because an undo needs its evidence.
SI_Pro_ConfigJournalRetentionDays.whenToChange: Only when your retention policy requires configuration history to be removed after a period.

SI_Pro_AuditRetentionMonths.label: Audit trail retention
SI_Pro_AuditRetentionMonths.purpose: How many months the Pro audit trail (every action in the web app, the jobs and setup: who, when, why, before and after) keeps its rows.
SI_Pro_AuditRetentionMonths.defaultText: not set: the audit trail is kept forever
SI_Pro_AuditRetentionMonths.effect: When set, the data sync removes audit rows older than this many months and records that removal on the trail itself. It cannot be shorter than 13 months; a smaller value or one that is not a whole number is refused and the trail is kept in full.
SI_Pro_AuditRetentionMonths.whenToChange: Set it when your retention policy requires audit evidence to be removed after a period -- keep it at least as long as the data the trail explains.

SI_Pro_DataSqlDatabase.label: Pro data sync database
SI_Pro_DataSqlDatabase.purpose: The SQL database the Pro data sync writes run data to, when it should differ from the Pro settings database.
SI_Pro_DataSqlDatabase.effect: Points the data sync, the close-loop mail and data setup at another database. Without any Pro database configured the data sync job is skipped.
SI_Pro_DataSqlDatabase.whenToChange: Only when you deliberately keep run data in a separate database from the Pro settings.

SI_Pro_DataSqlServer.label: Pro data sync SQL server
SI_Pro_DataSqlServer.purpose: The SQL server the Pro data sync writes run data to, when it should differ from the Pro settings database's server.
SI_Pro_DataSqlServer.effect: Points the data sync (and the close-loop mail's data source) at another server; the identity must have access there. Without any Pro database configured the data sync job is skipped.
SI_Pro_DataSqlServer.whenToChange: Only when run data lives on a different SQL server than the Pro settings.

SI_Pro_DataSync_DryRun.label: Pro data sync dry run
SI_Pro_DataSync_DryRun.purpose: Makes the Pro data sync plan what it would copy and purge without writing anything to SQL.
SI_Pro_DataSync_DryRun.defaultText: Off: the data sync writes to the database
SI_Pro_DataSync_DryRun.effect: On, no run data reaches the Pro database and nothing is purged, so Pro pages stop getting new data. Useful to check a new setup safely.
SI_Pro_DataSync_DryRun.whenToChange: Turn on briefly when testing a new database setup; turn off again afterwards.

SI_Pro_CmdbSql_Enabled.label: SQL CMDB connector
SI_Pro_CmdbSql_Enabled.purpose: Writes every asset SecurityInsight knows into a CI table in the Pro database (one row per asset with its tier, department, owner, business services, identifiers and change history), for reporting and Power BI.
SI_Pro_CmdbSql_Enabled.defaultText: On when a Pro database is configured
SI_Pro_CmdbSql_Enabled.effect: Off, the CMDB connector job ends at once and the CI table keeps what it last held; nothing is deleted. On, each run creates new CIs, updates changed ones and retires CIs that are gone.
SI_Pro_CmdbSql_Enabled.whenToChange: Turn off only if you do not want the CI table kept up to date.

SI_Pro_CmdbSql_RetireAfterRuns.label: Runs before a CI is retired
SI_Pro_CmdbSql_RetireAfterRuns.purpose: How many complete runs in a row an asset must be missing before the SQL CMDB connector retires its CI.
SI_Pro_CmdbSql_RetireAfterRuns.effect: Higher keeps CIs of assets that drop out now and then, but marks really removed assets as retired later. A retired CI is kept with its history and comes back if the asset is seen again. A run that reads the same snapshot as the last one does not count. Below 1 is raised to 1; non-numbers use 2.
SI_Pro_CmdbSql_RetireAfterRuns.whenToChange: Raise it if CIs are retired and reactivated for assets that are still there.

SI_Cmdb_RetireAfterDays.label: Days unseen before a CI may be retired
SI_Cmdb_RetireAfterDays.purpose: The least number of days an asset must go unseen before its CI is retired -- in the CI table and in the state handed to ServiceNow. A brake under every other rule: whatever decided the retirement (the grace period, the runs missing, an early retirement on the Not seen anymore page), the CI waits until its asset has been unseen this long.
SI_Cmdb_RetireAfterDays.effect: Higher keeps CIs of assets that are away for a while; a CI retired too early is the one mistake that does not heal by itself. No grace period can be shorter than this. Below 1 is raised to 1; non-numbers use 7.
SI_Cmdb_RetireAfterDays.whenToChange: Raise it if CIs are retired for assets that come back after a week or more.

SI_Pro_AssetRetire_GraceDays.label: Days before an unseen asset is retired
SI_Pro_AssetRetire_GraceDays.purpose: How many days an asset SecurityInsight no longer sees may stay unseen before it is retired: its open vulnerabilities close as AssetRetired (never as fixed), its CI in the CI table is retired, and ServiceNow gets the state (u_si_state = retired). Used for every category that has no value of its own.
SI_Pro_AssetRetire_GraceDays.effect: Until then the asset is listed on Assets & services > CMDB > Not seen anymore with its open findings, where an Admin may retire it early. Seen again = active again, and its findings reopen. Shorter than the seen-window (8 days) is raised to the seen-window; non-numbers use 30.
SI_Pro_AssetRetire_GraceDays.whenToChange: Raise it if assets are away longer than this and come back (for example laptops during a long holiday); lower it to close the findings of removed assets sooner.

SI_Pro_AssetRetire_GraceDays_ClientPc.label: Days before an unseen asset is retired: client PCs
SI_Pro_AssetRetire_GraceDays_ClientPc.purpose: The grace period for client PCs -- a device whose operating system is not a server (laptops, desktops). Overrides the general value for this category.
SI_Pro_AssetRetire_GraceDays_ClientPc.effect: An asset of this category that SecurityInsight has not seen for longer than this is retired; its open vulnerabilities close as AssetRetired and ServiceNow gets the state. Seen again = active again. Shorter than the seen-window (8 days) is raised to it.
SI_Pro_AssetRetire_GraceDays_ClientPc.whenToChange: Raise it if people are away longer than this with their laptop switched off (holidays, leave).

SI_Pro_AssetRetire_GraceDays_Server.label: Days before an unseen asset is retired: servers
SI_Pro_AssetRetire_GraceDays_Server.purpose: The grace period for servers -- a device with a server operating system, or an Arc-connected machine. Overrides the general value for this category.
SI_Pro_AssetRetire_GraceDays_Server.effect: An asset of this category that SecurityInsight has not seen for longer than this is retired; its open vulnerabilities close as AssetRetired and ServiceNow gets the state. Seen again = active again. Shorter than the seen-window (8 days) is raised to it.
SI_Pro_AssetRetire_GraceDays_Server.whenToChange: Lower it if your servers are decommissioned through a process you trust and you want their findings closed sooner.

SI_Pro_AssetRetire_GraceDays_ServicePrin.label: Days before an unseen asset is retired: service principals
SI_Pro_AssetRetire_GraceDays_ServicePrin.purpose: The grace period for service principals -- an Entra service principal or managed identity. Overrides the general value for this category.
SI_Pro_AssetRetire_GraceDays_ServicePrin.effect: An asset of this category that SecurityInsight has not seen for longer than this is retired; its open vulnerabilities close as AssetRetired and ServiceNow gets the state. Seen again = active again. Shorter than the seen-window (8 days) is raised to it.
SI_Pro_AssetRetire_GraceDays_ServicePrin.whenToChange: Raise it for service principals that are used only now and then.

SI_Pro_AssetRetire_GraceDays_User.label: Days before an unseen asset is retired: users
SI_Pro_AssetRetire_GraceDays_User.purpose: The grace period for users -- an Entra user account. Overrides the general value for this category.
SI_Pro_AssetRetire_GraceDays_User.effect: An asset of this category that SecurityInsight has not seen for longer than this is retired; its open vulnerabilities close as AssetRetired and ServiceNow gets the state. Seen again = active again. Shorter than the seen-window (8 days) is raised to it.
SI_Pro_AssetRetire_GraceDays_User.whenToChange: Raise it if accounts are disabled for long periods (leave) and come back.

SI_Pro_AssetRetire_GraceDays_AzureVm.label: Days before an unseen asset is retired: Azure virtual machines
SI_Pro_AssetRetire_GraceDays_AzureVm.purpose: The grace period for Azure virtual machines -- an Azure virtual machine or scale set, also when Defender reports it as a device. Overrides the general value for this category.
SI_Pro_AssetRetire_GraceDays_AzureVm.effect: An asset of this category that SecurityInsight has not seen for longer than this is retired; its open vulnerabilities close as AssetRetired and ServiceNow gets the state. Seen again = active again. Shorter than the seen-window (8 days) is raised to it.
SI_Pro_AssetRetire_GraceDays_AzureVm.whenToChange: Raise it for VMs that are deallocated for long periods.

SI_Pro_AssetRetire_GraceDays_AzureResour.label: Days before an unseen asset is retired: other Azure resources
SI_Pro_AssetRetire_GraceDays_AzureResour.purpose: The grace period for other Azure resources -- any Azure resource that is not a virtual machine. Overrides the general value for this category.
SI_Pro_AssetRetire_GraceDays_AzureResour.effect: An asset of this category that SecurityInsight has not seen for longer than this is retired; its open vulnerabilities close as AssetRetired and ServiceNow gets the state. Seen again = active again. Shorter than the seen-window (8 days) is raised to it.
SI_Pro_AssetRetire_GraceDays_AzureResour.whenToChange: Lower it if Azure resources are deleted for good and you want their findings closed sooner.

SI_Pro_CmdbSql_Kinds.label: Asset kinds written as CIs
SI_Pro_CmdbSql_Kinds.purpose: Which kinds of asset the SQL CMDB connector writes to the CI table: endpoint (devices), azure (Azure resources) and publicip (public IP addresses).
SI_Pro_CmdbSql_Kinds.effect: A kind you add gets its CIs on the next run. CIs of a kind you remove are kept as they are (not retired). Identities are never written as CIs; unknown values are ignored.
SI_Pro_CmdbSql_Kinds.whenToChange: Add publicip if you want public IP addresses in the CI table as well.

SI_Pro_CmdbSql_SeenWithinDays.label: CI seen-window
SI_Pro_CmdbSql_SeenWithinDays.purpose: How recently an asset's profile must have been published for the SQL CMDB connector to count the asset as present.
SI_Pro_CmdbSql_SeenWithinDays.effect: Shorter notices removed assets sooner but can count low-tier assets as missing, because they are re-profiled only weekly. A kind whose newest snapshot is older than this is not used at all and the run changes nothing. Below 1 is raised to 1.
SI_Pro_CmdbSql_SeenWithinDays.whenToChange: Only if you changed how often low-tier assets are re-profiled; keep it above the slowest re-check interval.

SI_Pro_CmdbSql_DryRun.label: SQL CMDB connector dry run
SI_Pro_CmdbSql_DryRun.purpose: Makes the SQL CMDB connector plan what it would create, update and retire without writing anything to SQL.
SI_Pro_CmdbSql_DryRun.defaultText: Off: the connector writes the CI table
SI_Pro_CmdbSql_DryRun.effect: On, the CI table is not changed and no run is recorded there; the plan is in the job's log and on the audit trail as a plan.
SI_Pro_CmdbSql_DryRun.whenToChange: Turn on briefly to check a new setup; turn off again afterwards.

SI_PublicIp_DcrName.label: Public IP data collection rule
SI_PublicIp_DcrName.purpose: Names the data collection rule the public IP engine sends its results through.
SI_PublicIp_DcrName.effect: Results are ingested through the named rule instead. A name that does not exist, or matches a rule from another install, makes ingestion fail or land in the wrong place.
SI_PublicIp_DcrName.whenToChange: Only when a same-named rule from another install collides, or you deployed a uniquely named rule.

SI_PublicIP_DiscoverySource.label: Public IP discovery source
SI_PublicIP_DiscoverySource.purpose: Chooses where the engine finds public IP addresses to check: classified assets (profile-cl), Azure and Defender inventory (arg-eg), or both (union).
SI_PublicIP_DiscoverySource.defaultText: profile-cl: public IPs of already classified servers, plus your extra targets.
SI_PublicIP_DiscoverySource.effect: arg-eg covers every Azure public IP and Defender node but without tier or CMDB context; union checks everything. Broader modes mean more addresses, longer runs and more Shodan lookups. Unknown values fall back to profile-cl.
SI_PublicIP_DiscoverySource.whenToChange: When you want Azure public IPs that are not attached to a classified asset to be checked too.

SI_PublicIP_ExtraTargets.label: Extra public IPs to scan
SI_PublicIP_ExtraTargets.purpose: A list of additional public IP addresses to check every run, such as partner or supply-chain addresses.
SI_PublicIP_ExtraTargets.defaultText: Empty: only discovered addresses are checked.
SI_PublicIP_ExtraTargets.effect: Listed addresses are always added to the candidate set and looked up in Shodan, adding a lookup per address. They carry no tier or CMDB details unless given in the public IP schema overlay file.
SI_PublicIP_ExtraTargets.whenToChange: When you want to watch external addresses you care about but that SecurityInsight cannot discover.

SI_PublicIp_TableName.label: Public IP table name
SI_PublicIp_TableName.purpose: Names the Log Analytics table the public IP engine writes to.
SI_PublicIp_TableName.effect: Results go to the named table. Reports, risk analysis and the web app read the standard name, so a different name hides public IP data from them.
SI_PublicIp_TableName.whenToChange: Practically never; keep the standard name.

SI_RA_StaleDeviceFilter.label: Risk Analysis stale device filter
SI_RA_StaleDeviceFilter.purpose: Optionally removes devices not seen recently from the heavy attack-path Risk Analysis reports: off, lenient or strict.
SI_RA_StaleDeviceFilter.defaultText: Off: no devices are filtered out
SI_RA_StaleDeviceFilter.effect: lenient drops devices last seen longer ago than SI_ActiveStaleDays; strict also drops devices with no last-seen date. Smaller, faster reports, but findings on those devices are hidden.
SI_RA_StaleDeviceFilter.whenToChange: Only if attack-path reports are swamped by devices that no longer exist.

SI_RATop50_BlobContainer.label: Shared top-50 cache container
SI_RATop50_BlobContainer.purpose: The storage container holding the shared top-50 risk summary, so several hosts or containers reuse one summary instead of each building it.
SI_RATop50_BlobContainer.effect: The shared summary is read from and written to this container in the staging storage account. Hosts pointing at different containers each build their own summary.
SI_RATop50_BlobContainer.whenToChange: Practically never; only if the staging container was renamed.

SI_RATop50_BlobName.label: Shared top-50 cache file
SI_RATop50_BlobName.purpose: The file path, inside the container, of the shared top-50 risk summary that several hosts or containers reuse.
SI_RATop50_BlobName.effect: The shared summary is stored under this path. Hosts using different paths each build their own summary, which costs extra time and AI calls.
SI_RATop50_BlobName.whenToChange: Practically never; only to keep separate installs from sharing one summary.

SI_RebuildAuthBlock.label: Re-pull sign-in from Key Vault
SI_RebuildAuthBlock.purpose: Makes the authentication setup script re-read service principal credentials from Key Vault and rewrite them, even when they are already in the configuration file.
SI_RebuildAuthBlock.defaultText: Off: existing credentials are kept and only tested
SI_RebuildAuthBlock.effect: When on, the next setup run replaces the sign-in block in your configuration file with fresh values from Key Vault, for example after rotating a secret.
SI_RebuildAuthBlock.whenToChange: Only after rotating or replacing the service principal credential in Key Vault.

SI_RequireMdeActive_Endpoint.label: Only Defender-active endpoints
SI_RequireMdeActive_Endpoint.purpose: Narrows the endpoint inventory to devices that Defender for Endpoint reports as active or recently seen.
SI_RequireMdeActive_Endpoint.defaultText: Off: a device seen recently by Defender, Exposure Management or Entra is kept
SI_RequireMdeActive_Endpoint.effect: On drops devices known only to Exposure Management or Entra, such as some Azure VMs, personal and IoT devices: fewer rows, but less coverage. Ignored when SI_IncludeInactive_Endpoint is on.
SI_RequireMdeActive_Endpoint.whenToChange: Only if you want the inventory to match the Defender portal's active device list.

SI_RequireRecentSignIn_Identity.label: Require recent identity sign-in
SI_RequireRecentSignIn_Identity.purpose: Restores the older, stricter rule that an identity must have signed in recently to be published.
SI_RequireRecentSignIn_Identity.defaultText: Off: identities without recent or available sign-in data are still published
SI_RequireRecentSignIn_Identity.effect: On also drops every identity without a sign-in within SI_ActiveStaleDays, including ones whose sign-in history is unavailable: fewer rows, but real accounts may be missing.
SI_RequireRecentSignIn_Identity.whenToChange: Only if you need the behaviour of the previous major version.

SI_DataOut_Outputs.label: Data out: outputs written
SI_DataOut_Outputs.purpose: Which data-out outputs SecurityInsight writes after each data sync: the Excel workbooks (CIs, findings, the findings summary, records) and the ServiceNow Import Set hand-offs. Each is a listed connector whose runs and items are recorded.
SI_DataOut_Outputs.defaultText: Not set: the outputs that are on by default are written
SI_DataOut_Outputs.effect: A list of output ids (for example excel-ci, excel-findings-detailed, servicenow-ci) writes exactly those and no others; an id that is not an output is left out with a warning. Outputs of the other edition are never written.
SI_DataOut_Outputs.whenToChange: When you want a workbook or a ServiceNow hand-off that is off by default, or want to stop one that is on.

SI_DataOut_ServiceNowCiTable.label: Data out: ServiceNow CI Import Set table
SI_DataOut_ServiceNowCiTable.purpose: The ServiceNow Import Set table the CI hand-off output (servicenow-ci) sends its rows to.
SI_DataOut_ServiceNowCiTable.defaultText: Not set: the ServiceNow CI hand-off output is not written, and its run says so
SI_DataOut_ServiceNowCiTable.effect: Rows are sent to this Import Set table, where your transform map creates and updates CIs. Without it the output does nothing.
SI_DataOut_ServiceNowCiTable.whenToChange: When you switch the servicenow-ci output on.

SI_DataOut_ServiceNowVulnTable.label: Data out: ServiceNow vulnerable item Import Set table
SI_DataOut_ServiceNowVulnTable.purpose: The ServiceNow Import Set table the vulnerable item output (servicenow-vulnerable-item) sends its rows to.
SI_DataOut_ServiceNowVulnTable.defaultText: Not set: the ServiceNow vulnerable item output is not written, and its run says so
SI_DataOut_ServiceNowVulnTable.effect: Rows are sent to this Import Set table, where your transform map creates and updates vulnerable items. Without it the output does nothing.
SI_DataOut_ServiceNowVulnTable.whenToChange: When you switch the servicenow-vulnerable-item output on.

SI_DataOut_ServiceNowRequest.label: Data out: ServiceNow resync or test batch
SI_DataOut_ServiceNowRequest.purpose: A one-time request for the ServiceNow outputs, carried out on the next sync: a full resync (every record in scope sent again as new, in one batch) or a test batch (at most 5 rows per output, which your importer never imports).
SI_DataOut_ServiceNowRequest.defaultText: Empty: no request. Each request is carried out once.
SI_DataOut_ServiceNowRequest.effect: resync:<token> sends every record in scope as new in the next batch (mode resync, imported like a normal batch). test:<token> first sends a test batch of at most 5 rows per output (mode test, never imported), then the normal batch.
SI_DataOut_ServiceNowRequest.whenToChange: After your ServiceNow team rebuilt or emptied its tables (resync), or while it builds and checks its importer (test batch). Use the buttons on Connectors > ServiceNow: one route.

SI_DataOut_ServiceNowStagingStatusTable.label: Data out: ServiceNow staging status table
SI_DataOut_ServiceNowStagingStatusTable.purpose: The ServiceNow import set table where SecurityInsight says when each push of a ServiceNow output starts (writing) and ends (complete, failed or held). Every data row carries the same batch id, so your importer imports a batch only once it is complete.
SI_DataOut_ServiceNowStagingStatusTable.defaultText: u_si_staging_status. An install that sent to ServiceNow before the staging status table existed has it empty: the rows are sent without it, with a warning, until your ServiceNow team creates the table and you set its name here.
SI_DataOut_ServiceNowStagingStatusTable.effect: Set: each push is one batch -- a writing row first, the batch id on every data row, then a complete, failed or held row. If the table is missing or lacks a column, nothing is sent. Empty: the rows are sent without a batch, and the ServiceNow check warns.
SI_DataOut_ServiceNowStagingStatusTable.whenToChange: After your ServiceNow team has created the staging status table (Connectors > the ServiceNow data-out connector > For your ServiceNow team), if it has another name than the default -- or, on an install that has it empty, to switch it on.

SI_Pro_CiChangeRetentionDays.label: CI change history kept
SI_Pro_CiChangeRetentionDays.purpose: How many days the change history of each configuration item (CI) is kept in the Pro database.
SI_Pro_CiChangeRetentionDays.effect: Older CI changes are removed after each data sync. Longer keeps more history on the CI page but grows the database.
SI_Pro_CiChangeRetentionDays.whenToChange: Shorten it to keep the database small; lengthen it when you need a longer audit of CI changes.

SI_Pro_CiDailyRetentionDays.label: CI daily trend kept
SI_Pro_CiDailyRetentionDays.purpose: How many days of each CI's daily trend (risk score, open findings by severity) the Pro database keeps.
SI_Pro_CiDailyRetentionDays.effect: Older daily rows are removed after each data sync, so trend charts go back this far.
SI_Pro_CiDailyRetentionDays.whenToChange: Shorten it to keep the database small; lengthen it for longer trend charts.

SI_Pro_FindingStateRetentionDays.label: Closed finding history kept
SI_Pro_FindingStateRetentionDays.purpose: How many days a closed finding's lifecycle row (first detected, closed, close reason) is kept in the Pro database.
SI_Pro_FindingStateRetentionDays.effect: Closed lifecycle rows older than this are removed after each data sync; open findings are never removed.
SI_Pro_FindingStateRetentionDays.whenToChange: Lengthen it when you report on fixes over a longer period.

SI_Pro_FindingSla_CriticalDays.label: Days to fix a critical finding
SI_Pro_FindingSla_CriticalDays.purpose: How many days a critical finding has to be fixed, counted from when it was first found (or found again after it was fixed).
SI_Pro_FindingSla_CriticalDays.effect: Sets the due date of every critical finding. A finding past its due date is shown as overdue on the CI page, the service views and the trend. 0 = critical findings have no due date.
SI_Pro_FindingSla_CriticalDays.whenToChange: Set it to the deadline your security policy gives critical findings.

SI_Pro_FindingSla_HighDays.label: Days to fix a high finding
SI_Pro_FindingSla_HighDays.purpose: How many days a high finding has to be fixed, counted from when it was first found (or found again after it was fixed).
SI_Pro_FindingSla_HighDays.effect: Sets the due date of every high finding. A finding past its due date is shown as overdue. 0 = high findings have no due date.
SI_Pro_FindingSla_HighDays.whenToChange: Set it to the deadline your security policy gives high findings.

SI_Pro_FindingSla_MediumDays.label: Days to fix a medium finding
SI_Pro_FindingSla_MediumDays.purpose: How many days a medium finding has to be fixed, counted from when it was first found (or found again after it was fixed).
SI_Pro_FindingSla_MediumDays.effect: Sets the due date of every medium finding. A finding past its due date is shown as overdue. 0 = medium findings have no due date.
SI_Pro_FindingSla_MediumDays.whenToChange: Set it to the deadline your security policy gives medium findings.

SI_Pro_FindingSla_LowDays.label: Days to fix a low finding
SI_Pro_FindingSla_LowDays.purpose: How many days a low finding has to be fixed, counted from when it was first found (or found again after it was fixed).
SI_Pro_FindingSla_LowDays.effect: Sets the due date of every low finding. A finding past its due date is shown as overdue. 0 = low findings have no due date.
SI_Pro_FindingSla_LowDays.whenToChange: Set it to the deadline your security policy gives low findings.

SI_Cmdb_Run.label: ServiceNow CMDB: write or plan
SI_Cmdb_Run.purpose: Whether the ServiceNow CMDB connector writes to your ServiceNow instance or only plans and reports what it would write.
SI_Cmdb_Run.defaultText: plan: nothing is written to ServiceNow; the match report is produced
SI_Cmdb_Run.effect: apply writes the matched CIs (and, with creating allowed, new ones) to ServiceNow on every run. plan writes nothing.
SI_Cmdb_Run.whenToChange: Set apply once the plan report shows the matches you expect.

SI_Cmdb_Mode.label: ServiceNow CMDB: match mode
SI_Cmdb_Mode.purpose: Whether the ServiceNow CMDB connector only updates CIs it matched, or may also create CIs for assets it could not match.
SI_Cmdb_Mode.defaultText: match-only: only matched CIs are updated
SI_Cmdb_Mode.effect: create-if-unmatched creates a CI for an asset ServiceNow does not know, when creating is also allowed (SI_Cmdb_AllowCreate).
SI_Cmdb_Mode.whenToChange: When SecurityInsight should add the assets your CMDB is missing.

SI_Cmdb_AllowCreate.label: ServiceNow CMDB: allow creating CIs
SI_Cmdb_AllowCreate.purpose: The second switch needed before the ServiceNow CMDB connector creates a CI.
SI_Cmdb_AllowCreate.effect: On, with the create-if-unmatched mode and apply, unmatched assets are created as CIs in ServiceNow.

SI_Cmdb_RowLimit.label: ServiceNow CMDB: row limit
SI_Cmdb_RowLimit.purpose: A limit on how many assets one ServiceNow CMDB run handles, for trying the connector on a few assets first.
SI_Cmdb_RowLimit.effect: A number above 0 handles only that many assets per run.

SI_Correlation_DryRun.label: Asset correlation: plan only
SI_Correlation_DryRun.purpose: Makes the asset correlation compute and report its results without publishing them.
SI_Correlation_DryRun.defaultText: Off: the correlation results are published
SI_Correlation_DryRun.effect: On, nothing is published, so the CI keys stay as they were on the last published run.
SI_Correlation_DryRun.whenToChange: Only while checking a change to the correlation.

SI_Correlation_RowLimit.label: Asset correlation: row limit
SI_Correlation_RowLimit.purpose: A limit on how many assets one correlation run reads, for troubleshooting.
SI_Correlation_RowLimit.effect: A number above 0 correlates only that many assets; the rest keep their previous result.

SI_VulnSync_Run.label: Vulnerability connectors: plan only
SI_VulnSync_Run.purpose: plan keeps every vulnerability connector in plan mode, whatever mode each connector has; it writes nothing.
SI_VulnSync_Run.defaultText: Not set: each connector's own mode decides
SI_VulnSync_Run.effect: plan: no vulnerability, ticket or row is written or closed by any connector; each run reports what it would do. apply or not set: each connector runs in its own mode.
SI_VulnSync_Run.whenToChange: To pause every vulnerability connector at once, for example during a change in ServiceNow.

SI_DisabledAssets_Collect.label: Disabled accounts and devices: collect them
SI_DisabledAssets_Collect.purpose: Whether disabled users, service principals and managed identities, and disabled computers are collected from the sources. Disabled means the account is disabled in its own directory (Entra accountEnabled false, AD account disabled); it is never guessed from inactivity.
SI_DisabledAssets_Collect.defaultText: On: disabled accounts and devices are collected
SI_DisabledAssets_Collect.effect: Off leaves them out of the profiles, so no later stage can see them -- the correlation, Risk Analysis, finding actions and connector settings below then have no effect for disabled assets. Their open findings, actions and tickets are kept as they are (never resolved or closed). The state is read on every run: an account that is enabled again is collected again on the next run. Each run logs how many were left out.
SI_DisabledAssets_Collect.whenToChange: Turn it off only if you never want to see disabled accounts or devices anywhere in SecurityInsight.
SI_DisabledAssets_Collect.hint: Later stages only see what is collected.

SI_DisabledAssets_Correlate.label: Disabled accounts and devices: CI correlation
SI_DisabledAssets_Correlate.purpose: Whether disabled users, service principals, managed identities and computers take part in the correlation that builds configuration items (CIs).
SI_DisabledAssets_Correlate.defaultText: On: disabled assets are correlated into CIs
SI_DisabledAssets_Correlate.effect: Off keeps disabled assets out of the CI build: no CI is built or changed from them, and the findings of an existing CI are kept as they are (never resolved or closed) until the account is enabled again. Has no effect while collection of disabled assets is off -- they are not collected then. Each run logs how many were left out.
SI_DisabledAssets_Correlate.whenToChange: Turn it off when disabled assets should not appear as CIs or reach your CMDB.

SI_DisabledAssets_RiskAnalysis.label: Disabled accounts and devices: Risk Analysis
SI_DisabledAssets_RiskAnalysis.purpose: Whether the Risk Analysis reports include disabled users, service principals, managed identities and computers.
SI_DisabledAssets_RiskAnalysis.defaultText: Off: the reports leave disabled assets out, except the reports where the disabled state is the finding
SI_DisabledAssets_RiskAnalysis.effect: On lets every report see disabled assets. Two reports always see them, whatever this says, because the disabled state is the finding there: a disabled guest still holding a privileged role, and a disabled service principal still owning a publicly reachable resource. Reports that ask about usable accounts (for example accounts without MFA) keep their own enabled filter. Has no effect while collection of disabled assets is off.
SI_DisabledAssets_RiskAnalysis.whenToChange: Turn it on when you also want findings for disabled accounts and devices in the reports, for example while cleaning them up.

SI_DisabledAssets_StateActions.label: Disabled accounts and devices: finding actions
SI_DisabledAssets_StateActions.purpose: Whether the finding and vulnerability lifecycle acts on disabled assets: opening, resolving and closing findings, the close-loop mail and opening or closing tickets.
SI_DisabledAssets_StateActions.defaultText: Off: findings of disabled assets are kept as they are
SI_DisabledAssets_StateActions.effect: Off freezes the findings of a disabled asset: they are shown as excluded (disabled), never resolved or closed, and a missing finding is not counted as fixed. When the account is enabled again, the same findings carry on. On treats disabled assets like any other. Has no effect while collection of disabled assets is off. Each run logs how many were left out.
SI_DisabledAssets_StateActions.whenToChange: Turn it on when findings on disabled assets should be opened and closed like any other.

SI_DisabledAssets_Connectors.label: Disabled accounts and devices: connectors and exports
SI_DisabledAssets_Connectors.purpose: Whether connectors and exports send disabled users, service principals, managed identities and computers out of SecurityInsight (ServiceNow, Jira, risk register, CMDB, data exports).
SI_DisabledAssets_Connectors.defaultText: Off: connectors and exports leave disabled assets out
SI_DisabledAssets_Connectors.effect: Off leaves disabled assets out of what is sent; a ticket or record already sent for one is kept as it is (never resolved or closed because the asset was left out) and carries on when the account is enabled again. On sends them like any other. Has no effect while collection of disabled assets is off. Each run logs how many were left out.
SI_DisabledAssets_Connectors.whenToChange: Turn it on when your CMDB or ticketing system should also hold disabled accounts and devices.

SI_RiskAnalysis_BuildSummaryByAI.label: AI summary in the report mail (container jobs)
SI_RiskAnalysis_BuildSummaryByAI.purpose: Decides whether the risk-analysis container jobs ask Azure OpenAI to write a summary of the findings.
SI_RiskAnalysis_BuildSummaryByAI.defaultText: Not set: the jobs follow your general AI summary setting, otherwise off.
SI_RiskAnalysis_BuildSummaryByAI.effect: When on, each report run makes AI calls, adding cost and run time; the run stops if Azure OpenAI details are missing. When off, reports have no AI summary.
SI_RiskAnalysis_BuildSummaryByAI.whenToChange: When you want AI-written summaries in scheduled container reports.
SI_RiskAnalysis_BuildSummaryByAI.hint: When the reports run as container jobs.

SI_RiskAnalysis_DceIngestionUri.label: Risk analysis ingestion address
SI_RiskAnalysis_DceIngestionUri.purpose: The data collection endpoint address risk analysis sends its results to in Log Analytics.
SI_RiskAnalysis_DceIngestionUri.defaultText: Falls back to SI_DceIngestionUri, else found automatically from the endpoint name.
SI_RiskAnalysis_DceIngestionUri.effect: Forces results to this address. A wrong address makes Log Analytics ingestion fail; the Excel and JSON output are still written.
SI_RiskAnalysis_DceIngestionUri.whenToChange: Rarely; only when the address cannot be found automatically.

SI_RiskAnalysis_DceName.label: Risk analysis collection endpoint
SI_RiskAnalysis_DceName.purpose: Names the data collection endpoint risk analysis uses for its Log Analytics results.
SI_RiskAnalysis_DceName.defaultText: Falls back to SI_DceName, then DceName, then the standard SecurityInsight endpoint name.
SI_RiskAnalysis_DceName.effect: Risk analysis ingests through the named endpoint instead of the shared one. A wrong name makes ingestion fail; local output is still written.
SI_RiskAnalysis_DceName.whenToChange: Only when risk analysis must use a different endpoint than the other engines.

SI_RiskAnalysis_DcrName_Detailed.label: Detailed report data collection rule
SI_RiskAnalysis_DcrName_Detailed.purpose: The name of the data collection rule the detailed Risk Analysis rows are sent through to Log Analytics.
SI_RiskAnalysis_DcrName_Detailed.effect: Detailed rows are sent through the named rule. A wrong name makes the detailed report ingest fail.
SI_RiskAnalysis_DcrName_Detailed.whenToChange: Only if you renamed the rule or must avoid a name clash with another install.

SI_RiskAnalysis_DcrName_Summary.label: Summary report data collection rule
SI_RiskAnalysis_DcrName_Summary.purpose: The name of the data collection rule the summary Risk Analysis rows are sent through to Log Analytics.
SI_RiskAnalysis_DcrName_Summary.effect: Summary rows are sent through the named rule. A wrong name makes the summary report ingest fail.
SI_RiskAnalysis_DcrName_Summary.whenToChange: Only if you renamed the rule or must avoid a name clash with another install.

SI_RiskAnalysis_DcrResourceGroup.label: Risk Analysis rule resource group
SI_RiskAnalysis_DcrResourceGroup.purpose: Resource group holding the data collection rules Risk Analysis uses to send its results to Log Analytics, when it should differ from the solution-wide one.
SI_RiskAnalysis_DcrResourceGroup.defaultText: Uses SI_DcrResourceGroup (then DcrResourceGroup); if none is set, the standard SecurityInsight rules group.
SI_RiskAnalysis_DcrResourceGroup.effect: Risk Analysis looks up, and creates if missing, its two collection rules in this resource group. A wrong group means new rules are created there, separate from the rest of the solution.
SI_RiskAnalysis_DcrResourceGroup.whenToChange: Rarely; only when Risk Analysis must ingest through rules kept apart from the other engines.

SI_RiskAnalysis_ExportContainer.label: Report storage container
SI_RiskAnalysis_ExportContainer.purpose: The storage container in your staging storage account where the risk-analysis container jobs save their reports.
SI_RiskAnalysis_ExportContainer.effect: Reports are saved to this container. It is ignored when a full export destination is set, or when no staging storage account is configured.
SI_RiskAnalysis_ExportContainer.whenToChange: Only if reports must be kept apart from the staging data.

SI_RiskAnalysis_ExportDestination.label: Risk Analysis report export location
SI_RiskAnalysis_ExportDestination.purpose: Storage URL where container-hosted Risk Analysis jobs save their report workbooks and data files.
SI_RiskAnalysis_ExportDestination.defaultText: Built at setup from the staging storage account, folder risk-analysis in the staging container.
SI_RiskAnalysis_ExportDestination.effect: Read by container setup and passed to the Risk Analysis jobs. Reports are uploaded to this URL instead; the identity must be able to write there. On a server install the ExportDestination setting is used instead.
SI_RiskAnalysis_ExportDestination.whenToChange: When reports must land in a different storage account or container. Re-run setup for it to take effect.

SI_RiskAnalysis_ExportPrefix.label: Report storage folder
SI_RiskAnalysis_ExportPrefix.purpose: The folder inside the report storage container where the risk-analysis container jobs save their reports.
SI_RiskAnalysis_ExportPrefix.effect: Reports are saved under this folder; empty saves them at the container's top level. Ignored when a full export destination is set.
SI_RiskAnalysis_ExportPrefix.whenToChange: Only if your report readers expect another folder.

SI_RiskAnalysis_Mode.label: Container report mode
SI_RiskAnalysis_Mode.purpose: Summary or Detailed, for the scheduled Summary report job; used only when the report template's name does not say which.
SI_RiskAnalysis_Mode.effect: Decides which report and Log Analytics table the job uses when a custom template does not name its mode. With the shipped templates the template decides and this has no effect; a separate job builds the Detailed report.
SI_RiskAnalysis_Mode.whenToChange: Only with a custom report template whose name contains neither Summary nor Detailed.

SI_RiskAnalysis_ReportTemplate.label: Container summary report template
SI_RiskAnalysis_ReportTemplate.purpose: The report template the scheduled Summary risk-analysis container job uses.
SI_RiskAnalysis_ReportTemplate.defaultText: Your default Summary template if set, otherwise the shipped Summary template
SI_RiskAnalysis_ReportTemplate.effect: The Summary job builds this template instead. A Detailed template here makes that job build a Detailed report.
SI_RiskAnalysis_ReportTemplate.whenToChange: When the scheduled Summary job should use your own template.

SI_RiskAnalysis_SendToLogAnalytics.label: Copy Risk Analysis report rows to Log Analytics (container jobs, at setup)
SI_RiskAnalysis_SendToLogAnalytics.purpose: Optional, at setup only: whether the Risk Analysis container jobs are made with the copy of their report rows to Log Analytics (SI_RiskAnalysis_Detailed_CL) switched on. SecurityInsight itself does not need it: its pages read the results from its database. Off by default.
SI_RiskAnalysis_SendToLogAnalytics.defaultText: Not set: the jobs follow Copy Risk Analysis report rows to Log Analytics, which is off by default.
SI_RiskAnalysis_SendToLogAnalytics.effect: On: the jobs are made with the copy on (see Copy Risk Analysis report rows to Log Analytics). Not set or off: the jobs follow that setting, off by default.
SI_RiskAnalysis_SendToLogAnalytics.whenToChange: Only when your own workbooks, Sentinel rules or KQL read the report rows in Log Analytics; leave it not set otherwise.
SI_RiskAnalysis_SendToLogAnalytics.hint: When the reports run as container jobs.

SI_RiskAnalysis_TableName_Detailed.label: Detailed Risk Analysis table name
SI_RiskAnalysis_TableName_Detailed.purpose: Name of the Log Analytics table that receives rows from the Detailed Risk Analysis report.
SI_RiskAnalysis_TableName_Detailed.effect: Detailed results are written to a different table. Workbooks, queries and the trend engine that read the standard table will no longer see new data unless they are changed too.
SI_RiskAnalysis_TableName_Detailed.whenToChange: Almost never; only to avoid a clash with an existing table of the same name.

SI_RiskAnalysis_TableName_Summary.label: Summary Risk Analysis table name
SI_RiskAnalysis_TableName_Summary.purpose: Name of the Log Analytics table that receives rows from the Summary Risk Analysis report.
SI_RiskAnalysis_TableName_Summary.effect: Summary results are written to a different table. Anything reading the standard table, such as workbooks, queries and trend, stops seeing new data unless changed too.
SI_RiskAnalysis_TableName_Summary.whenToChange: Almost never; only to avoid a clash with an existing table of the same name.

SI_RiskAnalysis_WorkspaceName.label: Risk Analysis workspace name
SI_RiskAnalysis_WorkspaceName.purpose: Name of the Log Analytics workspace Risk Analysis writes its results to, when it should differ from the solution-wide workspace.
SI_RiskAnalysis_WorkspaceName.defaultText: Uses SI_WorkspaceName (then WorkspaceName); if none, the standard SecurityInsight workspace name.
SI_RiskAnalysis_WorkspaceName.effect: Risk Analysis results go to this workspace, which is created if it does not exist. Ignored when SI_RiskAnalysis_WorkspaceResourceId or a workspace resource id is set.
SI_RiskAnalysis_WorkspaceName.whenToChange: Only when Risk Analysis results must go to a separate workspace from collection data.

SI_RiskAnalysis_WorkspaceResourceGroup.label: Risk Analysis workspace resource group
SI_RiskAnalysis_WorkspaceResourceGroup.purpose: Resource group used to find or create the Risk Analysis workspace when it is given by name.
SI_RiskAnalysis_WorkspaceResourceGroup.defaultText: Uses WorkspaceResourceGroup; if not set, the standard SecurityInsight resource group.
SI_RiskAnalysis_WorkspaceResourceGroup.effect: Changes where Risk Analysis looks for, and creates, its workspace when only a workspace name is known. Has no effect when a full workspace resource id is set.
SI_RiskAnalysis_WorkspaceResourceGroup.whenToChange: Only with SI_RiskAnalysis_WorkspaceName, when that workspace lives in a different resource group.

SI_RiskAnalysis_WorkspaceResourceId.label: Risk Analysis workspace resource id
SI_RiskAnalysis_WorkspaceResourceId.purpose: Full resource id of the Log Analytics workspace Risk Analysis writes to and reads collected data from, overriding the shared workspace.
SI_RiskAnalysis_WorkspaceResourceId.defaultText: Uses SI_WorkspaceResourceId (then WorkspaceResourceId); otherwise the workspace is found by name.
SI_RiskAnalysis_WorkspaceResourceId.effect: Risk Analysis ingests its results into, and reads the SecurityInsight tables from, this workspace, which may be in another subscription. A workspace without the collected data gives empty or partial reports.
SI_RiskAnalysis_WorkspaceResourceId.whenToChange: Only for split setups where Risk Analysis uses a different workspace than the rest of the solution.

SI_RiskReport_GlobalWeight_Azure.label: Azure share of overall score
SI_RiskReport_GlobalWeight_Azure.purpose: How much the Azure score counts in the overall risk score, relative to the other domains.
SI_RiskReport_GlobalWeight_Azure.effect: A higher value makes Azure findings move the overall score more and the other domains less. Individual findings and their scores do not change.
SI_RiskReport_GlobalWeight_Azure.whenToChange: Only if Azure matters more or less to your organisation than the default balance.

SI_RiskReport_GlobalWeight_Endpoint.label: Endpoint share of overall score
SI_RiskReport_GlobalWeight_Endpoint.purpose: How much the endpoint score counts in the overall risk score, relative to the other domains.
SI_RiskReport_GlobalWeight_Endpoint.effect: A higher value makes endpoint findings move the overall score more and the other domains less. Individual findings and their scores do not change.
SI_RiskReport_GlobalWeight_Endpoint.whenToChange: Only if endpoints matter more or less to your organisation than the default balance.

SI_RiskReport_GlobalWeight_Identity.label: Identity share of overall score
SI_RiskReport_GlobalWeight_Identity.purpose: How much the identity score counts in the overall risk score, relative to the other domains.
SI_RiskReport_GlobalWeight_Identity.effect: A higher value makes identity findings move the overall score more and the other domains less. Individual findings and their scores do not change.
SI_RiskReport_GlobalWeight_Identity.whenToChange: Only if identities matter more or less to your organisation than the default balance.

SI_RiskReport_GlobalWeight_PublicIP.label: Public IP share of overall score
SI_RiskReport_GlobalWeight_PublicIP.purpose: How much the public IP score counts in the overall risk score, relative to the other domains.
SI_RiskReport_GlobalWeight_PublicIP.effect: A higher value makes public IP findings move the overall score more and the other domains less. Individual findings and their scores do not change.
SI_RiskReport_GlobalWeight_PublicIP.whenToChange: Only if internet exposure matters more or less to your organisation than the default balance.

SI_RiskReport_SeverityWeight_Critical.label: Critical finding weight
SI_RiskReport_SeverityWeight_Critical.purpose: How heavily a Critical finding lowers the score in the management risk score (on a 0 to 10 scale, where 10 is the full penalty).
SI_RiskReport_SeverityWeight_Critical.effect: A lower value makes Critical findings pull the domain and overall scores down less. Values above 10 act as 10. The original per-finding risk score is not affected.
SI_RiskReport_SeverityWeight_Critical.whenToChange: Rarely; only to tune the management score to your own risk appetite.

SI_RiskReport_SeverityWeight_High.label: High severity weight
SI_RiskReport_SeverityWeight_High.purpose: Sets how heavily a High (or Medium-High) severity finding counts in the Risk Analysis score columns used for management reporting.
SI_RiskReport_SeverityWeight_High.effect: A higher weight lowers the secure-score value of High findings and raises their share of the domain and overall scores. The original risk score columns are not affected.
SI_RiskReport_SeverityWeight_High.whenToChange: Most installs never should; change only to align the scores with your own risk model.

SI_RiskReport_SeverityWeight_Low.label: Low severity weight
SI_RiskReport_SeverityWeight_Low.purpose: Sets how heavily a Low severity finding counts in the Risk Analysis score columns used for management reporting.
SI_RiskReport_SeverityWeight_Low.effect: A higher weight lowers the secure-score value of Low findings and gives them more influence on the domain and overall scores. The original risk score columns are not affected.
SI_RiskReport_SeverityWeight_Low.whenToChange: Most installs never should; change only to align the scores with your own risk model.

SI_RiskReport_SeverityWeight_Medium.label: Medium severity weight
SI_RiskReport_SeverityWeight_Medium.purpose: Sets how heavily a Medium severity finding counts in the Risk Analysis score columns used for management reporting.
SI_RiskReport_SeverityWeight_Medium.effect: A higher weight lowers the secure-score value of Medium findings and gives them more influence on the domain and overall scores. The original risk score columns are not affected.
SI_RiskReport_SeverityWeight_Medium.whenToChange: Most installs never should; change only to align the scores with your own risk model.

SI_RiskReport_TierMultiplier_T0.label: Tier 0 score multiplier
SI_RiskReport_TierMultiplier_T0.purpose: Sets how much more a finding on a Tier 0 (most critical) asset counts in the Risk Analysis domain and overall scores.
SI_RiskReport_TierMultiplier_T0.effect: A higher value makes Tier 0 findings dominate the domain and overall scores; a lower value spreads attention to less critical assets. The original risk score columns are not affected.
SI_RiskReport_TierMultiplier_T0.whenToChange: Most installs never should; change only if your tier model weighs critical assets differently.

SI_RiskReport_TierMultiplier_T1.label: Tier 1 score multiplier
SI_RiskReport_TierMultiplier_T1.purpose: Sets how much a finding on a Tier 1 asset counts in the Risk Analysis domain and overall scores.
SI_RiskReport_TierMultiplier_T1.effect: A higher value gives Tier 1 findings more influence on the domain and overall scores. The original risk score columns are not affected.
SI_RiskReport_TierMultiplier_T1.whenToChange: Most installs never should; change only if your tier model weighs assets differently.

SI_RiskReport_TierMultiplier_T2.label: Tier 2 score multiplier
SI_RiskReport_TierMultiplier_T2.purpose: Sets how much a finding on a Tier 2 asset counts in the Risk Analysis domain and overall scores; the baseline the other tiers compare to.
SI_RiskReport_TierMultiplier_T2.defaultText: 1 (the baseline); assets with no tier also count 1
SI_RiskReport_TierMultiplier_T2.effect: Changing it shifts the balance between Tier 2 assets and the other tiers in the domain and overall scores. The original risk score columns are not affected.
SI_RiskReport_TierMultiplier_T2.whenToChange: Most installs never should; change only if your tier model weighs assets differently.

SI_RiskReport_TierMultiplier_T3.label: Tier 3 score multiplier
SI_RiskReport_TierMultiplier_T3.purpose: Sets how much a finding on a Tier 3 (least critical) asset counts in the Risk Analysis domain and overall scores.
SI_RiskReport_TierMultiplier_T3.effect: A higher value gives low-criticality assets more influence on the domain and overall scores; a lower value nearly ignores them. The original risk score columns are not affected.
SI_RiskReport_TierMultiplier_T3.whenToChange: Most installs never should; change only if your tier model weighs assets differently.

SI_SchemaCatalogDcr.label: Schema catalog collection rule
SI_SchemaCatalogDcr.purpose: Name of the data collection rule schema discovery uses to send its catalog of found data fields to Log Analytics.
SI_SchemaCatalogDcr.effect: Schema catalog rows are sent through this rule instead. A rule that does not match the catalog table makes the catalog stop arriving.
SI_SchemaCatalogDcr.whenToChange: Almost never; only to avoid a name clash with an existing rule.

SI_SchemaCatalogTable.label: Schema catalog table name
SI_SchemaCatalogTable.purpose: Log Analytics table receiving the schema catalog: new data fields, relationships and draft proposals found by schema discovery.
SI_SchemaCatalogTable.effect: Schema discovery writes its catalog to this table. Queries reading the standard table will no longer see new rows.
SI_SchemaCatalogTable.whenToChange: Almost never; only to avoid a clash with an existing table.

SI_SchemaProposeAiCeiling.label: Schema discovery AI budget
SI_SchemaProposeAiCeiling.purpose: Maximum estimated AI spend, in US dollars, for drafting rules from new findings in one schema-discovery run.
SI_SchemaProposeAiCeiling.effect: Raising it lets more new findings get an AI-drafted rule per run, at higher AI cost. Findings beyond the budget wait for the next weekly run.
SI_SchemaProposeAiCeiling.whenToChange: Lower it to cap AI cost; raise it if many findings keep being deferred.

SI_SchemaTables.label: Schema discovery hunting tables
SI_SchemaTables.purpose: List of Defender advanced-hunting tables whose columns schema discovery checks for new fields.
SI_SchemaTables.defaultText: A shipped list of 17 high-signal tables (device, identity, alert, email, cloud app, exposure graph).
SI_SchemaTables.effect: Replaces the shipped list entirely. Fewer tables means a faster run but new fields elsewhere go unnoticed; tables you cannot query cause errors for that table.
SI_SchemaTables.whenToChange: Only to add newly released tables or drop ones your licences do not include.

SI_Shodan_ApiKey.label: Shodan API key
SI_Shodan_ApiKey.purpose: The Shodan API key used to look up what is exposed on your public IP addresses.
SI_Shodan_ApiKey.defaultText: Not set: older SHODAN_ApiKey name or SHODAN_API_KEY environment variable is tried; else Shodan lookups are skipped.
SI_Shodan_ApiKey.effect: With a key, each address is enriched with open ports, services and vulnerabilities from Shodan, using your Shodan plan's quota. Without it the engine still writes rows, but every Shodan field is empty.
SI_Shodan_ApiKey.whenToChange: Set it when you use the public IP engine; rotate it when you reset the key in Shodan.

SI_Shodan_AssetLimit.label: Shodan address limit (older name)
SI_Shodan_AssetLimit.purpose: Caps how many public IP addresses are checked per run.
SI_Shodan_AssetLimit.effect: A positive number trims the candidate list to that many addresses, so the run is shorter and uses fewer Shodan lookups, but results are incomplete.
SI_Shodan_AssetLimit.whenToChange: Only for testing or a quick trial run.

SI_Shodan_ForceFreshScan.label: Shodan fresh scans
SI_Shodan_ForceFreshScan.purpose: Asks Shodan to actively re-scan your addresses before reading results, instead of using only data Shodan already has.
SI_Shodan_ForceFreshScan.defaultText: Off: cached and existing Shodan data only, no scan credits spent.
SI_Shodan_ForceFreshScan.effect: On, a batch scan is submitted (at most once per fresh scan interval) and the run waits for it; if it does not finish in time the run writes no rows and the next run picks it up. Spends Shodan scan credits.
SI_Shodan_ForceFreshScan.whenToChange: When you need current results and your Shodan plan has scan credits; schedule extra runs a few hours apart.

SI_Shodan_FreshScanIntervalHours.label: Shodan fresh scan interval
SI_Shodan_FreshScanIntervalHours.purpose: The minimum time between two fresh Shodan scans when fresh scans are on.
SI_Shodan_FreshScanIntervalHours.effect: Lower values submit new scans more often, spending more scan credits; higher values reuse the last scan longer. Only matters when SI_Shodan_ForceFreshScan is on.
SI_Shodan_FreshScanIntervalHours.whenToChange: When your schedule or Shodan credit budget calls for more or fewer scans.

SI_Shodan_LastFreshScanPath.label: Shodan last scan state file
SI_Shodan_LastFreshScanPath.purpose: Where the engine records when the last fresh Shodan scan finished.
SI_Shodan_LastFreshScanPath.defaultText: A file in the solution's data folder.
SI_Shodan_LastFreshScanPath.effect: The interval check reads this file. Pointing it somewhere that is lost between runs means scans may be re-submitted early, spending extra credits.
SI_Shodan_LastFreshScanPath.whenToChange: Only when the data folder is not kept between runs.

SI_Shodan_LookbackDays.label: Public IP discovery lookback
SI_Shodan_LookbackDays.purpose: How far back the engine looks in the endpoint and Azure profile tables to find classified assets with public IPs.
SI_Shodan_LookbackDays.effect: Each asset's latest snapshot within the window is used. A shorter window drops assets not seen recently; a longer one keeps retired assets in scope.
SI_Shodan_LookbackDays.whenToChange: When profiling runs less often than weekly.

SI_Shodan_PendingScansPath.label: Shodan pending scan state file
SI_Shodan_PendingScansPath.purpose: Where the engine remembers a submitted Shodan scan that has not finished yet.
SI_Shodan_PendingScansPath.defaultText: A file in the solution's data folder.
SI_Shodan_PendingScansPath.effect: The next run reads this file to collect the pending scan. If the file is lost between runs, the scan result is not picked up and a new scan may be submitted.
SI_Shodan_PendingScansPath.whenToChange: Only when the data folder is not kept between runs.

SI_Shodan_ScanPollIntervalSec.label: Shodan scan poll interval
SI_Shodan_ScanPollIntervalSec.purpose: How often the engine checks whether a submitted fresh Shodan scan has finished.
SI_Shodan_ScanPollIntervalSec.effect: Shorter checks notice completion sooner but make more status calls; longer checks may wait past completion. Only used with fresh scans on.
SI_Shodan_ScanPollIntervalSec.whenToChange: Rarely; the default suits most installs.

SI_Shodan_ScanWaitMaxSec.label: Shodan scan wait limit
SI_Shodan_ScanWaitMaxSec.purpose: How long one run waits for a submitted fresh Shodan scan to finish.
SI_Shodan_ScanWaitMaxSec.effect: Longer waits make the run take longer but finish more scans in the same run; if the limit passes, the run writes no rows and the next run collects the scan.
SI_Shodan_ScanWaitMaxSec.whenToChange: When scans routinely take longer than five minutes for your address count.

SI_Shodan_ServerOnly.label: Scan server IPs only
SI_Shodan_ServerOnly.purpose: Limits endpoint-derived public IPs to servers, because a workstation's public IP is usually a home or mobile network you do not own.
SI_Shodan_ServerOnly.defaultText: On: only servers' public IPs are checked.
SI_Shodan_ServerOnly.effect: Off adds workstation public IPs, which are mostly internet provider addresses: more lookups and results that do not describe your own exposure.

SI_Shodan_ThrottleMs.label: Shodan call spacing
SI_Shodan_ThrottleMs.purpose: Pause between live Shodan lookups so the engine stays within Shodan's rate limit.
SI_Shodan_ThrottleMs.effect: A lower value speeds up large runs but may hit Shodan's rate limit and cause failed lookups on lower plans. Cached lookups are not delayed.
SI_Shodan_ThrottleMs.whenToChange: Lower it only if your Shodan plan allows faster calls.

SI_Shodan_TierMax.label: Highest tier to check
SI_Shodan_TierMax.purpose: Checks public IPs only for assets at or below this privilege tier (0 is most critical).
SI_Shodan_TierMax.effect: Lowering it, for example to 1, checks only the most critical assets, cutting Shodan lookups and cost but leaving lower-tier exposure unchecked.
SI_Shodan_TierMax.whenToChange: To control Shodan cost on a small plan.

SI_Shodan_TimeoutSec.label: Shodan call timeout
SI_Shodan_TimeoutSec.purpose: How long each Shodan lookup or scan submission may take before it is abandoned.
SI_Shodan_TimeoutSec.effect: Longer timeouts tolerate a slow service at the cost of longer runs; shorter ones fail faster, leaving that address without Shodan data for the run.
SI_Shodan_TimeoutSec.whenToChange: Only if lookups time out on a slow network.

SI_ShodanCacheAgeDays.label: Shodan cache age
SI_ShodanCacheAgeDays.purpose: How long a stored Shodan result is reused before the address is looked up again.
SI_ShodanCacheAgeDays.effect: Shorter means fresher data but more live Shodan calls and longer runs; longer saves calls but results can be out of date.
SI_ShodanCacheAgeDays.whenToChange: When you need fresher exposure data or must save Shodan quota.

SI_ShodanMonthlyCreditCap.label: Shodan monthly credit cap
SI_ShodanMonthlyCreditCap.purpose: A safety ceiling on the Shodan scan credits spent per month, by per-address on-demand scans and by the batch fresh scan.
SI_ShodanMonthlyCreditCap.effect: A scan that would take the month past the cap is refused (the batch fresh scan counts one credit per address), and so is any scan while the month's count cannot be read. Normal host lookups are not limited.
SI_ShodanMonthlyCreditCap.whenToChange: Match it to your Shodan plan's monthly scan credits.

SI_SignalMap_PromptVersion.label: AI signal map version
SI_SignalMap_PromptVersion.purpose: A version label for the stored AI signal weights per engine and asset type; changing it makes the engines ask the AI again.
SI_SignalMap_PromptVersion.effect: A new value ignores the stored weights and rebuilds them with fresh AI calls on the next run, which adds AI cost once. Keeping the value reuses the stored weights.
SI_SignalMap_PromptVersion.whenToChange: Only when you want the AI signal weights rebuilt, for example after a model change.

SI_SignInBatchSize.label: Sign-in query batch size
SI_SignInBatchSize.purpose: How many users are looked up in one sign-in log query during identity sign-in enrichment.
SI_SignInBatchSize.effect: Larger batches mean fewer queries but each is heavier and may hit query size or memory limits; smaller batches are safer but slower.
SI_SignInBatchSize.whenToChange: Only if sign-in queries fail on size limits or run too slowly.

SI_SignInLookbackDays.label: Sign-in history window
SI_SignInLookbackDays.purpose: How many days of sign-in and device logon history the identity and endpoint enrichment look back over.
SI_SignInLookbackDays.effect: A longer window catches less frequent sign-ins and device users but makes the queries slower and costlier; a shorter one is cheaper but may miss occasional use.
SI_SignInLookbackDays.whenToChange: When weekly activity is too short a window for your users' patterns.

SI_SimulateCLRowCount.label: Simulated table row count
SI_SimulateCLRowCount.purpose: Test-only setting that pads the data Risk Analysis reads from your workspace with synthetic rows, to test behaviour at large scale on a small tenant.
SI_SimulateCLRowCount.effect: Risk Analysis handles the extra synthetic rows, so runs get slower and heavier; the fake rows never match real assets and do not appear in the report. A warning is shown while active.
SI_SimulateCLRowCount.whenToChange: Never in normal use; only for scale testing. Usually set by the launcher's asset-simulation option.

SI_SingleProcess.label: Keep stage data in memory
SI_SingleProcess.purpose: Makes the profiling engines pass data between stages in memory instead of through the staging storage account.
SI_SingleProcess.defaultText: Off: data between stages goes through staging storage.
SI_SingleProcess.effect: On a single server run this can be much faster. It must stay off for parallel container jobs, where each worker only sees its own memory.
SI_SingleProcess.whenToChange: Only for single-server troubleshooting or speed tests; leave off otherwise.

SI_Sinks_Azure.label: Azure collection outputs
SI_Sinks_Azure.purpose: Chooses where the Azure collection writes its results: Log Analytics (LA), JSON files and/or Excel files.
SI_Sinks_Azure.defaultText: All three: Log Analytics, JSON and Excel
SI_Sinks_Azure.effect: Leaving out LA means no Azure data in your workspace, so Risk Analysis and workbooks miss it; the collected records still go to the database. Leaving out JSON or Excel only saves local files and time.
SI_Sinks_Azure.whenToChange: Most installs never should; drop file outputs if nobody uses them.

SI_Sinks_Endpoint.label: Endpoint collection outputs
SI_Sinks_Endpoint.purpose: Chooses where the endpoint collection writes its results: Log Analytics (LA), JSON files and/or Excel files.
SI_Sinks_Endpoint.defaultText: All three: Log Analytics, JSON and Excel
SI_Sinks_Endpoint.effect: Leaving out LA means no endpoint data in your workspace, so Risk Analysis and workbooks miss it; the collected records still go to the database. Leaving out JSON or Excel only saves local files and time.
SI_Sinks_Endpoint.whenToChange: Most installs never should; drop file outputs if nobody uses them.

SI_Sinks_Identity.label: Identity collection outputs
SI_Sinks_Identity.purpose: Chooses where the identity collection writes its results: Log Analytics (LA), JSON files and/or Excel files.
SI_Sinks_Identity.defaultText: All three: Log Analytics, JSON and Excel
SI_Sinks_Identity.effect: Leaving out LA means no identity data in your workspace, so Risk Analysis and workbooks miss it; the collected records still go to the database. Leaving out JSON or Excel only saves local files and time.
SI_Sinks_Identity.whenToChange: Most installs never should; drop file outputs if nobody uses them.
