SI_Sinks_PublicIp.label: Public IP collection outputs
SI_Sinks_PublicIp.purpose: Chooses where the public IP collection writes its results: Log Analytics (LA), JSON files and/or Excel files.
SI_Sinks_PublicIp.defaultText: All three: Log Analytics, JSON and Excel
SI_Sinks_PublicIp.effect: Leaving out LA means no public IP data in your workspace, so Risk Analysis and workbooks miss it; the collected records still go to the database. Leaving out JSON or Excel only saves local files and time.
SI_Sinks_PublicIp.whenToChange: Most installs never should; drop file outputs if nobody uses them.

SI_SPN_AppId.label: Service principal app id
SI_SPN_AppId.purpose: Application (client) id of the service principal the engines sign in as when not using managed identity.
SI_SPN_AppId.defaultText: Taken from SpnClientId or the platform; if none, managed identity
SI_SPN_AppId.effect: Decides which app registration reads data and ingests results; that app needs the required Graph, Azure and Log Analytics permissions. Without it, no service principal sign-in happens.
SI_SPN_AppId.whenToChange: Set during setup when you use a service principal; change when moving to a different app.

SI_SPN_CertStoreLocation.label: Certificate store location
SI_SPN_CertStoreLocation.purpose: Which Windows certificate store (LocalMachine or CurrentUser) holds the sign-in certificate of the service principal.
SI_SPN_CertStoreLocation.defaultText: Detected: the store that holds the certificate with its key, else LocalMachine
SI_SPN_CertStoreLocation.effect: Forces the store used for certificate sign-in. A wrong store makes certificate sign-in fail. Containers always use CurrentUser.
SI_SPN_CertStoreLocation.whenToChange: Rarely; only if automatic detection picks the wrong store on your host.

SI_SPN_CertThumbprint.label: Sign-in certificate thumbprint
SI_SPN_CertThumbprint.purpose: Thumbprint of the service principal's certificate, with its private key in the certificate store, used for certificate sign-in.
SI_SPN_CertThumbprint.defaultText: Taken from the platform's certificate setting if present; else no certificate sign-in
SI_SPN_CertThumbprint.effect: Lets the engines, ingestion and SQL connections sign in with this certificate. A wrong or missing certificate makes certificate sign-in fail; with both certificate and secret set, the certificate is preferred.
SI_SPN_CertThumbprint.whenToChange: Set at install and when the certificate is renewed.

SI_SPN_ObjectId.label: Service principal object id
SI_SPN_ObjectId.purpose: Object id (not app id) of the service principal, used to grant it rights on data collection rules and storage.
SI_SPN_ObjectId.defaultText: Looked up from the app id at run start
SI_SPN_ObjectId.effect: If it cannot be found, infrastructure preparation is skipped and new data collection rules may lack the ingest permission. A wrong id grants rights to the wrong principal.
SI_SPN_ObjectId.whenToChange: Only when the automatic lookup fails because the signing-in identity cannot read service principals.

SI_SPN_Secret.label: Service principal client secret
SI_SPN_Secret.purpose: Client secret of the service principal when the sign-in method is Secret.
SI_SPN_Secret.defaultText: Not set: certificate or managed identity is used
SI_SPN_Secret.effect: Enables secret-based sign-in. If a certificate thumbprint is also set, the certificate wins and the secret is ignored. Secrets expire and must be rotated.
SI_SPN_Secret.whenToChange: Only when you cannot use managed identity or a certificate; rotate via your Key Vault procedure.

SI_SPN_TenantId.label: Service principal tenant id
SI_SPN_TenantId.purpose: The Entra tenant the service principal signs in to, for data reads and Log Analytics ingestion.
SI_SPN_TenantId.defaultText: Taken from SpnTenantId, the platform, or the managed identity's sign-in
SI_SPN_TenantId.effect: Decides which tenant is read. A wrong value makes sign-in fail or targets the wrong tenant.
SI_SPN_TenantId.whenToChange: Set during setup when you use a service principal.

SI_StagingPath.label: Risk Analysis local staging folder
SI_StagingPath.purpose: A local folder where Risk Analysis writes its temporary query files and query error details.
SI_StagingPath.defaultText: A staging folder under the output path, else the temp folder
SI_StagingPath.effect: Moves Risk Analysis's temporary query files to this folder. It does not change the staging storage account.
SI_StagingPath.whenToChange: Only if the default folder is not writable or too small on your host.

SI_StorageAccount.label: Staging storage account
SI_StorageAccount.purpose: The storage account the collection engines use for staging data, caches, the shared catalog and the identity ledger.
SI_StorageAccount.defaultText: Not set: collection engines stop with an error
SI_StorageAccount.effect: Required for endpoint, identity, Azure and public IP collection. It is reached only with the signed-in identity, which needs the Storage Blob, Queue and Table Data Contributor roles on it. Changing it starts staging and caches from empty.
SI_StorageAccount.whenToChange: Set at install; change only when moving to a new storage account.

SI_StorageResourceGroup.label: Storage account resource group
SI_StorageResourceGroup.purpose: Names the Azure resource group that holds the SecurityInsight storage account. Setup creates the account and grants its permissions there; a collection run only checks that the account is there.
SI_StorageResourceGroup.defaultText: Same resource group as the workspace (or the data collection rules)
SI_StorageResourceGroup.effect: Setup looks the storage account up, creates it and grants permissions in this resource group; a run that does not find it there says so in one line and creates nothing. A wrong value makes setup create a second account in the wrong place.
SI_StorageResourceGroup.whenToChange: Only when your storage account lives in a different resource group from the workspace; setup normally writes it.

SI_SystemPrompt_azure.label: Azure AI instructions
SI_SystemPrompt_azure.purpose: Replaces the built-in instructions sent to Azure OpenAI when it classifies Azure resources.
SI_SystemPrompt_azure.effect: Changes how AI decides tiers and service types for Azure resources. A poorly written prompt can produce wrong tiers or unreadable answers, which fall back to a default tier. Has no effect while AI is off for the Azure engine.
SI_SystemPrompt_azure.whenToChange: Rarely; only to tune AI classification for your estate.

SI_SystemPrompt_endpoint.label: Endpoint AI instructions
SI_SystemPrompt_endpoint.purpose: Replaces the built-in instructions sent to Azure OpenAI when it classifies devices.
SI_SystemPrompt_endpoint.effect: Changes how AI decides tiers and service types for devices. A poorly written prompt can produce wrong tiers or unreadable answers, which fall back to a default tier. Has no effect while AI is off for endpoints.
SI_SystemPrompt_endpoint.whenToChange: Rarely; only to tune AI classification for your estate.

SI_SystemPrompt_identity.label: Identity AI instructions
SI_SystemPrompt_identity.purpose: Reserved for replacing the AI instructions for identity classification.
SI_SystemPrompt_identity.defaultText: Not used; identity classification never uses AI.
SI_SystemPrompt_identity.effect: No effect today: the identity engine never calls AI, so this text is never sent.
SI_SystemPrompt_identity.whenToChange: Never at present; it is kept for future use.

SI_TableNamePattern.label: Profile table name pattern
SI_TableNamePattern.purpose: The pattern used to name each collection engine's Log Analytics table, where {0} is replaced by the engine name.
SI_TableNamePattern.effect: Changing it sends collection data to new tables; reports and workbooks expecting the standard names will not find the data.
SI_TableNamePattern.whenToChange: Only if you maintain a parallel naming scheme; most installs never should.

SI_TenantDomain.label: Tenant domain in mails and links
SI_TenantDomain.purpose: Tenant domain shown in report mail subjects and used in the Azure portal links Risk Analysis adds to findings on Azure resources.
SI_TenantDomain.defaultText: Read from Microsoft Graph for mail subjects; the tenant id is used in portal links
SI_TenantDomain.effect: Changes the domain in mail subjects and how Azure portal links are written; links work either way. A wrong domain mislabels the mails and opens links in the wrong directory.
SI_TenantDomain.whenToChange: Optional; set it if the run cannot read the domain from Microsoft Graph, or you prefer another domain in subjects and links.

SI_Telemetry_Enabled.label: Status reports to Invardia
SI_Telemetry_Enabled.purpose: Whether the install sends Invardia one status report a day and one short report per engine run: which engine ran, whether it ended ok, with warnings or failed, how long it took, the stage and the kind of error. Community reports are anonymous (a random install id; no tenant, host name or error text; counts only as ranges). Pro reports are identified by the install key and carry the error text with secrets removed.
SI_Telemetry_Enabled.effect: Off sends nothing at all: no report is built, no file is written and Invardia is never contacted for this. For Pro, Invardia then cannot see failed or silent runs and warn you about them.
SI_Telemetry_Enabled.whenToChange: Turn it off if your organisation does not allow status reports to leave the environment.

SI_Telemetry_SetupControls.label: Setup report to Invardia
SI_Telemetry_SetupControls.purpose: Pro installs with an install key send Invardia one setup report a day: a list of critical settings (updater, update ring, install key, licence, mail, permissions, last run, backup) with ok / missing / wrong / unknown, so Invardia can see what is not set up and help you. No secrets, no names of people and no error text are sent.
SI_Telemetry_SetupControls.defaultText: all: every control, SecurityInsight's own too (sent again with only the minimum list when Invardia does not take it)
SI_Telemetry_SetupControls.effect: 'all' (the default) sends the minimum list every product shares and SecurityInsight's own controls (SQL database reachable, job layout, run limits, last daily run, data sources, last CI build, Log Analytics ingestion, licence edition); when Invardia does not take that report, it is sent again once with only the minimum list, and the run log says so. 'minimum' sends only the minimum list. 'off' sends no setup report; the daily status report and the run reports are not affected. Status reports to Invardia off (SI_Telemetry_Enabled) turns this off too.
SI_Telemetry_SetupControls.whenToChange: Keep 'all'. Choose 'minimum' to send only the shared list, or 'off' if your organisation does not allow the setup state to leave the environment.
SI_Telemetry_SetupControls.hint: all = also SecurityInsight's own controls (default). minimum = the shared control list only. off = no setup report.

SI_Telemetry_SendEndpoints.label: Send this install's links to Invardia
SI_Telemetry_SendEndpoints.purpose: Pro installs with an install key can send Invardia this install's own links -- the web app's and the MCP server's addresses -- with the daily status report, so every mail Invardia sends about this environment carries an Open SecurityInsight button. Only the addresses are sent: no names, no secrets.
SI_Telemetry_SendEndpoints.defaultText: On -- switch it off to send no links
SI_Telemetry_SendEndpoints.effect: On: the daily status report carries the web app's and the MCP server's addresses (read from the install's own hosting). Off: it carries no links. A failed run's report links to the run health page either way.
SI_Telemetry_SendEndpoints.whenToChange: Switch it off only if Invardia should not see this install's web app and MCP addresses.

SI_GuardMail_Enabled.label: Mail when a safety check stops a step
SI_GuardMail_Enabled.purpose: Mails a person when a safety check holds, refuses or stops a step to protect your data -- for example when far more vulnerabilities would close than usual.
SI_GuardMail_Enabled.effect: Off sends no such mail: the event is still recorded in run health, on the Guards page of the Pro web app and in the audit trail, and still reported to Invardia when status reports are on. While a check keeps tripping, at most one mail a day is sent, saying how many times it happened.
SI_GuardMail_Enabled.whenToChange: Leave it on. Turn it off only if another system already watches these events for you.

SI_GuardMail_To.label: Safety-check mail recipients
SI_GuardMail_To.purpose: The addresses that receive the mail when a safety check holds, refuses or stops a step.
SI_GuardMail_To.defaultText: The report recipients (MailTo); without those, the SecurityInsight Pro SuperAdmins whose sign-in name is a mail address
SI_GuardMail_To.effect: These addresses get the mails instead of the report recipients.
SI_GuardMail_To.whenToChange: Set it to the team that runs SecurityInsight day to day, when that is not the team that reads the reports.
SI_GuardMail_To.hint: Empty: the default recipients, else the SuperAdmins.

SI_Pro_DataQuality_Mail_Enabled.label: Data-quality mail
SI_Pro_DataQuality_Mail_Enabled.purpose: One mail a day when a key number of the latest pipeline run is far off its usual range -- for example far fewer assets, a report with no rows, or risk factors suddenly missing.
SI_Pro_DataQuality_Mail_Enabled.effect: Off sends no data-quality mail: the warnings are still shown on Operations > Data quality and in Run health. Nothing is ever blocked by them either way.
SI_Pro_DataQuality_Mail_Enabled.whenToChange: Leave it on. Turn it off only if another system already watches these numbers for you.

SI_Pro_DataQuality_Mail_To.label: Data-quality mail recipients
SI_Pro_DataQuality_Mail_To.purpose: The addresses that receive the daily data-quality mail.
SI_Pro_DataQuality_Mail_To.defaultText: The safety-check mail recipients (SI_GuardMail_To); without those the report recipients (MailTo), else the SecurityInsight Pro SuperAdmins
SI_Pro_DataQuality_Mail_To.effect: These addresses get the data-quality mail instead of the default recipients.
SI_Pro_DataQuality_Mail_To.whenToChange: Set it to the people who change SecurityInsight's settings, so a setting that caused a drop is corrected quickly.

SI_Pro_DataQuality_AssetDropPercent.label: Data quality: asset drop
SI_Pro_DataQuality_AssetDropPercent.purpose: When the assets of a source (Defender for Endpoint, Entra ID, Azure, public IPs) or the active CIs fall this many percent or more below the median of the last 3 runs, it is shown as a data-quality warning.
SI_Pro_DataQuality_AssetDropPercent.effect: Lower warns about smaller drops; higher only about large ones. A warning never blocks anything.
SI_Pro_DataQuality_AssetDropPercent.whenToChange: Raise it when the number of assets moves a lot from day to day on purpose.

SI_Pro_DataQuality_ReportDropPercent.label: Data quality: report drop
SI_Pro_DataQuality_ReportDropPercent.purpose: When a Risk Analysis report has 0 rows, or falls this many percent or more below the median of the last 3 runs, it is shown as a data-quality warning -- the sign of a query that suddenly returns nothing.
SI_Pro_DataQuality_ReportDropPercent.effect: Lower warns about smaller drops; higher only about large ones. A report at 0 rows always warns. A warning never blocks anything.
SI_Pro_DataQuality_ReportDropPercent.whenToChange: Raise it when your reports shrink a lot on purpose (a large remediation round).

SI_Pro_DataQuality_FillDropPoints.label: Data quality: column fill drop
SI_Pro_DataQuality_FillDropPoints.purpose: When the share of rows that carry a key value -- the probability and consequence risk factors, the tier, the SQL tag, and the CIs' asset type and owner -- falls this many percentage points or more below the median of the last 3 runs, it is shown as a data-quality warning.
SI_Pro_DataQuality_FillDropPoints.effect: Lower warns about smaller drops in fill; higher only about large ones. A warning never blocks anything.
SI_Pro_DataQuality_FillDropPoints.whenToChange: Lower it if you want to hear early about owners or factors going missing.

SI_Pro_DataQuality_TierShiftPercent.label: Data quality: tier shift
SI_Pro_DataQuality_TierShiftPercent.purpose: When the active CIs in a tier (0 to 3) change by this share of all active CIs or more compared with the median of the last 3 runs -- or the CIs about to retire rise by it -- it is shown as a data-quality warning. The typical cause: a customised rule that moved all servers to one tier.
SI_Pro_DataQuality_TierShiftPercent.effect: Lower warns about smaller moves between tiers; higher only about large ones. A warning never blocks anything.
SI_Pro_DataQuality_TierShiftPercent.whenToChange: Raise it while you re-tier your estate on purpose.

SI_Pro_SourceDropout_AssetDropAction.label: Far fewer assets from a source: what to do
SI_Pro_SourceDropout_AssetDropAction.purpose: What happens when a source's collection completes with far fewer assets than its last good collection (down by the data-quality asset drop limit or more). That can be a real clean-up, for example many Azure resources removed, or a source that answered only in part.
SI_Pro_SourceDropout_AssetDropAction.effect: confirm: the last good collection is kept (nothing is marked not seen), the run goes on, and the drop is accepted by itself when the next complete collection of that source shows the same level -- a real clean-up takes effect one run later. accept: the collection is taken as it comes and the safety check only reports it.
SI_Pro_SourceDropout_AssetDropAction.whenToChange: Set accept when large clean-ups are normal for you and must show at once.

SI_Pro_LifecycleStaleOpenRepair.label: One-time repair of stale finding records
SI_Pro_LifecycleStaleOpenRepair.purpose: A one-time clean-up of the finding history. Before a fix of October 2026, a finding that no CI held could be closed as no longer monitored when it had only moved to a CI, and such a finding could stay open under its old asset key. This repair puts those records right once.
SI_Pro_LifecycleStaleOpenRepair.effect: off: nothing. count: nothing is changed; the data sync's log says how many finding records the repair would change and what they would become. apply: once, after a complete collection -- a record whose CI id is empty gets none (nothing visible changes), and a finding still open under an old asset key that the newest collection reports open under its CI is closed as rekeyed (the same finding, now under its CI; not a fix). Nothing is deleted; every other record goes through the usual rule.
SI_Pro_LifecycleStaleOpenRepair.whenToChange: Only when support asks for it: first count, then apply. It is removed in a later release once it has run everywhere.

SI_Guard_CollectionSourceAssetDrop_Enabl.label: Collection: far fewer assets from one source
SI_Guard_CollectionSourceAssetDrop_Enabl.purpose: The safety check that protects your configuration items (CIs) and everything calculated from them: One source returned far fewer assets than in its last good collection, although the collection completed.
SI_Guard_CollectionSourceAssetDrop_Enabl.effect: Off: a collection with far fewer assets is taken as it comes -- the assets the source no longer lists are marked not seen at once, and their CIs retire after the usual days. On: the check works as described on the Guards page.
SI_Guard_CollectionSourceAssetDrop_Enabl.whenToChange: Leave it on. Turn it off only when this check keeps stopping work you know is right -- read what Off means first.

SI_Guard_CollectionSourceAssetDrop_Mail.label: Collection: far fewer assets from one source: mail
SI_Guard_CollectionSourceAssetDrop_Mail.purpose: Whether this safety check sends a mail when it trips.
SI_Guard_CollectionSourceAssetDrop_Mail.defaultText: On (follows the check: nothing is mailed while the check is off)
SI_Guard_CollectionSourceAssetDrop_Mail.effect: Off: the event is still shown on the Guards page and kept in run health and the audit trail, but no mail is sent for it. The install-wide switch "Mail when a safety check stops a step" still applies to every check.
SI_Guard_CollectionSourceAssetDrop_Mail.whenToChange: Turn it off for a check whose mails you do not need, instead of turning the check off.

SI_Guard_CiBuildConcurrent_Enabled.label: CI build started while another was running
SI_Guard_CiBuildConcurrent_Enabled.purpose: The safety check that protects your configuration items (CIs) from being written by two builds at the same time: A CI build was started while another CI build was still running.
SI_Guard_CiBuildConcurrent_Enabled.effect: Off: no event. The second CI build still waits for the first one, because two builds never write the CIs at the same time. On: the check works as described on the Guards page.
SI_Guard_CiBuildConcurrent_Enabled.whenToChange: Leave it on: it only reports, and nothing is stopped by it. Turn it off when you do not need to know that a CI build had to wait.

SI_Guard_CiBuildConcurrent_Mail.label: CI build started while another was running: mail
SI_Guard_CiBuildConcurrent_Mail.purpose: Whether this safety check sends a mail when it trips.
SI_Guard_CiBuildConcurrent_Mail.defaultText: On (follows the check: nothing is mailed while the check is off)
SI_Guard_CiBuildConcurrent_Mail.effect: This check only reports and stops nothing, so it sends no mail either way: the event is shown on the Guards page and kept in run health and the audit trail.
SI_Guard_CiBuildConcurrent_Mail.whenToChange: Nothing to change: a check that only reports is not mailed.

SI_Pro_Pipeline_GoOnAfterFailedStep.label: Failed step: show what was collected all the same
SI_Pro_Pipeline_GoOnAfterFailedStep.purpose: When the correlation or Risk Analysis fails after the collections completed, the data sync and the verification still run on what is stored, so the web app shows what was collected instead of nothing. The run is marked as not complete and says what is missing.
SI_Pro_Pipeline_GoOnAfterFailedStep.effect: Off holds every step after a failed one until the next good run, as before: a new install then shows nothing until its first run completes. On or off, nothing is closed, no ticket is changed and no mail is sent from a run that is not complete.
SI_Pro_Pipeline_GoOnAfterFailedStep.whenToChange: Leave it on. Turn it off only if the web app must never show data of a run in which a step failed.

SI_Pro_PublishPartialRun.label: Show a run in which a report fell back to an earlier result
SI_Pro_PublishPartialRun.purpose: Every page shows one run: the last run that completed in full. A run in which a report could not be completed and fell back to its last complete result is not shown by default -- the pages keep the last complete run, so nothing on a page is from two runs.
SI_Pro_PublishPartialRun.effect: On: such a run is shown, marked "a part of this run is from an earlier result". Off: the pages keep the last complete run until a run completes in full.
SI_Pro_PublishPartialRun.whenToChange: Leave it off. Turn it on only when a report keeps failing and the rest of the newest run must be shown all the same.

SI_Pro_Pipeline_FirstRunRestarts.label: First collection: restarts of a failed step
SI_Pro_Pipeline_FirstRunRestarts.purpose: On a new install's first collection, a step that fails or is stopped is started again at once and carries on from what it finished, this many times. After that the run ends with a warning that names the step and who must act.
SI_Pro_Pipeline_FirstRunRestarts.effect: Higher tries more often before the first collection ends with a warning; 0 means a failed step is not started again. Only the steps that collect, correlate and load the web app are started again -- never a step that writes to a CMDB, to ServiceNow or to a ticket. It has no effect after the first complete collection.
SI_Pro_Pipeline_FirstRunRestarts.whenToChange: Leave it at 2. Set 0 only when a failed step of the first collection must be looked at before anything is started again.

SI_Pro_SourceDropout_HoldDeliveryDays.label: Source down: days until delivery waits
SI_Pro_SourceDropout_HoldDeliveryDays.purpose: When the collection of one source (identities, Azure resources, endpoints, the public IP scan) fails, the run goes on with that source's last good collection and says how old it is. When a source has had no good collection for this many days or more, delivery waits: no mail is sent and no ticket is changed until that source collects again.
SI_Pro_SourceDropout_HoldDeliveryDays.effect: Lower makes delivery wait sooner; higher lets mails and ticket updates go out longer on older data. 0 means delivery never waits for a source. The calculation always goes on, and nothing is closed or retired because a source is down.
SI_Pro_SourceDropout_HoldDeliveryDays.whenToChange: Raise it when a source is known to be down for longer and the mails should keep going out meanwhile.

SI_DataHealth_Enabled.label: Data health check
SI_DataHealth_Enabled.purpose: Every day SecurityInsight checks its own data: a random 10% of each source's records (at least 50) are read from the source and looked up in the newest collection, and a random 10% of the devices with vulnerability findings are asked again from Defender. It only reads. Three anomalous days in a row make the data Unhealthy, one good day makes it Healthy again; while Unhealthy nothing is sent out unless a SuperAdmin lets a channel through.
SI_DataHealth_Enabled.effect: Off: nothing is checked, the state is no longer updated and nothing is held because of data health. On: the check runs with the verification job every day.
SI_DataHealth_Enabled.whenToChange: Keep it on. Switch it off only for a short time while Microsoft support confirms a problem in a source.

SI_DataHealth_Margin_EntraUsers.label: Data health margin: Entra users
SI_DataHealth_Margin_EntraUsers.purpose: How many of the checked Entra users may be missing from the newest collection or differ from Entra before the day counts as anomalous, as a percent of the users checked (never fewer than the minimum records below).
SI_DataHealth_Margin_EntraUsers.effect: Higher tolerates more differences before the data turns Unhealthy; lower turns it Unhealthy sooner.
SI_DataHealth_Margin_EntraUsers.whenToChange: Raise it only when the users change so fast that the daily check sees normal changes as differences.

SI_DataHealth_Margin_EntraApps.label: Data health margin: Entra apps and service principals
SI_DataHealth_Margin_EntraApps.purpose: How many of the checked Entra apps and service principals may be missing from the newest collection or differ from Entra before the day counts as anomalous, as a percent of those checked (never fewer than the minimum records below).
SI_DataHealth_Margin_EntraApps.effect: Higher tolerates more differences before the data turns Unhealthy; lower turns it Unhealthy sooner.
SI_DataHealth_Margin_EntraApps.whenToChange: Raise it only when apps are added and removed so often that normal changes count as differences.

SI_DataHealth_Margin_Devices.label: Data health margin: Defender devices
SI_DataHealth_Margin_Devices.purpose: How many of the checked Defender for Endpoint devices may be missing from the newest collection or differ from Defender before the day counts as anomalous, as a percent of the devices checked (never fewer than the minimum records below).
SI_DataHealth_Margin_Devices.effect: Higher tolerates more differences before the data turns Unhealthy; lower turns it Unhealthy sooner.
SI_DataHealth_Margin_Devices.whenToChange: Raise it only when many devices are onboarded or removed every day.

SI_DataHealth_Margin_Azure.label: Data health margin: Azure resources
SI_DataHealth_Margin_Azure.purpose: How many of the checked Azure resources may be missing from the newest collection or differ from Azure before the day counts as anomalous, as a percent of the resources checked (never fewer than the minimum records below).
SI_DataHealth_Margin_Azure.effect: Higher tolerates more differences before the data turns Unhealthy; lower turns it Unhealthy sooner.
SI_DataHealth_Margin_Azure.whenToChange: Raise it only when resources are created and deleted all day (for example short-lived test environments).

SI_DataHealth_Margin_DefenderForCloud.label: Data health margin: Defender for Cloud recommendations
SI_DataHealth_Margin_DefenderForCloud.purpose: How many of the checked resources with Defender for Cloud recommendations may be missing from the newest collection or have a different number of open recommendations before the day counts as anomalous, as a percent of those checked (never fewer than the minimum records below).
SI_DataHealth_Margin_DefenderForCloud.effect: Higher tolerates more differences before the data turns Unhealthy; lower turns it Unhealthy sooner.
SI_DataHealth_Margin_DefenderForCloud.whenToChange: Raise it only when Defender for Cloud re-evaluates many resources between the collection and the check.

SI_DataHealth_Margin_Vulnerabilities.label: Data health margin: vulnerabilities
SI_DataHealth_Margin_Vulnerabilities.purpose: How many of the vulnerabilities Defender reports for the checked devices may be missing from SecurityInsight's findings before the day counts as anomalous, as a percent of those vulnerabilities (never fewer than the minimum records below).
SI_DataHealth_Margin_Vulnerabilities.effect: Higher tolerates more differences before the data turns Unhealthy; lower turns it Unhealthy sooner.
SI_DataHealth_Margin_Vulnerabilities.whenToChange: Raise it when vulnerabilities are left out on purpose (excluded vulnerabilities, a minimum age) and the check counts them.

SI_DataHealth_Margin_RiskAnalysis.label: Data health margin: Risk Analysis reports
SI_DataHealth_Margin_RiskAnalysis.purpose: Per Risk Analysis report with vulnerability findings: how many of the checked findings may differ from what Defender reports now (missing, or no longer reported) before the day counts as anomalous, as a percent of those checked (never fewer than the minimum records below).
SI_DataHealth_Margin_RiskAnalysis.effect: Higher tolerates more differences before the data turns Unhealthy; lower turns it Unhealthy sooner.
SI_DataHealth_Margin_RiskAnalysis.whenToChange: Raise it only when devices are patched so often that findings fixed since the run count as differences.

SI_DataHealth_MarginMinimum.label: Data health margin: minimum records
SI_DataHealth_MarginMinimum.purpose: The fewest differences any data health margin allows, whatever its percent -- so a small source does not turn the data Unhealthy over one or two records.
SI_DataHealth_MarginMinimum.effect: Higher tolerates more differences in small sources; lower makes small sources stricter.

SI_Telemetry_SendHealth.label: Send the data health result to Invardia
SI_Telemetry_SendHealth.purpose: Pro installs with an install key send Invardia the daily data health result -- the state and, per source and report, how many records were checked, found, missing and different. Counts only: no names, ids or values.
SI_Telemetry_SendHealth.defaultText: On -- switch it off to send nothing about data health
SI_Telemetry_SendHealth.effect: On: every daily check, and at once when the state changes, the counts go to Invardia, which uses them to hold an update ring from moving on. Off: nothing about data health is sent.
SI_Telemetry_SendHealth.whenToChange: Keep it on. Switch it off only if your organisation does not allow the data health counts to leave the environment.

SI_Guards_Enabled.label: All guards (safety checks)
SI_Guards_Enabled.purpose: One switch for every safety check that holds, refuses or stops a step to protect your data (the list below and the Guards page).
SI_Guards_Enabled.effect: WARNING -- Off turns EVERY safety check off at once: SecurityInsight then closes vulnerability records, retires CIs, hands over batches and loads collections even when the data looks broken or incomplete, so a failed collection can close or retire everything it no longer sees. Nothing is held for release and no guard mail is sent; each check says once in its job log that it is off. The checks that only report a stop SecurityInsight cannot skip (the source failed, the licence) stop reporting it. On: every check works as set below.
SI_Guards_Enabled.whenToChange: Leave it on. Turn it off only for a short time, when the checks stop work you know is right -- and prefer turning off or tuning the one check that is in the way.
SI_Guards_Enabled.hint: Off = every check below is off.

SI_VulnSync_MaxClosePercent.label: Vulnerability close limit (% of open records)
SI_VulnSync_MaxClosePercent.purpose: The largest share of the open vulnerability records the connector may close in one run before it holds the closes for an Admin to release.
SI_VulnSync_MaxClosePercent.effect: A run that would close more than this share of the open records closes none of them and holds them (Guards page: release once). Only the records that really close count -- not first absences, held or out-of-scope records, and not closes a fresh Defender assessment confirms.
SI_VulnSync_MaxClosePercent.whenToChange: Raise it if your patch rounds regularly fix more than this share at once.

SI_VulnSync_MaxCloseAbsolute.label: Vulnerability close limit (number of records)
SI_VulnSync_MaxCloseAbsolute.purpose: An optional limit on HOW MANY vulnerability records the connector may close in one run, on top of the share above.
SI_VulnSync_MaxCloseAbsolute.defaultText: 0 = no limit on the number (only the share counts)
SI_VulnSync_MaxCloseAbsolute.effect: 0: only the share of the open records decides -- a patch round that closes hundreds of records out of thousands goes through. Above 0: a run that would close more records than this is held as well.
SI_VulnSync_MaxCloseAbsolute.whenToChange: Leave it at 0 for vulnerabilities. Set a number only if you want a hard cap regardless of the size of your estate.

SI_VulnSync_CollapseFloor.label: Vulnerabilities: share that must still be reported
SI_VulnSync_CollapseFloor.purpose: The share (0 to 1) of the open vulnerability records the newest results must still report before anything may close.
SI_VulnSync_CollapseFloor.effect: When fewer of the open records are still reported, the run looks like a partial collection and closes nothing. 0 switches this check off; 1 forbids every close.
SI_VulnSync_CollapseFloor.whenToChange: Lower it if your estate legitimately shrinks a lot between runs.

SI_Guard_VulnConnectorCloseCeiling_Enabl.label: Vulnerability close limit
SI_Guard_VulnConnectorCloseCeiling_Enabl.purpose: The safety check that protects open vulnerability records: SecurityInsight would have closed far more vulnerability records in one run than it allows, so it closed none.
SI_Guard_VulnConnectorCloseCeiling_Enabl.effect: Off: the step goes on as if the check had not tripped -- the vulnerability connector closes every record the run would close, however many; nothing is held for release. On: the check works as described on the Guards page.
SI_Guard_VulnConnectorCloseCeiling_Enabl.whenToChange: Off by default: only the two brakes stay on (CIs retired by mistake, duplicate vulnerability records) -- this check is a warning you can switch on. Turn it on when you want it to hold or stop the step, and mail, again.

SI_Guard_VulnConnectorCloseCeiling_Mail.label: Vulnerability close limit: mail
SI_Guard_VulnConnectorCloseCeiling_Mail.purpose: Whether this safety check sends a mail when it trips.
SI_Guard_VulnConnectorCloseCeiling_Mail.defaultText: On (follows the check: nothing is mailed while the check is off)
SI_Guard_VulnConnectorCloseCeiling_Mail.effect: Off: the event is still shown on the Guards page and kept in run health and the audit trail, but no mail is sent for it. The install-wide switch "Mail when a safety check stops a step" still applies to every check.
SI_Guard_VulnConnectorCloseCeiling_Mail.whenToChange: Turn it off for a check whose mails you do not need, instead of turning the check off.

SI_Guard_VulnConnectorEmptySnapshot_Enab.label: Vulnerabilities: empty result
SI_Guard_VulnConnectorEmptySnapshot_Enab.purpose: The safety check that protects open vulnerability records: The newest Risk Analysis results held no vulnerabilities while records are still open, so nothing was closed.
SI_Guard_VulnConnectorEmptySnapshot_Enab.effect: Off: the step goes on as if the check had not tripped -- an EMPTY result closes the open records it no longer reports, so a failed collection can close every open vulnerability. On: the check works as described on the Guards page.
SI_Guard_VulnConnectorEmptySnapshot_Enab.whenToChange: Off by default: only the two brakes stay on (CIs retired by mistake, duplicate vulnerability records) -- this check is a warning you can switch on. Turn it on when you want it to hold or stop the step, and mail, again.

SI_Guard_VulnConnectorEmptySnapshot_Mail.label: Vulnerabilities: empty result: mail
SI_Guard_VulnConnectorEmptySnapshot_Mail.purpose: Whether this safety check sends a mail when it trips.
SI_Guard_VulnConnectorEmptySnapshot_Mail.defaultText: On (follows the check: nothing is mailed while the check is off)
SI_Guard_VulnConnectorEmptySnapshot_Mail.effect: Off: the event is still shown on the Guards page and kept in run health and the audit trail, but no mail is sent for it. The install-wide switch "Mail when a safety check stops a step" still applies to every check.
SI_Guard_VulnConnectorEmptySnapshot_Mail.whenToChange: Turn it off for a check whose mails you do not need, instead of turning the check off.

SI_Guard_VulnConnectorCollapse_Enabled.label: Vulnerabilities: result far smaller than usual
SI_Guard_VulnConnectorCollapse_Enabled.purpose: The safety check that protects open vulnerability records: Far fewer of the open vulnerability records are still reported than usual, which looks like a partial collection rather than a real fix, so nothing was closed.
SI_Guard_VulnConnectorCollapse_Enabled.effect: Off: the step goes on as if the check had not tripped -- a result that lost most of its findings closes the records it no longer reports. On: the check works as described on the Guards page.
SI_Guard_VulnConnectorCollapse_Enabled.whenToChange: Off by default: only the two brakes stay on (CIs retired by mistake, duplicate vulnerability records) -- this check is a warning you can switch on. Turn it on when you want it to hold or stop the step, and mail, again.

SI_Guard_VulnConnectorCollapse_Mail.label: Vulnerabilities: result far smaller than usual: mail
SI_Guard_VulnConnectorCollapse_Mail.purpose: Whether this safety check sends a mail when it trips.
SI_Guard_VulnConnectorCollapse_Mail.defaultText: On (follows the check: nothing is mailed while the check is off)
SI_Guard_VulnConnectorCollapse_Mail.effect: Off: the event is still shown on the Guards page and kept in run health and the audit trail, but no mail is sent for it. The install-wide switch "Mail when a safety check stops a step" still applies to every check.
SI_Guard_VulnConnectorCollapse_Mail.whenToChange: Turn it off for a check whose mails you do not need, instead of turning the check off.

SI_Guard_VulnConnectorScopeChanged_Enabl.label: Vulnerabilities: scope changed
SI_Guard_VulnConnectorScopeChanged_Enabl.purpose: The safety check that protects open vulnerability records: The scope of the collection changed, so records that dropped out of it were not closed.
SI_Guard_VulnConnectorScopeChanged_Enabl.effect: Off: the step goes on as if the check had not tripped -- records that dropped out of the collection scope are closed like any other absent record. On: the check works as described on the Guards page.
SI_Guard_VulnConnectorScopeChanged_Enabl.whenToChange: Off by default: only the two brakes stay on (CIs retired by mistake, duplicate vulnerability records) -- this check is a warning you can switch on. Turn it on when you want it to hold or stop the step, and mail, again.

SI_Guard_VulnConnectorScopeChanged_Mail.label: Vulnerabilities: scope changed: mail
SI_Guard_VulnConnectorScopeChanged_Mail.purpose: Whether this safety check sends a mail when it trips.
SI_Guard_VulnConnectorScopeChanged_Mail.defaultText: On (follows the check: nothing is mailed while the check is off)
SI_Guard_VulnConnectorScopeChanged_Mail.effect: Off: the event is still shown on the Guards page and kept in run health and the audit trail, but no mail is sent for it. The install-wide switch "Mail when a safety check stops a step" still applies to every check.
SI_Guard_VulnConnectorScopeChanged_Mail.whenToChange: Turn it off for a check whose mails you do not need, instead of turning the check off.

SI_Guard_VulnConnectorRunIncomplete_Enab.label: Vulnerabilities: Risk Analysis run not finished
SI_Guard_VulnConnectorRunIncomplete_Enab.purpose: The safety check that protects open vulnerability records: The Risk Analysis run behind these results did not finish cleanly, so nothing was closed.
SI_Guard_VulnConnectorRunIncomplete_Enab.effect: Off: the step goes on as if the check had not tripped -- records are closed even when the Risk Analysis run behind the results did not finish cleanly. On: the check works as described on the Guards page.
SI_Guard_VulnConnectorRunIncomplete_Enab.whenToChange: Off by default: only the two brakes stay on (CIs retired by mistake, duplicate vulnerability records) -- this check is a warning you can switch on. Turn it on when you want it to hold or stop the step, and mail, again.

SI_Guard_VulnConnectorRunIncomplete_Mail.label: Vulnerabilities: Risk Analysis run not finished: mail
SI_Guard_VulnConnectorRunIncomplete_Mail.purpose: Whether this safety check sends a mail when it trips.
SI_Guard_VulnConnectorRunIncomplete_Mail.defaultText: On (follows the check: nothing is mailed while the check is off)
SI_Guard_VulnConnectorRunIncomplete_Mail.effect: Off: the event is still shown on the Guards page and kept in run health and the audit trail, but no mail is sent for it. The install-wide switch "Mail when a safety check stops a step" still applies to every check.
SI_Guard_VulnConnectorRunIncomplete_Mail.whenToChange: Turn it off for a check whose mails you do not need, instead of turning the check off.

SI_Guard_VulnConnectorSnapshotIncomplete.label: Vulnerabilities: results not known to be complete
SI_Guard_VulnConnectorSnapshotIncomplete.purpose: The safety check that protects open vulnerability records: The newest Risk Analysis results are not known to be complete, so findings were opened and updated but nothing was closed.
SI_Guard_VulnConnectorSnapshotIncomplete.effect: Off: the step goes on as if the check had not tripped -- absences are counted and records closed even when the newest results are not known to be complete. On: the check works as described on the Guards page.
SI_Guard_VulnConnectorSnapshotIncomplete.whenToChange: Off by default: only the two brakes stay on (CIs retired by mistake, duplicate vulnerability records) -- this check is a warning you can switch on. Turn it on when you want it to hold or stop the step, and mail, again.

SI_Guard_VulnConnectorSnapshotIncomplete.label: Vulnerabilities: results not known to be complete: mail
SI_Guard_VulnConnectorSnapshotIncomplete.purpose: Whether this safety check sends a mail when it trips.
SI_Guard_VulnConnectorSnapshotIncomplete.defaultText: On (follows the check: nothing is mailed while the check is off)
SI_Guard_VulnConnectorSnapshotIncomplete.effect: Off: the event is still shown on the Guards page and kept in run health and the audit trail, but no mail is sent for it. The install-wide switch "Mail when a safety check stops a step" still applies to every check.
SI_Guard_VulnConnectorSnapshotIncomplete.whenToChange: Turn it off for a check whose mails you do not need, instead of turning the check off.

SI_Guard_VulnConnectorTargetIncomplete_E.label: Vulnerabilities: target not read in full
SI_Guard_VulnConnectorTargetIncomplete_E.purpose: The safety check that protects your vulnerability target from duplicate records: The vulnerability target (for example the ServiceNow table) could not be read in full, so nothing was written: every record the read missed would have been opened again as a duplicate.
SI_Guard_VulnConnectorTargetIncomplete_E.effect: Off: no event and no mail. The step itself still stops, because writing after a partial read of the target would open every record the read missed again as a duplicate. On: the check works as described on the Guards page.

SI_Guard_SchemaGateRefused_Mail.defaultText: On (follows the check: nothing is mailed while the check is off)
SI_Guard_SchemaGateRefused_Mail.effect: Off: the event is still shown on the Guards page and kept in run health and the audit trail, but no mail is sent for it. The install-wide switch "Mail when a safety check stops a step" still applies to every check.
SI_Guard_SchemaGateRefused_Mail.whenToChange: Turn it off for a check whose mails you do not need, instead of turning the check off.

SI_Guard_UpdateSchemaFailed_Enabled.label: Update: database update failed
SI_Guard_UpdateSchemaFailed_Enabled.purpose: The safety check that protects your SecurityInsight installation from running a new version on an old database: An update stopped before it changed anything, because the new version's database changes could not be applied.
SI_Guard_UpdateSchemaFailed_Enabled.effect: Off: no event and no mail. The step itself still stops, because the database update failed. On: the check works as described on the Guards page.
SI_Guard_UpdateSchemaFailed_Enabled.whenToChange: Off by default: only the two brakes stay on (CIs retired by mistake, duplicate vulnerability records) -- this check is a warning you can switch on. Turn it on when you want it to hold or stop the step, and mail, again.

SI_Guard_UpdateSchemaFailed_Mail.label: Update: database update failed: mail

SI_Guard_LicenceStateInvalid_Enabled.label: Licence not valid
SI_Guard_LicenceStateInvalid_Enabled.purpose: The safety check that protects the SecurityInsight Pro features: The SecurityInsight Pro licence does not verify (it has expired or is not valid for this install), so the Pro jobs did not run.
SI_Guard_LicenceStateInvalid_Enabled.effect: Off: no event and no mail. The step itself still stops, because the licence, not this switch, decides which Pro features run. On: the check works as described on the Guards page.
SI_Guard_LicenceStateInvalid_Enabled.whenToChange: Off by default: only the two brakes stay on (CIs retired by mistake, duplicate vulnerability records) -- this check is a warning you can switch on. Turn it on when you want it to hold or stop the step, and mail, again.

SI_Guard_LicenceStateGrace_Enabled.label: Licence grace period
SI_Guard_LicenceStateGrace_Enabled.purpose: The safety check that protects the SecurityInsight Pro features: The SecurityInsight Pro licence is in its grace period.
SI_Guard_LicenceStateGrace_Enabled.effect: Off: no event and no mail during the licence grace period; everything keeps running. On: the check works as described on the Guards page.
SI_Guard_LicenceStateGrace_Enabled.whenToChange: Off by default: only the two brakes stay on (CIs retired by mistake, duplicate vulnerability records) -- this check is a warning you can switch on. Turn it on when you want it to hold or stop the step, and mail, again.

SI_Guard_LicenceStateGrace_Mail.whenToChange: Turn it off for a check whose mails you do not need, instead of turning the check off.

SI_Guard_AuditRetentionRefused_Enabled.label: Audit trail retention setting
SI_Guard_AuditRetentionRefused_Enabled.purpose: The safety check that protects the audit trail: The audit trail retention setting (SI_Pro_AuditRetentionMonths) is not a whole number of at least 13 months, so nothing was removed.
SI_Guard_AuditRetentionRefused_Enabled.effect: Off: no event and no mail. The step itself still stops, because the retention setting is not valid. On: the check works as described on the Guards page.
SI_Guard_AuditRetentionRefused_Enabled.whenToChange: Off by default: only the two brakes stay on (CIs retired by mistake, duplicate vulnerability records) -- this check is a warning you can switch on. Turn it on when you want it to hold or stop the step, and mail, again.

SI_Guard_AuditRetentionRefused_Mail.label: Audit trail retention setting: mail
SI_Guard_AuditRetentionRefused_Mail.purpose: Whether this safety check sends a mail when it trips.
SI_Guard_AuditRetentionRefused_Mail.defaultText: On (follows the check: nothing is mailed while the check is off)
SI_Guard_AuditRetentionRefused_Mail.effect: Off: the event is still shown on the Guards page and kept in run health and the audit trail, but no mail is sent for it. The install-wide switch "Mail when a safety check stops a step" still applies to every check.
SI_Guard_AuditRetentionRefused_Mail.whenToChange: Turn it off for a check whose mails you do not need, instead of turning the check off.

SI_Guard_ExemptionBulkRefused_Enabled.label: Bulk exemption limit
SI_Guard_ExemptionBulkRefused_Enabled.purpose: The safety check that protects your findings from being exempted in bulk by mistake: A request to exempt or change many findings at once was refused (no narrowing filter, or more findings than the limit allows).
SI_Guard_ExemptionBulkRefused_Enabled.effect: Off: no event and no mail. The request itself is still refused, because a whole collection is never exempted in one go -- raise the limit instead (Settings > Exemptions: Most findings in one bulk exemption request, up to 2,000). On: the check works as described on the Guards page.
SI_Guard_ExemptionBulkRefused_Enabled.whenToChange: Off by default: only the two brakes stay on (CIs retired by mistake, duplicate vulnerability records) -- this check is a warning you can switch on. Turn it on when you want it to hold or stop the step, and mail, again.

SI_Guard_ExemptionBulkRefused_Mail.label: Bulk exemption limit: mail

SI_Guard_FlowRunCatchUp_Enabled.label: Daily flow: start held for the previous run
SI_Guard_FlowRunCatchUp_Enabled.purpose: The safety check that protects the order of the daily jobs: A scheduled start of the daily job flow was held because the previous run was still running; it ran once as soon as that run finished.
SI_Guard_FlowRunCatchUp_Enabled.effect: Off: no event and no mail; the daily flow still waits for its previous run. On: the check works as described on the Guards page.
SI_Guard_FlowRunCatchUp_Enabled.whenToChange: Off by default: only the two brakes stay on (CIs retired by mistake, duplicate vulnerability records) -- this check is a warning you can switch on. Turn it on when you want it to hold or stop the step, and mail, again.

SI_Guard_FlowRunCatchUp_Mail.purpose: Whether this safety check sends a mail when it trips.

SI_Guard_FlowRunCatchUp_Mail.whenToChange: Turn it off for a check whose mails you do not need, instead of turning the check off.

SI_Guard_FlowStepSkipped_Enabled.label: Daily flow: jobs skipped
SI_Guard_FlowStepSkipped_Enabled.purpose: The safety check that protects the jobs that depend on an earlier job: One or more jobs in the daily flow were skipped because a job they need did not succeed.
SI_Guard_FlowStepSkipped_Enabled.effect: Off: no event and no mail; jobs that need a failed job are still skipped. On: the check works as described on the Guards page.
SI_Guard_FlowStepSkipped_Enabled.whenToChange: Off by default: only the two brakes stay on (CIs retired by mistake, duplicate vulnerability records) -- this check is a warning you can switch on. Turn it on when you want it to hold or stop the step, and mail, again.

SI_Guard_FlowStepSkipped_Mail.label: Daily flow: jobs skipped: mail
SI_Guard_FlowStepSkipped_Mail.purpose: Whether this safety check sends a mail when it trips.
SI_Guard_FlowStepSkipped_Mail.defaultText: On (follows the check: nothing is mailed while the check is off)
SI_Guard_FlowStepSkipped_Mail.effect: Off: the event is still shown on the Guards page and kept in run health and the audit trail, but no mail is sent for it. The install-wide switch "Mail when a safety check stops a step" still applies to every check.
SI_Guard_FlowStepSkipped_Mail.whenToChange: Turn it off for a check whose mails you do not need, instead of turning the check off.

SI_Guard_FlowStepStartFailed_Enabled.label: Daily flow: job did not start
SI_Guard_FlowStepStartFailed_Enabled.purpose: The safety check that protects the jobs of the daily flow: A job in the daily flow could not start: its container stopped before SecurityInsight ran (an Azure platform problem).
SI_Guard_FlowStepStartFailed_Enabled.effect: Off: no event and no mail; a job that does not start is still not run. On: the check works as described on the Guards page.
SI_Guard_FlowStepStartFailed_Enabled.whenToChange: Off by default: only the two brakes stay on (CIs retired by mistake, duplicate vulnerability records) -- this check is a warning you can switch on. Turn it on when you want it to hold or stop the step, and mail, again.

SI_Guard_FlowStepStartFailed_Mail.label: Daily flow: job did not start: mail
SI_Guard_FlowStepStartFailed_Mail.purpose: Whether this safety check sends a mail when it trips.
SI_Guard_FlowStepStartFailed_Mail.defaultText: On (follows the check: nothing is mailed while the check is off)
SI_Guard_FlowStepStartFailed_Mail.effect: Off: the event is still shown on the Guards page and kept in run health and the audit trail, but no mail is sent for it. The install-wide switch "Mail when a safety check stops a step" still applies to every check.
SI_Guard_FlowStepStartFailed_Mail.whenToChange: Turn it off for a check whose mails you do not need, instead of turning the check off.

SI_Guard_FlowStepInterrupted_Enabled.label: Daily flow: job interrupted
SI_Guard_FlowStepInterrupted_Enabled.purpose: The safety check that protects the jobs that depend on an earlier job: A job in the daily flow was interrupted and was not started again automatically.
SI_Guard_FlowStepInterrupted_Enabled.effect: Off: no event and no mail; an interrupted job is still not started again. On: the check works as described on the Guards page.
SI_Guard_FlowStepInterrupted_Enabled.whenToChange: Off by default: only the two brakes stay on (CIs retired by mistake, duplicate vulnerability records) -- this check is a warning you can switch on. Turn it on when you want it to hold or stop the step, and mail, again.

SI_Guard_FlowStepInterrupted_Mail.label: Daily flow: job interrupted: mail
SI_Guard_FlowStepInterrupted_Mail.purpose: Whether this safety check sends a mail when it trips.
