SI_Guard_FlowStepInterrupted_Mail.effect: Off: the event is still shown on the Guards page and kept in run health and the audit trail, but no mail is sent for it. The install-wide switch "Mail when a safety check stops a step" still applies to every check.
SI_Guard_FlowStepInterrupted_Mail.whenToChange: Turn it off for a check whose mails you do not need, instead of turning the check off.

SI_Guard_JobExecutionPreviousRunning_Ena.label: Job started while still running
SI_Guard_JobExecutionPreviousRunning_Ena.purpose: The safety check that protects a job from running twice at the same time: A job was started while its previous run was still running, so the new run did nothing.
SI_Guard_JobExecutionPreviousRunning_Ena.effect: Off: no event and no mail. The step itself still stops, because two runs of one job never run at the same time. On: the check works as described on the Guards page.
SI_Guard_JobExecutionPreviousRunning_Ena.whenToChange: Off by default: only the two brakes stay on (CIs retired by mistake, duplicate vulnerability records) -- this check is a warning you can switch on. Turn it on when you want it to hold or stop the step, and mail, again.

SI_Guard_JobExecutionPreviousRunning_Mai.label: Job started while still running: mail
SI_Guard_JobExecutionPreviousRunning_Mai.purpose: Whether this safety check sends a mail when it trips.
SI_Guard_JobExecutionPreviousRunning_Mai.defaultText: On (follows the check: nothing is mailed while the check is off)
SI_Guard_JobExecutionPreviousRunning_Mai.effect: Off: the event is still shown on the Guards page and kept in run health and the audit trail, but no mail is sent for it. The install-wide switch "Mail when a safety check stops a step" still applies to every check.
SI_Guard_JobExecutionPreviousRunning_Mai.whenToChange: Turn it off for a check whose mails you do not need, instead of turning the check off.

SI_Guard_JobRunThrottledStuck_Enabled.label: Job stuck on throttling
SI_Guard_JobRunThrottledStuck_Enabled.purpose: The safety check that protects the data of a job that Microsoft keeps throttling: A job has not completed for a long time, because Microsoft throttled every run of it.
SI_Guard_JobRunThrottledStuck_Enabled.effect: Off: no event and no mail when a job is stuck on throttling. Throttled runs are still shown as throttled on the Jobs and Run health pages. On: the check works as described on the Guards page.
SI_Guard_JobRunThrottledStuck_Enabled.whenToChange: Off by default: only the two brakes stay on (CIs retired by mistake, duplicate vulnerability records) -- this check is a warning you can switch on. Turn it on when you want it to hold or stop the step, and mail, again.

SI_Guard_JobRunThrottledStuck_Mail.label: Job stuck on throttling: mail
SI_Guard_JobRunThrottledStuck_Mail.purpose: Whether this safety check sends a mail when it trips.
SI_Guard_JobRunThrottledStuck_Mail.defaultText: On (follows the check: nothing is mailed while the check is off)
SI_Guard_JobRunThrottledStuck_Mail.effect: Off: the event is still shown on the Guards page and kept in run health and the audit trail, but no mail is sent for it. The install-wide switch "Mail when a safety check stops a step" still applies to every check.
SI_Guard_JobRunThrottledStuck_Mail.whenToChange: Turn it off for a check whose mails you do not need, instead of turning the check off.

SI_Throttle_StuckHours.label: Stuck on throttling after (hours)
SI_Throttle_StuckHours.purpose: How long a job may keep being throttled by Microsoft, without completing, before the one "stuck" alert is sent.
SI_Throttle_StuckHours.effect: A throttled run is normal: it is shown as throttled, it is not mailed, and the job runs again at its next scheduled time. When a job has been throttled on every run for this many hours (and at least two runs), one alert says it is stuck. Whichever comes first of this and the number of runs below. The next run that completes clears it.
SI_Throttle_StuckHours.whenToChange: Raise it if you get the alert for jobs that catch up by themselves; lower it if you need to know sooner.

SI_Throttle_StuckRuns.label: Stuck on throttling after (runs)
SI_Throttle_StuckRuns.purpose: How many throttled runs in a row, without one that completes, send the one "stuck" alert.
SI_Throttle_StuckRuns.effect: When a job has been throttled this many runs in a row, one alert says it is stuck -- whichever comes first of this and the number of hours above. The next run that completes clears it.
SI_Throttle_StuckRuns.whenToChange: Raise it for jobs that run very often; lower it if you need to know sooner.

SI_Telemetry_Endpoint.label: Status report address
SI_Telemetry_Endpoint.purpose: The https address the status reports are sent to.
SI_Telemetry_Endpoint.effect: Reports go to this address instead. Only https addresses are used; anything else sends nothing.
SI_Telemetry_Endpoint.whenToChange: Practically never; only if Invardia tells you to use another address.

SI_TierCadence_Default.label: Re-check interval, unknown tier
SI_TierCadence_Default.purpose: How often an asset whose privilege tier is not yet known is re-processed when the per-asset skip schedule is in use.
SI_TierCadence_Default.effect: Shorter intervals refresh such assets more often at the cost of run time; longer ones skip them more. Only applies when the fingerprint cache is turned on and the run is not a full run.
SI_TierCadence_Default.whenToChange: Rarely; only when you run incremental profiling with the fingerprint cache on.

SI_TierCadence_T0.label: Re-check interval, tier 0
SI_TierCadence_T0.purpose: How often tier 0 assets (domain controllers, break-glass and global admins) are re-processed when the per-asset skip schedule is in use.
SI_TierCadence_T0.effect: A number is read as hours; text such as '3d' also works. Shorter keeps the most critical assets fresher but costs run time. Only applies with the fingerprint cache on and outside full runs.
SI_TierCadence_T0.whenToChange: Rarely; only when you run incremental profiling with the fingerprint cache on.

SI_TierCadence_T1.label: Re-check interval, tier 1
SI_TierCadence_T1.purpose: How often tier 1 assets (production servers, privileged users) are re-processed when the per-asset skip schedule is in use.
SI_TierCadence_T1.effect: A number is read as hours; text such as '3d' also works. Shorter means fresher data and longer runs. Only applies with the fingerprint cache on and outside full runs.
SI_TierCadence_T1.whenToChange: Rarely; only when you run incremental profiling with the fingerprint cache on.

SI_TierCadence_T2.label: Re-check interval, tier 2
SI_TierCadence_T2.purpose: How often tier 2 assets (workstations, regular users) are re-processed when the per-asset skip schedule is in use.
SI_TierCadence_T2.effect: A number is read as hours; text such as '3d' also works. Shorter means fresher data and longer runs. Only applies with the fingerprint cache on and outside full runs.
SI_TierCadence_T2.whenToChange: Rarely; only when you run incremental profiling with the fingerprint cache on.

SI_TierCadence_T3.label: Re-check interval, tier 3
SI_TierCadence_T3.purpose: How often tier 3 assets (test and development, externals, guests, unmanaged) are re-processed when the per-asset skip schedule is in use.
SI_TierCadence_T3.effect: A number is read as hours; text such as '7d' also works. Shorter means fresher data and longer runs. Only applies with the fingerprint cache on and outside full runs.
SI_TierCadence_T3.whenToChange: Rarely; only when you run incremental profiling with the fingerprint cache on.

SI_Trend_DcrName.label: Trend data collection rule name
SI_Trend_DcrName.purpose: The name of the data collection rule the trend engine publishes its daily rollup through.
SI_Trend_DcrName.defaultText: The engine's own rule name for the trend table.
SI_Trend_DcrName.effect: Sends the trend rollup through a differently named data collection rule. A wrong name means the rollup is published through a rule you did not intend, or fails to publish.
SI_Trend_DcrName.whenToChange: Only when the default rule name clashes with an existing one in your workspace.

SI_Trend_DryRun.label: Trend dry run
SI_Trend_DryRun.purpose: Lets the trend engine compute and print its rollup without publishing anything.
SI_Trend_DryRun.defaultText: Off: the rollup is published every run.
SI_Trend_DryRun.effect: When on, nothing is written to the trend table, so the trend line and weekly history get a gap for every dry-run day. A command-line switch on the run wins over this value.
SI_Trend_DryRun.whenToChange: For a first trial run, or while checking numbers; switch it back off afterwards.

SI_Trend_Grain.label: Trend source detail level
SI_Trend_Grain.purpose: Chooses whether the trend rollup is built from the Risk Analysis summary results or the detailed per-asset results.
SI_Trend_Grain.effect: 'Detailed' rolls up from the detailed Risk Analysis table instead, which only helps if your reports publish at that level. Any value other than Summary or Detailed falls back to Summary with a warning.
SI_Trend_Grain.whenToChange: Only if your Risk Analysis reports are published at the detailed level and you want the trend built from that.

SI_Trend_Weeks.label: Weekly rate weeks shown
SI_Trend_Weeks.purpose: How many weeks the printed weekly opened/closed view covers when the trend engine is run by hand with the weekly rate view.
SI_Trend_Weeks.effect: Only changes how many weeks are printed when a person asks for the weekly rate view on a VM run. The weekly history that is stored is unaffected, and scheduled container runs do not print the view.
SI_Trend_Weeks.whenToChange: Rarely; when you want a longer or shorter printed history during a manual run.

SI_UAMI_ClientId.label: Managed identity client id (older name)
SI_UAMI_ClientId.purpose: Client id of a user-assigned managed identity; the older name for SI_ManagedIdentityClientId, and the one container jobs and ingestion read.
SI_UAMI_ClientId.defaultText: Copied from SI_ManagedIdentityClientId; empty means system-assigned
SI_UAMI_ClientId.effect: Selects the user-assigned identity used for sign-in and ingestion. Several ingestion paths use managed identity only when this is set.
SI_UAMI_ClientId.whenToChange: Rarely; set SI_ManagedIdentityClientId instead, unless configuring a container job directly.

SI_Verbose.label: Verbose diagnostic logging
SI_Verbose.purpose: Adds detailed diagnostic lines (routing, timing, merge statistics, samples) to the run log.
SI_Verbose.effect: Run logs become much longer and more detailed, which helps support find problems. Collected data and reports are unchanged.
SI_Verbose.whenToChange: When investigating a problem or when support asks for it; turn off again afterwards.

SI_VulnSync_CloseAfterRuns.label: Runs before a vulnerability closes
SI_VulnSync_CloseAfterRuns.purpose: How many complete runs in a row a vulnerability must be missing from an asset that was seen before the close-loop marks it fixed.
SI_VulnSync_CloseAfterRuns.effect: Higher avoids closing and reopening vulnerabilities that devices report on and off, but confirms real fixes later. Runs where the asset was not seen do not count. Below 1 is raised to 1; non-numbers use 2.
SI_VulnSync_CloseAfterRuns.whenToChange: Raise it if vulnerabilities keep closing and reopening on the same devices.

SI_WorkspaceName.label: Log Analytics workspace name
SI_WorkspaceName.purpose: Name of the Log Analytics workspace SecurityInsight writes its data to and reads from.
SI_WorkspaceName.defaultText: log-platform-management-securityinsight when the resource id gives none
SI_WorkspaceName.effect: Used when creating a missing workspace and in run messages; Risk Analysis uses it when no workspace resource id is set. A wrong name can make setup create a new workspace.
SI_WorkspaceName.whenToChange: Set at install; the workspace resource id is the main setting.

SI_WorkspaceResourceGroup.label: Workspace resource group
SI_WorkspaceResourceGroup.purpose: Names the Azure resource group of the Log Analytics workspace the engines write to.
SI_WorkspaceResourceGroup.defaultText: Taken from the workspace resource id; otherwise 'rg-securityinsight'
SI_WorkspaceResourceGroup.effect: The workspace is looked up in this resource group (setup creates it there). A collection run creates nothing: a workspace it does not find is said in one line, and the send fails.
SI_WorkspaceResourceGroup.whenToChange: Set once during setup to match your workspace; change only if the workspace moves.

SI_WorkspaceResourceId.label: Log Analytics workspace
SI_WorkspaceResourceId.purpose: Full Azure resource id of the Log Analytics workspace all engines write to and query.
SI_WorkspaceResourceId.defaultText: Not set: correlation, CMDB and vulnerability engines stop; others fall back
SI_WorkspaceResourceId.effect: Decides where all SecurityInsight data lands and is read from; also gives the subscription for ingestion. Changing it starts a new data history in the new workspace.
SI_WorkspaceResourceId.whenToChange: Set at install; change only when moving to another workspace.

SMTP_UseSSL.label: Encrypted mail connection
SMTP_UseSSL.purpose: Whether report e-mails are sent to the mail server over an encrypted (SSL/TLS) connection.
SMTP_UseSSL.defaultText: Not set: Risk Analysis mail fails (run continues); the daily close-loop mail sends unencrypted
SMTP_UseSSL.effect: On: the connection is encrypted, as most cloud relays require. Off: plain connection, typical for an internal relay on port 25. A mismatch with the server makes sending fail.
SMTP_UseSSL.whenToChange: Set it to match your mail server; setup asks for it.

SMTPFrom.label: Mail sender address
SMTPFrom.purpose: The From address on every mail.
SMTPFrom.defaultText: Falls back to MailFrom, then SMTPUser; with signed-in mail the run stops at start
SMTPFrom.effect: Sets who the mail appears to come from. A sender the relay has not verified gets the mail rejected. With no sender at all and anonymous mail, mail is skipped with a warning.
SMTPFrom.whenToChange: Set it whenever mail is on; use an address your mail relay accepts as sender.
SMTPFrom.hint: Use an address your mail server accepts as sender.

SMTPPassword.label: Mail server password
SMTPPassword.purpose: Password (or app password) of the mail server account.
SMTPPassword.defaultText: Not set: signed-in mail cannot start; containers read it from your Key Vault
SMTPPassword.effect: Needed whenever mail is sent with sign-in. Without it, a Risk Analysis run with mail on stops at start and the daily close-loop mail is not sent.
SMTPPassword.whenToChange: Set it when you turn mail on with a relay that needs sign-in, and when the password changes.

SMTPPort.label: Mail server port
SMTPPort.purpose: The network port of the mail server used for report e-mails, for example 25, 465 or 587.
SMTPPort.defaultText: No fallback for Risk Analysis mail; the daily close-loop mail uses 587 with encryption, else 25
SMTPPort.effect: Must match the mail server and the encryption setting; a wrong port makes sending fail (the run itself continues).
SMTPPort.whenToChange: Set it to match your mail server; setup asks for it.
SMTPPort.hint: Usually 587 with an encrypted connection, 25 without.

SI_Mail_Mode.label: How mail is sent
SI_Mail_Mode.purpose: How SecurityInsight sends every mail: sharedMailbox = an Office 365 shared mailbox through Microsoft Graph as SecurityInsight's own identity (recommended); smtp = your own SMTP relay; none = no mail.
SI_Mail_Mode.defaultText: Not set: your SMTP relay when a mail server is set, else no mail
SI_Mail_Mode.effect: Every mail (reports, safety-check alerts, close-loop, exemption, governance and digest mails, licence notices) goes this way. With sharedMailbox SecurityInsight sends only once it has verified that Mail.Send is restricted to the shared mailbox.
SI_Mail_Mode.whenToChange: Set up with Settings > E-mail > Set up mail, or setup\Set-SIMail.ps1.
SI_Mail_Mode.hint: The shared mailbox is recommended: no password to keep, and Exchange lets SecurityInsight send only as that one mailbox.

SI_Mail_From.label: Shared mailbox (sender)
SI_Mail_From.purpose: The shared mailbox SecurityInsight sends as. With an SMTP relay it is the From address (and wins over the older sender settings).
SI_Mail_From.defaultText: Not set: with a shared mailbox nothing is sent; with SMTP the older sender setting is used
SI_Mail_From.effect: Mail comes from this address. With a shared mailbox, Exchange must allow SecurityInsight's identity to send as it (and only as it).
SI_Mail_From.whenToChange: Set when you set up mail, or when the mailbox changes.

SI_Mail_ProbeMailbox.label: Mailbox to prove the restriction
SI_Mail_ProbeMailbox.purpose: An ordinary mailbox OUTSIDE the shared mailbox's scope. Before it sends, SecurityInsight checks that it may NOT send as this mailbox -- which proves Mail.Send is restricted. Nothing is delivered by the check.
SI_Mail_ProbeMailbox.defaultText: Not set: the restriction counts as verified only when an Exchange administrator confirmed it
SI_Mail_ProbeMailbox.effect: Without it (and without a confirmation) SecurityInsight does not send through the shared mailbox.
SI_Mail_ProbeMailbox.whenToChange: Set once, to an administrator's own mailbox; setup fills it in.

SI_Mail_RestrictionAttestation.label: Restriction confirmed by
SI_Mail_RestrictionAttestation.purpose: Who confirmed that Mail.Send is restricted to the shared mailbox (Test-ServicePrincipalAuthorization), and when. Used only when no other mailbox can be tested.
SI_Mail_RestrictionAttestation.effect: Counts as verified when the check against another mailbox cannot run.
SI_Mail_RestrictionAttestation.whenToChange: Set by the mail setup, or after your Exchange administrator ran the check.

SI_Mail_SmtpKept.label: Keep the SMTP relay (by choice)
SI_Mail_SmtpKept.purpose: Says that your own SMTP relay is kept on purpose, so SecurityInsight stops suggesting the move to an Office 365 shared mailbox.
SI_Mail_SmtpKept.defaultText: Off: SecurityInsight recommends moving to an Office 365 shared mailbox, and Home and Settings > E-mail show that hint
SI_Mail_SmtpKept.effect: On: the SMTP relay is kept by choice -- the amber "move to an Office 365 shared mailbox" hint is hidden on Home and on Settings > E-mail, and mail shows as set up. A failed test mail is still shown in red. Mail is sent exactly as before.
SI_Mail_SmtpKept.whenToChange: When you decide to keep your own SMTP relay; Ignore on the Home banner sets it, Undo on Settings > E-mail clears it.

SmtpServer.label: Mail server
SmtpServer.purpose: Host name of the mail server (SMTP relay) every SecurityInsight mail is sent through.
SmtpServer.defaultText: Not set: no mail can be sent (reports are still written)
SmtpServer.effect: All Risk Analysis and close-loop mail goes through this server. Without it, sending fails with an error but the run completes.
SmtpServer.whenToChange: Set it when you turn report mail on.

SMTPUser.label: Mail server user name
SMTPUser.purpose: User name of the mail server account that sends the mails.
SMTPUser.defaultText: Not set: signed-in mail cannot start; some installs read it from your Key Vault
SMTPUser.effect: Needed with the password whenever mail is sent with sign-in. Without it, a Risk Analysis run with mail on stops at start, unless anonymous mail is on.
SMTPUser.whenToChange: Set it when you turn mail on with a relay that needs sign-in.

SpnCertificateThumbprint.label: Certificate thumbprint (launcher name)
SpnCertificateThumbprint.purpose: Thumbprint of the certificate in the local certificate store that the service principal signs in with; the recommended alternative to a client secret.
SpnCertificateThumbprint.defaultText: Copied from SI_SPN_CertThumbprint; empty means no certificate sign-in
SpnCertificateThumbprint.effect: When set with an app id, the launchers sign in with the certificate. A thumbprint that is not in the store makes sign-in fail.
SpnCertificateThumbprint.whenToChange: When you sign in with a certificate and do not use the SI_SPN_ names.

SpnClientId.label: App id (launcher name)
SpnClientId.purpose: Application (client) id of the service principal the launchers sign in as; older name kept in step with SI_SPN_AppId.
SpnClientId.effect: Used by the launchers for certificate, Key Vault and secret sign-in; without it those methods stop with an error.

SpnClientSecret.label: Client secret (launcher name)
SpnClientSecret.purpose: Plain client secret the launchers sign in with when no managed identity, Key Vault secret or certificate is configured.
SpnClientSecret.defaultText: Copied from SI_SPN_Secret; not set means no secret sign-in
SpnClientSecret.effect: Enables plain-secret sign-in, which the launcher warns is for testing only. Storing a secret in a file is a security risk.
SpnClientSecret.whenToChange: Only in labs; prefer managed identity, a certificate or a Key Vault secret.

SpnKeyVaultName.label: Key Vault name (older name)
SpnKeyVaultName.purpose: Name of the Azure Key Vault holding the service principal secret and other credentials; older name accepted alongside SI_KeyVaultName.
SpnKeyVaultName.defaultText: Not set: SI_KeyVaultName is used; no vault means no vault reads
SpnKeyVaultName.effect: With a secret name, the launchers read the client secret from this vault using the host's managed identity. SI_KeyVaultName wins when both are set.
SpnKeyVaultName.whenToChange: Rarely; set SI_KeyVaultName instead on new installs.

SpnSecretName.label: Key Vault secret name
SpnSecretName.purpose: Name of the Key Vault secret that holds the service principal's client secret.
SpnSecretName.defaultText: Not set: the secret is not read from Key Vault
SpnSecretName.effect: With a vault name and app id, the launchers fetch the client secret from Key Vault at each run, so no secret is stored on disk. A wrong name stops the run.
SpnSecretName.whenToChange: When the service principal secret is kept in Key Vault rather than using a certificate or managed identity.

SpnTenantId.label: Tenant id (launcher name)
SpnTenantId.purpose: The Entra tenant id the launchers sign in to; older name kept in step with SI_SPN_TenantId.
SpnTenantId.defaultText: Copied from SI_SPN_TenantId; with managed identity, read from the sign-in
SpnTenantId.effect: Required for service principal sign-in; without it and without managed identity the launcher stops with an error.

SubscriptionId.label: Azure subscription (older name)
SubscriptionId.purpose: Older name for the subscription Risk Analysis uses to find or create its workspace and ingestion resources.
SubscriptionId.defaultText: Derived from the workspace resource id, else the signed-in subscription
SubscriptionId.effect: Risk Analysis uses it first when resolving the workspace; other engines use it only when SI_AzSubscriptionId and the workspace resource id give none. A wrong value points at the wrong subscription.
SubscriptionId.whenToChange: Rarely; prefer setting the full workspace resource id.

Summary.label: Run Summary report
Summary.purpose: Run-mode switch telling Risk Analysis to build the Summary report and use the Summary mail settings and table.
Summary.defaultText: Off; with neither Summary nor Detailed set, the Summary report is still built by default.
Summary.effect: Selects the Summary report template, its mail recipients and its Log Analytics table. Setting it together with Detailed stops the run with an error.
Summary.whenToChange: Normally set by the launcher or container job, not in the configuration file.

UseManagedIdentity.label: Managed identity on (launcher name)
UseManagedIdentity.purpose: Tells the launchers to sign in with the host's managed identity; set automatically by the sign-in method choice.
UseManagedIdentity.defaultText: On when no service principal is configured; otherwise off
UseManagedIdentity.effect: When on, launchers sign in as the Azure VM's or Arc server's identity (or a user-assigned one), and that identity needs the permissions.

WhatIfMode.label: Dry run
WhatIfMode.purpose: Requests a run that shows what would change without changing anything.
WhatIfMode.effect: In the configuration it is read only by asset tagging, which then only reports the tags it would apply or remove. Every other engine ignores it in the configuration (scheduled runs always publish, and each run says the value was ignored): a dry run of profiling, Risk Analysis or the tier classifier is asked for per run -- start the launcher with -WhatIfMode, or set SI_WHATIF=1 on one container job execution. Such a run says so at its start and its end. Profiling and Risk Analysis then write their results to local files only -- nothing goes to Log Analytics, the mail, the export location or the caches; the run-health record says dry run. The tier classifier writes its result beside the catalog, never over it.
WhatIfMode.whenToChange: In the configuration: only before the first real asset-tagging run. To preview any other engine, use -WhatIfMode on that one run.

WorkspaceName.label: Workspace name (older name)
WorkspaceName.purpose: Older name for the Log Analytics workspace name, read by Risk Analysis and setup checks.
WorkspaceName.effect: Used by Risk Analysis only when no workspace resource id and no SI_WorkspaceName is set; it may then find or create a workspace with this name.
WorkspaceName.whenToChange: Never on new installs; set SI_WorkspaceResourceId instead.

WorkspaceResourceGroup.label: Workspace resource group (older name)
WorkspaceResourceGroup.purpose: Resource group of the Log Analytics workspace, used by Risk Analysis when it must find or create the workspace.
WorkspaceResourceGroup.effect: Used when SI_RiskAnalysis_WorkspaceResourceGroup is not set; its region also decides where missing resources are created. A wrong group can create a new workspace.
WorkspaceResourceGroup.whenToChange: Rarely; prefer setting the full workspace resource id.

WorkspaceResourceId.label: Workspace resource id (older name)
WorkspaceResourceId.purpose: Older name for the full workspace resource id, read by Risk Analysis when the newer setting is not set.
WorkspaceResourceId.effect: Used only when SI_RiskAnalysis_WorkspaceResourceId and SI_WorkspaceResourceId are not set. A wrong value sends Risk Analysis data and queries to another workspace.
WorkspaceResourceId.whenToChange: Never on new installs; set SI_WorkspaceResourceId instead.

WriteJsonOutput.label: Risk report JSON copy
WriteJsonOutput.purpose: Also writes the Risk Analysis report as a JSON file next to the Excel file, for tools that read machine-readable data.
WriteJsonOutput.effect: On: an extra JSON file is written and uploaded with the Excel file; slightly more disk space and run time.
WriteJsonOutput.whenToChange: Turn on when another tool or pipeline needs the report as JSON.
